short_description.id: Siluman Kalajengking adalah antagonis dalam novel klasik Journey to the West.
short_description.en: The Scorpion Demoness is an antagonist in the classic novel Journey to the West.

long_description.id: Siluman Kalajengking adalah antagonis dalam novel klasik Journey to the West. Wujud asli tokoh ini adalah kalajengking raksasa sebesar pipa.
long_description.en: The Scorpion Demoness is an antagonist in the classic novel Journey to the West. The character's true form is a giant scorpion the size of a pipa.

long_description.id: Sengatan ekornya mampu melukai Buddha dan Sun Wukong dalam cerita. Ia menghuni Pipa Cave di Venom Mountain, dekat Women's Kingdom. Ia menculik Tang Sanzang dan berusaha membujuknya menikah. Maori Xingguan menundukkannya dengan berubah menjadi ayam jantan raksasa berjengger dua.
long_description.en: Her tail sting can injure both the Buddha and Sun Wukong in the story. She lives in Pipa Cave on Venom Mountain near the Women's Kingdom. She abducts Tang Sanzang and tries to persuade him to marry her. Maori Xingguan defeats her by becoming a giant rooster with two combs.

long_description.id: Teks novel sendiri menjelaskan wujudnya melalui ucapan sang Bodhisattva: garpu bermata tiga milik siluman itu adalah sepasang capit, dan tusukan yang menyakitkan datang dari kait ekor bernama daoma du. Di novel itu juga diceritakan bahwa ia pernah menusuk ibu jari Rulai di Kuil 雷音寺. Sun Wukong menyebut tempat gurunya tertawan di Gua 琵琶洞. Dalam episode yang sama, sang penguasa bintang tampil sebagai ayam jantan berjengger ganda; kokokannya membuat siluman itu menampakkan wujud kalajengking sebesar pipa dan akhirnya mati.
long_description.en: The novel itself explains her form through the Bodhisattva's words: the demoness's three-pronged fork is a pair of pincers, and the painful sting comes from a tail hook called daoma du. It also tells that she once stung Rulai's thumb at the Temple 雷音寺. Sun Wukong names the cave 琵琶洞 as where his master is held. In the same episode the star official appears as a double-crested rooster whose crowing makes the demoness show her true form as a pipa-sized scorpion and finally die.

description.id: Dalam novel, tusukan kait di ekornya disebut daoma du dan terasa sangat menyakitkan, bahkan bagi Rulai.
description.en: In the novel, the sting of the hook on her tail is called daoma du and is excruciating, even to Rulai.

statement.id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva menjelaskan bahwa garpu bermata tiga milik siluman itu sebenarnya sepasang capit, bahwa tusukan yang menyakitkan berasal dari kait di ujung ekor yang disebut "daoma du", dan bahwa wujud aslinya adalah siluman kalajengking.
statement.en: In the novel, the Bodhisattva explains that the demoness's three-pronged fork is really a pair of pincers, that the painful sting comes from a hook on her tail called "daoma du" (horse-felling venom), and that her true body is a scorpion spirit.

claims.quote: 他前者在雷音寺聽佛談經，如來見了，不合用手推他一把，他就轉過鉤子，把如來左手中拇指上扎了一下。如來也疼難禁，即著金剛拿他。

statement.id: Menurut sang Bodhisattva dalam novel, siluman itu pernah mendengarkan Buddha berbicara tentang sutra di Kuil 雷音寺 (Leiyin); ketika Rulai (如來) mendorongnya, ia memutar kaitnya dan menusuk ibu jari tengah tangan kiri Rulai hingga sakit tak tertahankan.
statement.en: According to the Bodhisattva in the novel, the demoness once listened to the Buddha discuss the sutras at the Temple 雷音寺 (Leiyin); when Rulai (如來) pushed her, she turned her hook and stung the middle thumb of Rulai's left hand, causing him unbearable pain.

claims.quote: 那星官斂雲霧整束朝衣，停執事分開左右，上前作禮道：「大聖何來？」行者道：「專來拜煩救師父一難。」星官道：「何難？在何地方？」行者道：「在西梁國毒敵山琵琶洞。」

statement.id: Sun Wukong (行者) memberi tahu sang penguasa bintang bahwa gurunya sedang dalam kesulitan di Gua 琵琶洞 di Gunung 毒敵山 di negeri 西梁國.
statement.en: Sun Wukong (行者) tells the star official that his master is in trouble in the cave 琵琶洞 on the mountain 毒敵山 in the country 西梁國.

claims.quote: 原來是一隻雙冠子大公雞，昂起頭來，約有六七尺高，對著妖怪叫了一聲。那怪即時就現了本相，原來是個琵琶來大小的一個蝎子精。這星官再叫一聲，那怪渾身酥軟，死在坡前。

statement.id: Di novel itu, sang penguasa bintang tampil sebagai ayam jantan besar berjengger ganda setinggi sekitar enam atau tujuh chi (尺); ketika ia berkokok, siluman itu menampakkan wujud aslinya, kalajengking sebesar pipa, lalu lemas dan mati setelah kokokan kedua.
statement.en: In the novel the star official appears as a great double-crested rooster about six or seven chi (尺) tall; when it crows, the demoness reveals her true form, a scorpion as big as a pipa, and after a second crow her body goes limp and she dies.

short_description.id: Sea Swine atau Porcus Marinus adalah sebutan untuk makhluk laut mitologis yang tercatat sejak Yunani kuno dan digambarkan pada peta Carta marina sebagai babi monster berkaki naga.
short_description.en: The Sea Swine or Porcus Marinus was a name for mythological sea creatures recorded from ancient Greece and shown on the Carta marina as a monstrous hog with dragon-like feet.

long_description.id: Nama Sea Swine atau Porcus Marinus telah disematkan pada beragam makhluk laut dan monster mitologis sepanjang sejarah, dengan rujukan tertua yang dapat ditelusuri ke masa Yunani kuno. Dalam peta terkenal Carta marina serta ukiran kayunya, makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai monster berkaki empat mirip naga dengan satu mata di bagian pusar yang dipercaya menghuni perairan selatan Iceland.
long_description.en: The name Sea Swine or Porcus Marinus was applied to various marine and mythological creatures throughout history, traceable back to ancient Greece. In the Carta marina and accompanying wood carvings, it was rendered as a fantastical beast with four dragon's feet and an eye at its navel living south of Iceland.

long_description.id: Catatan lain menggambarkan hewan-hewan ini "berkepala seperti babi, bertaring dan bergading seperti babi hutan", dilaporkan bepergian dalam kawanan beratus-ratus ekor. Naturalis John Ray menegaskan bahwa babi laut dan lumba-lumba pelabuhan (porpoise) adalah hal yang sama.
long_description.en: Other accounts described the animals as "headed like a Hog, toothed, and tusked like a Boar", reported travelling in packs of hundreds. The naturalist John Ray stated explicitly that the sea swine and the porpoise were one and the same.

long_description.id: Orkney Museums mengutip uraian Olaus tentang 'monsterous Hog' dengan kepala babi, kaki seperti naga, mata ketiga di perut, dan ekor bercabang, dan menyebut makhluk itu didasarkan pada pamflet anonim yang terbit di Roma pada 1537. Sebuah pameran perpustakaan universitas menambahkan bahwa tafsir yang dicetak di Roma menganggap bagian-bagian tubuhnya sebagai lambang kaum bidah yang hidup seperti babi, dan bahwa Olaus Magnus mengaitkannya dengan nafsu dan keserakahan. Menurut tafsir itu, keempat kaki naganya melambangkan keinginan dan perbuatan manusia yang sangat jahat, dan pameran itu menegaskan bahwa makhluk ini disalin dari pamflet Roma tahun 1537, bukan khayalan pribadi Magnus.
long_description.en: Orkney Museums quotes Olaus's description of a 'monsterous Hog' with a hog's head, dragon-like feet, a third eye in the belly and a forked tail, and says it was based on an anonymous pamphlet published in Rome in 1537. A university library exhibition adds that the interpretation printed in Rome read its parts as symbols of heretics living like swine, and that Olaus Magnus tied it to lust and greed. In that interpretation the four dragon-like feet signify the grossly evil desires and acts of mankind, and the exhibition stresses that the creature was copied from a Rome pamphlet of 1537 rather than being Magnus's own invention.

cultural_context.id: Menurut sebuah pameran perpustakaan universitas, babi laut pada peta itu ditafsirkan sebagai lambang kaum bidah yang hidup seperti babi, dan sebagai lambang dosa nafsu dan keserakahan bagi Olaus Magnus.
cultural_context.en: According to a university library exhibition, the sea-pig on the map was interpreted as a symbol of heretics living like swine, and as a symbol of the sins of lust and greed for Olaus Magnus.

title.en: The sea-pig on the Carta marina

role.id: Makhluk monster yang digambarkan di peta

summary.id: Sebuah uraian yang dikutip menggambarkan babi monster berkepala babi, berkaki empat seperti naga, bermata ketiga di perut, dan berekor bercabang; ia didasarkan pada laporan dalam pamflet Roma tahun 1537 dan ditafsirkan sebagai lambang kaum bidah yang hidup seperti babi.
summary.en: A quoted description portrays a monstrous hog with a hog's head, four dragon-like feet, a third eye in the belly and a forked tail; it was based on reports in a Rome pamphlet of 1537 and interpreted as a symbol of heretics living like swine.

description.id: Pamflet anonim yang terbit di Roma memuat laporan tentang hewan aneh yang menjadi dasar babi laut pada peta Olaus.
description.en: An anonymous pamphlet published in Rome carried accounts of a strange animal that became the basis of the sea swine on Olaus's map.

learning_questions.en: Why did Renaissance cartographers portray pig-like sea beasts with dragon feet on sea charts like the Carta marina?

summary.en: In this Dumaguete legend a crow-bodied Sigbin lives on Dalugdug and eats anyone who comes near its home. At the end it is said the Sigbin never returned to Negros, still lives in the mountains of Cebu, and people fear it so much that they lock themselves indoors after dark.

short_description.id: Sigbin adalah makhluk mitologi Filipina yang keluar malam hari untuk mengisap darah korban melalui bayangannya; dalam banyak kisah ia mirip kambing tanpa tanduk, bertelinga sangat besar, dan dapat menjadi tak terlihat.
short_description.en: The sigbin is a creature of Philippine mythology that comes out at night to suck victims' blood through their shadows; in many accounts it resembles a hornless goat with very large ears and can become invisible.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, sigbin keluar malam hari untuk mengisap darah korban melalui bayangan mereka. Ia dikatakan berjalan mundur dengan kepala tertunduk di antara kaki belakangnya, dan dapat menjadi tak terlihat, terutama oleh manusia. Wujudnya mirip kambing tanpa tanduk, tetapi bertelinga sangat besar yang dapat ditepukkan seperti tangan dan berekor panjang lentur yang dapat dipakai sebagai cambuk; ia juga mengeluarkan bau memuakkan.
long_description.en: In Philippine mythology, the sigbin comes out at night to drink victims' blood by way of their shadows. It moves backwards, head held low between its hind legs, and can turn invisible, above all to humans. It looks like a hornless goat but has very large ears it can clap like hands and a long flexible tail usable as a whip; it also gives off a nauseating smell.

long_description.id: Sigbin dipercaya keluar dari sarangnya pada Pekan Suci untuk mencari anak-anak yang akan dibunuh demi jantungnya, yang dijadikan jimat. Menurut legenda, ada keluarga yang disebut Sigbinan yang dapat memerintah makhluk ini dan menyimpannya dalam guci tanah liat, dan aswang konon memeliharanya sebagai hewan peliharaan. Mitos ini dikenal luas di Visayas dan Mindanao, terutama di pedesaan.
long_description.en: The sigbin is believed to emerge from its lair during Holy Week to look for children to kill for their hearts, which it makes into amulets. By legend, families called Sigbinan can command these creatures and keep them in clay jars, and aswangs are said to keep them as pets. The myth is widely known in the Visayas and Mindanao, especially in rural areas.

long_description.id: Gambaran sigbin berbeda-beda menurut sumber. Dalam sebuah legenda Dumaguete di Negros Occidental, Sigbin penghuni Dalugdug bertubuh seperti gagak raksasa dengan dua kaki panjang mirip belalang, memangsa siapa pun yang mendekati rumahnya, dan pada akhir kisah dikatakan masih hidup di pegunungan Cebu. Sebuah buku tahun 1978 menggambarkannya sebagai hewan malam mirip anjing berkaki depan menyempit seperti kanguru, dan sebuah kamus mitologi tahun 1895 mendefinisikannya sebagai roh pendamping yang terikat kontrak melayani seseorang.
long_description.en: Portrayals of the sigbin differ by source. In a Dumaguete legend from Negros Occidental, the Sigbin of Dalugdug has a body like a monstrous crow with two long grasshopper-like legs, eats anyone who comes near its home, and at the end is said still to live in the mountains of Cebu. A 1978 book describes it as a nocturnal dog-like animal with forelegs constricted like a kangaroo's, and a mythological dictionary of 1895 defines it as a spirit familiar bound by contract to serve a person.

long_description.id: Sigbin disebut dalam berbagai kepercayaan daerah Visayas: dalam kumpulan cerita Boholano, di antara lupan-on dalam kosmogoni Kinaray-a yang direkam di Mariit, dan sebagai makhluk daerah di komunitas penutur Hiligaynon. Dalam sebuah kisah rakyat, Sigbin dari Negros dan Bohol hadir di antara makhluk-makhluk yang berkumpul dari berbagai pulau. Sigbinan juga dicatat sebagai penyihir yang dapat berubah menjadi buaya, ular, atau anjing, dan sebagai salah satu dari lima roh yang dikenal sebagai asuang.
long_description.en: The sigbin is named in several Visayan regional beliefs: in Boholano collections, among the lupan-on of a Kinaray-a cosmogony recorded in Mariit, and as a regional being in Hiligaynon-speaking communities. In one folktale, Sigbins from Negros and Bohol are among the creatures gathered from many islands. The sigbinan is also recorded as a sorcerer able to turn into alligators, serpents or dogs, and as one of the five spirits known as asuang.

long_description.id: Ada dugaan bahwa legenda ini berasal dari penampakan hewan langka, bahkan kerabat kanguru, tetapi dugaan itu dibantah karena Garis Wallace memisahkan fauna Australia dari Filipina.
long_description.en: Some speculate the legend comes from sightings of a rare animal, even a relative of the kangaroo, but this is disputed because the Wallace Line separates the species of Australia and New Guinea from those of the Philippines.

claims.quote: Catalina of Dumaguete This is a legend of Dumaguete, the capital of the province of Negros Occidental. ... On Dalugdug there lived a terrible Sigbin. Its body was like that of a monstrous crow, but just under its neck were two long legs like those of a grasshopper, which enabled it to leap great distances without using its wings.

statement.id: Dalam legenda Dumaguete di Negros Occidental, Sigbin penghuni Dalugdug digambarkan bertubuh seperti burung gagak raksasa dengan dua kaki panjang mirip belalang di bawah lehernya yang membuatnya dapat melompat jauh tanpa memakai sayap.
statement.en: In a legend of Dumaguete in Negros Occidental, the Sigbin living on Dalugdug is described as having a body like a monstrous crow, with two long grasshopper-like legs under its neck that let it leap great distances without using its wings.

claims.quote: On Dalugdug there lived a terrible Sigbin. ... It ate any one who came near its home, so when the people saw Catalina start to climb the mountain they begged her to come back.

statement.id: Dalam legenda itu Sigbin di Dalugdug memangsa siapa pun yang mendekati rumahnya, sehingga orang-orang memohon agar Catalina yang mulai mendaki gunung itu kembali.
statement.en: In that legend the Sigbin on Dalugdug ate anyone who came near its home, so the people begged Catalina, who began to climb the mountain, to come back.

claims.quote: The Sigbin has never returned to Negros. It still lives in the mountains of Cebu and the people are so afraid of it that they lock themselves in their houses after dark and can hardly be induced to come out.

statement.id: Menurut penutup legenda itu, Sigbin tidak pernah kembali ke Negros; ia masih hidup di pegunungan Cebu dan orang begitu takut padanya sehingga mengunci diri di rumah setelah gelap dan nyaris tak mau keluar.
statement.en: According to the legend's close, the Sigbin never returned to Negros; it still lives in the mountains of Cebu and people fear it so much that they lock themselves in their houses after dark and can hardly be induced to come out.

claims.quote: The Faithlessness of Sinogo Somewhere off the northern coast of Mindanao a strong current begins to travel northward. ... There were huge Buayas from Mindanao, fierce Tic-bolans from Luzon, savage Sigbins from Negros and Bohol, hundreds of Unglocs from Panay and Leyte, and great Uak Uaks and other frightful monsters from Samar and Cebu.

statement.id: Dalam kisah "The Faithlessness of Sinogo", makhluk-makhluk dari berbagai pulau berkumpul, antara lain Sigbin buas dari Negros dan Bohol, bersama Buayas dari Mindanao, Tic-bolan dari Luzon, Unglocs dari Panay dan Leyte, serta Uak Uaks dari Samar dan Cebu.
statement.en: In the tale "The Faithlessness of Sinogo", creatures from various islands gather, among them savage Sigbins from Negros and Bohol, together with Buayas from Mindanao, Tic-bolans from Luzon, Unglocs from Panay and Leyte, and Uak Uaks from Samar and Cebu.

claims.quote: SIGBIN – (Visayan) A designation used by the Visayan people to refer to a certain type of spirit familiar that supposedly accompanied a person, to whom the spirit was bound by contract to serve constantly. (compare: Sigbinan.) (source: DICCIONARIO MITOLÓGICO DE FILIPINAS, Ferdinand Blumentritt [1895], translated and republished by The Aswang Project, 2021)

statement.id: Kamus mitologi tahun 1895 yang diterjemahkan ulang Aswang Project mendefinisikan sigbin di kalangan Visayas sebagai roh pendamping yang menyertai seseorang dan terikat kontrak untuk melayaninya terus-menerus.
statement.en: A mythological dictionary of 1895, re-published in translation by the Aswang Project, defines the sigbin among the Visayans as a spirit familiar that accompanied a person and was bound by contract to serve constantly.

claims.quote: SIGBIN – (Negros Occidental) The sigbin is another nocturnal animal resembling a dog whose forelegs are constricted in the manner of the kangaroo. (Source: Witchcraft, Filipino Style, Nid Anima, Omar Publishing, 1978)

statement.id: Sebuah buku tahun 1978 yang dikutip Aswang Project menggambarkan sigbin di Negros Occidental sebagai hewan malam mirip anjing yang kaki depannya menyempit seperti kanguru.
statement.en: A 1978 book cited by the Aswang Project describes the sigbin in Negros Occidental as a nocturnal animal resembling a dog whose forelegs are constricted like a kangaroo's.

claims.quote: SIGBINAN – (Visayan) The early Visayan people believed the there was a certain type of sorcerer that was called a sigbinan who could transform into alligators,serpents, or dogs who would bite or slay many men. (source: DICCIONARIO MITOLÓGICO DE FILIPINAS, Ferdinand Blumentritt [1895], translated and republished by The Aswang Project, 2021)

statement.id: Menurut kamus mitologi tahun 1895 yang sama, orang Visayas awal percaya ada jenis penyihir bernama sigbinan yang dapat berubah menjadi buaya, ular, atau anjing yang menggigit atau membunuh banyak orang.
statement.en: According to the same 1895 dictionary, the early Visayans believed in a kind of sorcerer called a sigbinan who could transform into alligators, serpents or dogs that would bite or slay many men.

claims.quote: There are many spirits who are known as asuang but the five most powerful are here given according to their rank, (a) Tagbanua, (b) Tagamaling, (c) Sigbinan, (d) Lumaman, (e) Bigwa.

statement.id: Sebuah catatan yang dikutip Aswang Project menyebut Sigbinan sebagai salah satu dari lima roh paling kuat yang dikenal sebagai asuang, bersama Tagbanua, Tagamaling, Lumaman, dan Bigwa.
statement.en: An account cited by the Aswang Project lists Sigbinan among the five most powerful spirits known as asuang, together with Tagbanua, Tagamaling, Lumaman and Bigwa.

claims.quote: Boholano collections describe engkanto, duende, spirits associated with trees and caves, wandering dead, uncanny lights, sigbin, aswang, and other dangerous night beings.

statement.id: Menurut Aswang Project, kumpulan cerita Boholano menggambarkan engkanto, duende, roh pohon dan gua, arwah gentayangan, cahaya aneh, sigbin, aswang, dan makhluk malam berbahaya lainnya.
statement.en: According to the Aswang Project, Boholano collections describe engkanto, duende, tree and cave spirits, wandering dead, uncanny lights, the sigbin, aswang and other dangerous night beings.

claims.quote: This is a documented Kinaray-a cosmogony, but specifically one recorded in Mariit. ... Numerous lupan-on occupy the land, including named forms such as tamawo, kama-kama, murokpok, mantiw, sigbin, and mulang.

statement.id: Aswang Project mencatat kosmogoni Kinaray-a yang direkam di Mariit, di mana banyak lupan-on menempati daratan, dengan bentuk bernama seperti tamawo, kama-kama, murokpok, mantiw, sigbin, dan mulang.
statement.en: The Aswang Project records a Kinaray-a cosmogony recorded in Mariit in which numerous lupan-on occupy the land, including named forms such as tamawo, kama-kama, murokpok, mantiw, sigbin and mulang.

claims.quote: Hiligaynon-speaking communities live across Iloilo, Negros Occidental, Guimaras, and neighboring areas. ... Other regional beings include the sigbin, kapre, aswang, and water-dwellers.

statement.id: Aswang Project menyebut komunitas penutur Hiligaynon tersebar di Iloilo, Negros Occidental, Guimaras, dan sekitarnya, dan menyebut sigbin, kapre, aswang, dan penghuni air sebagai makhluk daerah lain.
statement.en: The Aswang Project says Hiligaynon-speaking communities live across Iloilo, Negros Occidental, Guimaras and neighbouring areas, and lists the sigbin, kapre, aswang and water-dwellers as other regional beings.

claims.quote: the dominant endemic cultural heritage featured in Bol-anon narratives using Folklore Theory and Post-Colonial Theory. ... It also illustrates that folk beliefs weave a vibrant cultural tapestry featuring mythical creatures such as santilmo, ungu, wuwog, tambaloslos, engkanto, wakwak, and sigbin.

statement.id: Abstrak jurnal tentang narasi Bol-anon menyatakan kepercayaan rakyat merajut permadani budaya yang menampilkan makhluk mitos seperti santilmo, ungu, wuwog, tambaloslos, engkanto, wakwak, dan sigbin.
statement.en: A journal abstract on Bol-anon narratives states that folk beliefs weave a vibrant cultural tapestry featuring mythical creatures such as santilmo, ungu, wuwog, tambaloslos, engkanto, wakwak and sigbin.

short_description.id: Takaonna ("perempuan tinggi") adalah yōkai yang muncul dalam buku bergambar Toriyama Sekien, digambarkan memanjangkan tubuh untuk mengintip rumah bordil.
short_description.en: Takaonna ("tall woman") is a Japanese yōkai who appeared in Toriyama Sekien's illustrated book and is described as elongating her body to peek into brothels.

long_description.id: Takaonna adalah yōkai dalam buku bergambar karya Toriyama Sekien. Gambarnya menunjukkan perempuan dengan tubuh bagian bawah yang memanjang di dekat bangunan yang tampak seperti rumah bordil. Buku itu tidak memuat teks penjelasan, sehingga tidak jelas yōkai macam apa yang dimaksud.
long_description.en: Takaonna is a yōkai in Toriyama Sekien's illustrated book. The picture shows a woman with an elongated lower body beside what appears to be a brothel. No caption accompanies the image, so what Sekien meant it to be remains uncertain.

long_description.id: Satu tafsir menganggapnya ciptaan asli yang memparodikan Yoshiwara di zaman Edo. Ahli cerita rakyat Morihiko Fujisawa menjelaskan bahwa dalam cerita dari Prefektur Wakayama, Takaonna menakuti orang di lantai dua rumah bordil, sedangkan kaidan karya Norio Yamada menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan sederhana yang tak pernah bisa bersama pria semasa hidup. Kenji Murakami menilai penjelasan Fujisawa hanyalah satu tafsir dan kaidan Yamada kisah yang berbeda.
long_description.en: One interpretation takes it as an original invention parodying the Yoshiwara of the Edo period. The folklorist Morihiko Fujisawa explains that in a story from Wakayama Prefecture a Takaonna frightens people on the second floors of brothels, while a kaidan by Norio Yamada depicts her as a homely woman who could never be with a man in life. Kenji Murakami judges Fujisawa's account to be only one interpretation and Yamada's kaidan a different tale.

long_description.id: Menurut Yokai.com, taka onna sebagian besar waktu tampak seperti perempuan biasa tetapi dapat memanjangkan tubuh hingga beberapa meter. Mereka sering terlihat mengintip jendela lantai dua dan jarang menyerang secara fisik, meski senang menakut-nakuti. Yokai.com juga menyebut penampakannya memuncak pada zaman Edo.
long_description.en: According to Yokai.com, taka onna look like ordinary women most of the time but can elongate their bodies to several meters. They are often seen peering into second-story windows and rarely attack physically, though they enjoy scaring people. Yokai.com also says sightings peaked in the Edo period.

description.en: According to Yokai.com, taka onna can elongate their bodies to several meters in height; in Yamada's kaidan she elongates her body to peek into the second floor of brothels.

display_name.en: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain

short_description.id: Nyonya Gunung Tembaga adalah makhluk legendaris para penambang Ural, penguasa Pegunungan Ural, pelindung penambang dan pemilik kekayaan bawah tanah yang tersembunyi.
short_description.en: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain is a legendary being of the Ural miners, mistress of the Ural Mountains, patroness of miners and owner of hidden underground riches.

long_description.id: Nyonya Gunung Tembaga, juga disebut Gadis Malakit (Malakhitnitsa), adalah makhluk legendaris para penambang Ural, penguasa Pegunungan Ural di Rusia dan tokoh mitologi Slavia serta dongeng Rusia. Dalam cerita ia tampil sebagai perempuan muda sangat cantik bermata hijau bergaun malakit, atau sebagai kadal. Ia dianggap pelindung penambang dan pemilik kekayaan bawah tanah yang dapat mengizinkan atau mencegah penambangan di tempat tertentu.
long_description.en: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain, also the Malachite Maid (Malakhitnitsa), is a legendary being of the Ural miners, ruler of Russia's Ural Mountains and a figure of Slavic myth and Russian tales. Tales show her either as a lizard or as a lovely young woman with green eyes, dressed in malachite. Miners saw her as their patroness and as owner of hidden underground wealth who could allow or forbid mining in particular places.

long_description.id: "Gunung Tembaga" adalah tambang Gumyoshevsky, tambang tertua di Ural, kini di kota Polevskoy. Ia menjadi terkenal lewat kumpulan kisah Ural karya Pavel Bazhov, Kotak Malakit. Ia memerintah kadal-kadal gunung dan dapat menjelma kadal atau ular. Orang yang melihatnya jatuh di bawah pengaruhnya; ia baik kepada orang baik dan pengrajin terampil, membantu mereka menemukan permata dan emas, tetapi bila syaratnya dilanggar orang itu kehilangan keberuntungan dan keterampilan, bahkan bisa mati.
long_description.en: "The Copper Mountain" is the Gumyoshevsky mine, the oldest in the Urals, now in the town of Polevskoy. She became famous through Pavel Bazhov's collection of Ural tales, The Malachite Box. She commands the mountain lizards and can take the form of a lizard or a snake. Whoever sees her falls under her spell; she is kind to good people and skilled craftsmen, helping them find gems and gold, but if her conditions are broken the person loses all luck and skill and may even die.

long_description.id: Sebagai tokoh sastra, ia muncul dalam skaz ketiga Pavel Bazhov dari The Malachite Box, "The Mistress of the Copper Mountain", yang pertama kali terbit pada 1936. Dalam teks itu sang tokoh berpakaian malakit dan dikelilingi kadal yang tak terhitung banyaknya, dan ia memperingatkan pemuda itu bahwa menginjak pelayannya akan membawa celaka; ia juga dapat berlari seperti kadal dengan kepala manusia. Ia mencari orang yang tidak takut pada siapa pun, mengancam akan menenggelamkan tembaga di Gumeshki, dan memuji pemuda yang tidak tergiur kekayaannya; tambang itu kemudian menyusut dan terendam, dan orang berkata sang Nyonya marah karena tiang-tiang dipasang di gereja.
long_description.en: As a literary figure she features in Pavel Bazhov's The Malachite Box, in the third skaz, which came out in 1936. In that text she wears malachite and is surrounded by countless lizards, and she warns the young man that crushing her servant will bring trouble; she can also run like a lizard with a human head. She looks for someone who fears nobody, threatens to sink the copper in Gumeshki, and praises a young man who is not tempted by her riches; the mine later declines and floods, and people say the Mistress was angry because pillars were put up in a church.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan yang dicatat, perempuan tidak turun ke tambang karena itu wilayah sang Nyonya, dan anak-anak diajari agar tidak berteriak di dekat batu karena ia tidak menyukai suara keras. Ia juga dapat disebut Nyonya Gunung atau Ibu Gunung; dalam banyak dongeng ia dianggap sama dengan Azovka. Ada hipotesis bahwa ia mewakili Venus, karena tembaga setempat dicap dengan lambang Venus.
long_description.en: According to the recorded beliefs, women did not go down into the mine because it was her domain, and children were taught not to shout near the stones because she disliked loud noises. She may also be called the Mistress of the Mountain or the Mountain Mother; in many folktales she is identical with Azovka. One hypothesis holds that she represents Venus, because local copper was branded with the Venus symbol.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, orang yang melihatnya jatuh di bawah pengaruhnya; ia baik kepada orang baik dan pengrajin terampil, membantu mereka menemukan permata dan emas, tetapi bila syaratnya tak dipenuhi orang itu kehilangan keberuntungan dan keterampilan, bahkan bisa mati.
statement.en: By legend whoever sees the Mistress falls under her spell; she is kind to good people and skilled craftsmen, helping them find jewels and gold, but if her conditions are not met the person loses all luck and skill and may even die.

claims.quote: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain became a well known character from her appearance in Pavel Bazhov's collection of Ural Mountains folktales (also known as skaz) under the title The Malachite Box.

statement.id: Nyonya Gunung Tembaga menjadi tokoh terkenal lewat kumpulan cerita rakyat Ural karya Pavel Bazhov, Kotak Malakit (The Malachite Box).
statement.en: The Mistress became well known through Pavel Bazhov's collection of Ural folktales, The Malachite Box.

claims.quote: The coat of arms of Polevskoy (from left to right): the Venus symbol (♀), which represents the chemical element copper and was the brand of the Polevskoy Copper Smelting Plant, the Mistress of the Copper Mountain depicted as the golden lizard

statement.id: Lambang kota Polevskoy menampilkan Nyonya Gunung Tembaga sebagai kadal emas.
statement.en: The coat of arms of Polevskoy shows the Mistress of the Copper Mountain as a golden lizard.

claims.quote: e.g. women did not come down in the mine, because it was the Mistress's domain, and young men seeking her patronage did not marry.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan itu, perempuan tidak turun ke tambang karena tambang adalah wilayah sang Nyonya, dan para pemuda yang mencari perlindungannya tidak menikah.
statement.en: According to the beliefs described, women did not go down into the mine because it was the Mistress's domain, and young men seeking her patronage did not marry.

claims.quote: Children were taught not to shout and quarrel next to the stones, and to keep quiet in the mines, because, according to popular belief, the Maid disliked loud noises.

statement.id: Anak-anak diajari agar tidak berteriak dan bertengkar di dekat batu dan diam di tambang, karena menurut kepercayaan rakyat sang Gadis tidak menyukai suara keras.
statement.en: Children were taught not to shout and quarrel near the stones and to keep quiet in the mines, because by popular belief the Maid disliked loud noises.

claims.quote: In many national folktales, the Mistress and Azovka (lit. "the Azov Girl") are identical with each other, and the same stories are told about each of them.

statement.id: Dalam banyak dongeng rakyat, sang Nyonya dan Azovka ("Gadis Azov") dianggap sama, dan kisah yang sama diceritakan tentang keduanya.
statement.en: In many folktales the Mistress and Azovka ("the Azov Girl") are identical, and the same stories are told about each.

claims.quote: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain may be called just "The Mistress of the Mountain", and also has many other names, such as The Mountain Mother

statement.id: Ia juga dapat disebut "Nyonya Gunung" dan memiliki banyak nama lain, antara lain Ibu Gunung.
statement.en: She may also be called "The Mistress of the Mountain" and has many other names, among them The Mountain Mother.

claims.quote: There is also a hypothesis that she represents the Roman goddess Venus, as local copper from the Polevskoy Copper Smelting Plant was branded with the Venus symbol

statement.id: Ada hipotesis bahwa ia mewakili dewi Romawi Venus, karena tembaga setempat dari pabrik peleburan tembaga Polevskoy dicap dengan lambang Venus.
statement.en: There is a hypothesis that she represents the Roman goddess Venus, because local copper from the Polevskoy Copper Smelting Plant was branded with the Venus symbol.

claims.quote: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain appears in the third Pavel Bazhov's skaz from The Malachite Box, "The Mistress of the Copper Mountain", first published in the 11th issue of Krasnaya Nov in 1936

statement.id: Sang Nyonya muncul dalam skaz ketiga Pavel Bazhov dari The Malachite Box, "The Mistress of the Copper Mountain", yang pertama kali terbit di edisi ke-11 Krasnaya Nov pada 1936.
statement.en: The Mistress appears in the third skaz of Pavel Bazhov's The Malachite Box, "The Mistress of the Copper Mountain", first published in issue 11 of Krasnaya Nov in 1936.

claims.quote: The character Queen of the Copper Mountain appeared in Mercedes Lackey's 2007 novel Fortune's Fool.

statement.id: Tokoh Queen of the Copper Mountain muncul dalam novel Fortune's Fool karya Mercedes Lackey tahun 2007.
statement.en: The character Queen of the Copper Mountain appeared in Mercedes Lackey's 2007 novel Fortune's Fool.

claims.quote: Из шелкового, слышь-ко, малахиту платье. Сорт такой бывает. Камень, а на глаз как шелк, хоть рукой погладить.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Bazhov, pakaian sang tokoh adalah gaun dari malakit sutra, batu yang tampak seperti sutra dan ingin diusap dengan tangan.
statement.en: In Bazhov's tale her dress is made of silk malachite, a stone that looks like silk and that one wants to stroke with the hand.

claims.quote: Он обошел и видит – ящерок тут несчисленно. И все, слышь-ко, разные. Одни, например, зеленые, другие голубые, которые в синь впадают, а то как глина либо песок с золотыми крапинками.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, pemuda itu melihat kadal yang tak terhitung banyaknya di sekitarnya, semuanya berbeda: ada yang hijau, ada yang biru, dan ada yang seperti tanah liat atau pasir dengan bintik emas.
statement.en: In the tale the young man sees countless lizards, all different: some green, some blue, some like clay or sand with golden specks.

claims.quote: Теперь тебе ступить некуда. Раздавишь мою слугу – беда будет.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, sang tokoh berkata kepada pemuda bahwa tidak ada tempat untuk melangkah dan bahwa menginjak pelayannya akan membawa celaka.
statement.en: In the tale she tells the young man he has nowhere to step and that trouble will follow if he crushes her servant.

claims.quote: Сама тоже на ноги вскочила, прихватилась рукой за камень, подскочила и тоже, как ящерка, побежала по камню-то. Вместо рук-ног – лапы у yее зеленые стали, хвост высунулся, по хребтине до половины черная полоска, а голова человечья.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, sang tokoh berlari menaiki batu seperti kadal: dari tangan dan kakinya tumbuh cakar hijau, ekor menjulur, ada garis hitam di punggung, dan kepalanya tetap kepala manusia.
statement.en: In the tale she runs up the rock like a lizard: green paws replace her hands and feet, a tail sticks out, a black stripe runs along the back, and her head stays human.

claims.quote: Мне как раз такого и надо, который никого не боится.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, sang tokoh berkata bahwa yang ia butuhkan adalah orang yang tidak takut pada siapa pun.
statement.en: In the tale she says that the person she needs is one who fears nobody.

claims.quote: Ежели еще будешь эту мою железную шапку ломать, так я тебе всю медь в Гумешках туда спущу, что никак ее не добыть

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, ia mengancam akan menurunkan semua tembaga di Gumeshki sedemikian dalam hingga tak dapat ditambang jika "topi besi"-nya terus dirusak.
statement.en: In the tale she threatens to sink all the copper in Gumeshki so deep it cannot be mined if her "iron cap" is broken any further.

claims.quote: Не обзарился ты на мои богатства, не променял свою Настеньку на каменну девку.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, ia memuji pemuda itu karena tidak tergiur kekayaannya dan tidak menukar tunangannya dengan "gadis batu".
statement.en: In the tale she praises the young man for not being tempted by her riches and not trading his fiancée for the "stone maiden".

claims.quote: Нашел, конечно, Степан. Что ему, коли он все нутро горы вызнал и сама Хозяйка ему пособляла.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, Stepan berhasil menemukannya karena ia mengenal seluruh isi gunung dan sang Nyonya sendiri membantunya.
statement.en: In the tale Stepan succeeds in finding it because he knows the whole inside of the mountain and the Mistress herself helped him.

claims.quote: Так с той поры Гумешки на убыль и пошли, а потом их и вовсе затопило. Говорили, что это Хозяйка огневалась за столбы – то, слышь-ко, что их в церкву поставили.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, tambang Gumeshki mulai menyusut dan akhirnya terendam; orang mengatakan sang Nyonya marah karena tiang-tiang dipasang di gereja.
statement.en: In the tale the Gumeshki mine began to decline and was finally flooded; people said the Mistress was angry because the pillars had been put up in a church.

short_description.id: Tin-Tin adalah duende dan tokoh mitos cerita rakyat pesisir Ekuador, berasal dari Pulau Puná. Kini ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk jahat berukuran kecil yang mengejar perempuan muda.
short_description.en: The Tin-Tin is a duende and mythical figure of Ecuador's coastal folklore, originally from Puná Island. Today he is described as a small malevolent being who pursues young women.

long_description.id: Tin-Tin (juga ditulis Tintín atau Tin-Tín) adalah duende dan tokoh mitos dalam cerita rakyat pesisir Ekuador yang berasal dari Pulau Puná. Legendanya menyebar lewat tradisi lisan para montubio, petani pesisir, dan penduduk pantai di seluruh zona pesisir Ekuador, termasuk daerah pedesaan dan berhutan di Guayaquil serta provinsi Manabí.
long_description.en: The Tin-Tin (also written Tintín or Tin-Tín) is a duende and mythical figure of Ecuador's coastal folklore, originally from Puná Island. His legend spread through the oral tradition of the montubios, coastal peasants, and coastal people across Ecuador's coastal zone, including the rural and wooded areas of Guayaquil and Manabí province.

long_description.id: Menurut versi yang tertulis, pada masa kini ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk jahat sejenis duende yang mengejar perempuan muda, lajang atau bersuami. Wujudnya kecil dan berkepala besar, mirip duende atau gnom ajaib, bertopi besar sekali, dan bersiul melengking yang muram. Di Isla Corazón (Manabí) ia disebut Felipe atau Felipe el tintin, dipercaya hidup di hutan bakau dan memikat perempuan dengan gitarnya.
long_description.en: In the written accounts, today he is described as a malevolent duende-like being who pursues young women, single or married. He is small and big-headed, resembling a duende or magical gnome, wearing an enormous hat and giving a wailing, gloomy whistle. On Isla Corazón (Manabí) he is called Felipe or Felipe el tintin, is believed to live in the mangroves, and charms women with his guitar.

long_description.id: Di beberapa bagian Manabí ia dikenal dapat berubah menjadi burung, khususnya Pedrote atau Motmot. Asalnya disebut berasal dari dewa pra-Hispanik Pulau Puná bernama Tin, sang Dewa Kelelawar yang aktif malam dan dapat membuahi perempuan. Salah satu ciri yang disebutkan mirip dengan versi Andes, Chuzalongo.
long_description.en: In some parts of Manabí he is known for being able to turn into a bird, specifically the Pedrote or Motmot. His origin is said to lie in a pre-Hispanic deity of Puná Island called Tin, a nocturnal Bat God who could impregnate women. One of the traits mentioned resembles the Andean version, the Chuzalongo.

short_description.id: Toyol atau tuyul adalah arwah bayi dalam cerita rakyat Melayu dan Indonesia yang dipanggil dukun dengan ilmu hitam, terutama untuk mencuri harta orang lain demi tuannya.
short_description.en: The toyol or tuyul is an undead infant of Malay and Indonesian folklore, invoked by shamans through black magic, chiefly to steal others’ wealth for its master.

long_description.id: Toyol atau tuyul adalah bayi mayat hidup dalam cerita rakyat Indonesia dan Melayu, yang juga dikenal dalam mitologi Asia Tenggara lain. Ia biasanya dipanggil sebagai pembantu oleh dukun, pawang, atau bomoh dengan ilmu hitam, terutama untuk mencuri harta orang. Toyol dikenal luas membawa untung bagi tuannya, tetapi kemalangan bagi orang yang sial bertemu dengannya.
long_description.en: The toyol or tuyul is an undead infant of Indonesian and Malay folklore, also found in other Southeast Asian mythologies. It is usually invoked as a helper by shamans (dukun, pawang or bomoh) through black magic, chiefly to rob people of their wealth. The toyol is popularly known to bring good luck to its master but mishap to those unfortunate enough to meet it.

long_description.id: Namanya berbeda di tiap daerah: toyol dalam bahasa Melayu, tuyul dalam bahasa Indonesia, thuyul dalam bahasa Jawa, dan kecit dalam bahasa Sunda; di Thailand, yang laki-laki disebut kuman-thong dan yang perempuan kuman-lay. Secara tradisional ia digambarkan seperti balita yang hampir telanjang; tuyul Indonesia ditambah kulit hijau dan telinga runcing, dan dapat memanjat dinding serta atap. Satu makalah menyebut toyol dipelihara tuannya dalam botol atau, dalam penuturan lain, disembunyikan dalam guci di rumah, dan bergerak begitu cepat sehingga tidak dapat ditangkap. Menurut makalah itu, toyol dapat dibeli dari orang yang mempraktikkan ilmu hitam seperti dukun, dan pembelinya perlu menjinakkannya.
long_description.en: Its name varies by region: toyol in Malay, tuyul in Indonesian, thuyul in Javanese and kecit in Sundanese; in Thailand the male is kuman-thong and the female kuman-lay. It is traditionally pictured as a near-naked toddler; the Indonesian tuyul adds green skin and pointed ears, and can scale walls and roofs. One paper says the toyol is kept by its master in a bottle or, in other accounts, hidden in a jar in the house, and moves so fast that people cannot catch it. According to that paper, a toyol can be bought from practitioners of black magic such as the dukun, and its buyer needs to tame it.

long_description.id: Sifatnya dikatakan seperti anak kecil yang suka bermain, menyukai permen, mainan, dan pakaian, dan konon hanya mencuri separuh barang berharga seseorang. Ukuran kecil dan tingkah kekanak-kanakannya dikatakan membuatnya tidak berbahaya, tetapi ia melakukan perbuatan jahil lain bila diperintah. Menurut satu makalah, tuannya harus memberinya makan darah dari jari kakinya setiap malam dan memberinya susu tiap pagi, dan ia hanya menuruti tuannya. Tanpa tuan, toyol dikatakan hidup bebas di hutan, dan menurut makalah yang sama ia tidak memangsa orang seperti tiyanak.
long_description.en: It is said to behave like a playful child that loves sweets, toys and clothes, and supposedly steals only half of a person’s valuables. Its small size and childish tendencies are said to make it harmless, yet it carries out other mischievous acts when commanded. According to one paper, its master must feed it blood from his toes every night and milk each morning, and it only obeys its master. Without a master the toyol is said to live freely in the woods, and according to the same paper it does not devour people as the tiyanak does.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan pada toyol punya fungsi sosial, antara lain sebagai alat pendisiplinan, penjaga hierarki sosial, dan pengusir orang luar, dan orang kaya atau sukses kerap dituduh memelihara toyol. Satu makalah tentang ritual pesugihan Jawa menyebut cerita tentang memiliki tuyul sebagai penilaian moral yang pedas terhadap tatanan ekonomi yang menindas orang miskin. Makalah lain menyebut kekayaan seketika dapat diperoleh lewat ritual dukun dengan imbalan darah yang diberikan anggota keluarga perempuan lewat menyusui, dan menafsirkan kepercayaan pada roh anak sebagai berakar pada keyakinan bahwa semua makhluk, termasuk bayi, punya jiwa; roh-roh itu digambarkan bernasib buruk hingga mati sebelum lahir.
long_description.en: Belief in the toyol has social functions, including discipline, maintaining social hierarchy and warding off outsiders, and wealthy or successful people are often accused of keeping one. One paper on a Javanese wealth ritual describes tales of owning a tuyul as a damning moral judgment about an economic order that weighs crushingly on the poor. Another paper says instant riches can be had through a dukun’s rituals in exchange for blood a female family member gives through breastfeeding, and interprets belief in child spirits as rooted in the belief that all beings, babies included, have a soul; these spirits are described as having met a bad fate, dying before birth.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan ini masih hidup: pada 2006 seorang nelayan di Kuala Pahang, Malaysia, melaporkan menemukan toyol dalam botol yang kemudian diserahkan ke museum negeri, dan pada 2019 warga Mengwi, Bali, menyalahkan tuyul atas hilangnya uang seorang warga.
long_description.en: The belief lives on: in 2006 a fisherman at Kuala Pahang, Malaysia, reported finding a bottled toyol that was handed to the state museum, and in 2019 residents of Mengwi, Bali, blamed a tuyul for a neighbour’s missing money.

cultural_context.id: Tuduhan memelihara toyol terhadap orang kaya atau pejabat dianggap sebagai cara menjelaskan ketimpangan sebagai hal di luar kendali, atau sekadar ungkapan rasa iri; satu makalah juga membacanya sebagai penilaian moral terhadap tatanan ekonomi yang menindas orang miskin.
cultural_context.en: Accusing the rich or officials of keeping a toyol is seen as a way to explain inequality as beyond one’s control, or simply to voice resentment; one paper also reads it as a moral judgment on an economic order that weighs on the poor.

claims.quote: A toyol or tuyul is an undead infant in Indonesian and Malay folklore. It also appears in the various other mythologies of Southeast Asia and is typically invoked as a helper by shamans (dukun, pawang, or bomoh) by means of black magic. A common use for the toyol includes using it for financial gain, where the creature robs people of their riches, making it similar to the Babi ngepet

statement.id: Toyol atau tuyul adalah bayi mayat hidup dalam cerita rakyat Indonesia dan Melayu, juga muncul dalam mitologi Asia Tenggara lain, dan biasanya dipanggil sebagai pembantu oleh dukun, pawang, atau bomoh dengan ilmu hitam; pemakaiannya yang umum adalah untuk keuntungan uang, dengan mencuri harta orang, mirip babi ngepet.
statement.en: The toyol or tuyul is an undead infant of Indonesian and Malay folklore, also in other Southeast Asian mythologies, typically invoked as a helper by shamans (dukun, pawang, bomoh) through black magic; a common use is financial gain, robbing people of their riches, similar to the babi ngepet.

claims.quote: The Malay word toyol is tuyul in Indonesian, thuyul in Javanese, and kecit in Sundanese. It is also known as cohen kroh in Khmer, and kwee kia in Hokkien. In Thai, the male is called kuman-thong while the female is named kuman-lay. A similar creature exists in Philippine mythology which is known as tiyanak.

statement.id: Toyol (Melayu) disebut tuyul dalam bahasa Indonesia, thuyul dalam bahasa Jawa, kecit dalam bahasa Sunda; di Thailand yang laki-laki kuman-thong dan yang perempuan kuman-lay; makhluk serupa di Filipina disebut tiyanak.
statement.en: Toyol (Malay) is tuyul in Indonesian, thuyul in Javanese, kecit in Sundanese; in Thai the male is kuman-thong and the female kuman-lay; a similar Philippine creature is the tiyanak.

claims.quote: The toyol is traditionally and commonly described as looking no different from a near-naked toddler. ... the toyol is claimed to look like a normal child with the exception of sharp teeth and red eyes, but the Indonesian tuyul has the addition of green skin and pointed ears. The tuyul has the ability to scale walls and climb roofs.

statement.id: Toyol secara tradisional digambarkan seperti balita hampir telanjang, dengan gigi tajam dan mata merah; tuyul Indonesia ditambah kulit hijau dan telinga runcing, dan dapat memanjat dinding serta atap.
statement.en: The toyol is traditionally a near-naked toddler with sharp teeth and red eyes; the Indonesian tuyul adds green skin and pointed ears and can scale walls and roofs.

claims.quote: The toyol's behaviour and personality is typically said to be similar to that of a playful child, where it enjoys sweets, toys, and clothes.

statement.id: Perilaku toyol dikatakan seperti anak kecil yang suka bermain, menyukai permen, mainan, dan pakaian.
statement.en: The toyol behaves like a playful child fond of sweets, toys and clothes.

claims.quote: Aside from the belief in the supernatural, the toyol serves a range of social functions, including acting as a disciplinary tool, to assist in maintaining social hierarchy, and to ward off perceived outsiders away from the community.

statement.id: Kepercayaan pada toyol punya fungsi sosial, antara lain sebagai alat pendisiplinan, penjaga hierarki sosial, dan pengusir orang luar.
statement.en: Belief in the toyol serves social functions, including discipline, maintaining hierarchy and warding off outsiders.

claims.quote: It is not an uncommon occurrence for people to associate those with wealth and success to having used a toyol, and this negative association is extended to even government officials.

statement.id: Orang kaya dan sukses, bahkan pejabat pemerintah, tidak jarang dituduh memakai toyol.
statement.en: The wealthy and successful, even government officials, are often associated with using a toyol.

claims.quote: These stories of corruption and amorality have been theorised to be a method of negating dissonance, where through associating social status with the supernatural, it allows for the people to believe and accept that the matter is beyond their control. statement.id: Cerita semacam ini diteorikan sebagai cara meredam disonansi, sehingga orang dapat menerima bahwa status sosial di luar kendali mereka; atau sekadar ungkapan rasa iri.
statement.en: Such stories are theorized as a way to reduce dissonance, letting people accept status as beyond their control; or simply a way to voice resentment.

short_description.id: Uirapuru é um ser mitológico brasileiro, descrito como um guerreiro transformado em pássaro e considerado o rei do amor. Segundo a lenda, ele canta para sua amada e seu canto é associado à sorte.
short_description.en: The Uirapuru is a Brazilian mythological being, described as a warrior turned into a bird and regarded as the king of love. In the legend he sings to his beloved, and his song is linked with luck.

long_description.id: Uirapuru adalah makhluk mitologi yang digambarkan sebagai manusia yang berubah menjadi burung, yang oleh masyarakat asli Brasil dianggap sebagai raja cinta. Dalam satu versi legenda, seorang pemuda pejuang jatuh cinta pada istri seorang kepala suku besar dan, karena tak dapat mendekatinya, meminta Tupã mengubahnya menjadi burung. Tupã mengabulkannya dengan menjadikannya burung berwarna merah bata yang bernyanyi pada malam hari untuk kekasihnya.
long_description.en: The Uirapuru is a mythological being described as a man turned into a bird, whom the Brazilian Indians regard as the king of love. In one version of the legend a young warrior fell in love with the wife of a great chief and, unable to approach her, asked Tupã to turn him into a bird. Tupã granted his wish, making him a brick-red bird that sang at night for his beloved.

long_description.id: Sang kepala suku ikut mendengar nyanyian itu dan, terpikat, mengejar burung itu untuk menangkapnya; namun Uirapuru bersembunyi di dalam hutan dan sang kepala suku tersesat di sana. Pada malam hari Uirapuru terus bernyanyi, berharap kekasihnya menemukan lagunya. Sumber lain menceritakan kisah serupa dengan seorang pejuang dan putri kepala suku.
long_description.en: The chief also noticed the song and, fascinated, chased the bird to capture it; but the Uirapuru hid deep in the forest and the chief got lost there. At night the Uirapuru keeps singing, hoping his beloved will discover his song. Another source tells a similar story of a warrior and the chief's daughter.

long_description.id: Uirapuru dianggap sebagai jimat pembawa kebahagiaan dalam cinta dan bisnis serta keberuntungan. Menurut Portal Amazônia, ada legenda bahwa orang yang mendengar nyanyiannya diberkati keberuntungan dan dapat mengajukan permintaan, serta legenda bahwa membawa bulu atau sepotong sarangnya menarik cinta dan kesetiaan; portal itu juga menyebut nyanyian burung ini unik, mampu berlangsung 10 atau 15 menit tanpa mengulang satu nada pun.
long_description.en: The Uirapuru is regarded as an amulet bringing happiness in love and business, and luck. According to Portal Amazônia, one legend says that whoever hears its song is blessed with luck and may make a wish, and another that carrying a feather or a piece of its nest attracts love and fidelity; the portal also calls the bird's song unique, able to run 10 or 15 minutes without repeating a note.

cultural_context.id: Uirapuru dianggap jimat pembawa kebahagiaan dalam cinta, bisnis, dan keberuntungan; Portal Amazônia menyebut sebagian legenda tentangnya, seperti mengubur burung itu di depan toko, ikut mengancam kelestariannya.
cultural_context.en: The Uirapuru is regarded as an amulet bringing happiness in love, business and luck; Portal Amazônia says some legends about it, such as burying the bird in front of a business, also threaten the species' survival.

short_description.id: Vrykolakas adalah mayat hidup berbahaya dalam cerita rakyat Yunani, umumnya disamakan dengan vampir Slavia; ia keluar dari makam, terutama pada malam hari.
short_description.en: The vrykolakas is a harmful undead creature of Greek folklore, generally equated with the Slavic vampire; it issues from the tomb, chiefly at night.

long_description.id: Vrykolakas adalah mayat hidup berbahaya dalam cerita rakyat Yunani. Ia mirip banyak makhluk legenda lain, tetapi umumnya disamakan dengan vampir dari cerita rakyat negara-negara Slavia tetangga.
long_description.en: The vrykolakas is a harmful undead creature of Greek folklore. It resembles many legendary creatures but is generally equated with the vampire of neighbouring Slavic folklore.

long_description.id: Dalam karya Lawson, Leo Allatius menulis bahwa vrykolakas adalah tubuh orang yang hidupnya jahat, sering yang dikucilkan uskupnya, yang tidak membusuk dan kulitnya meregang seperti kulit gendang. Menurutnya setan masuk ke dalam tubuh itu, yang keluar dari makam terutama pada malam hari untuk memanggil penghuni rumah, dan siapa yang menjawab mati keesokan harinya. Ia juga dikatakan membunuh orang hanya dengan penampakannya, bahkan pada siang hari.
long_description.en: In Lawson's work, Leo Allatius writes that the vrykolakas is the body of a man of evil life, often one excommunicated by his bishop, which does not decompose and whose skin stretches like the parchment of a drum. According to him the devil enters this body, which issues from the tomb chiefly at night to call one of the household, and whoever answers dies next day. It is also said to kill people by its mere aspect, even in the daytime.

long_description.id: Sebuah sejarah daerah yang dikutip Lawson menyatakan bahwa roh jahat masuk ke tubuh orang mati yang hidup jahat atau dikucilkan lalu berubah menjadi vrykolakas atau manusia-iblis. Kebiasaan umumnya adalah duduk di atas orang yang sedang tidur hingga menimbulkan rasa sesak yang menyiksa. Tembakan senjata api dapat mengusirnya, dan menurut Allatius tubuhnya dikeluarkan dari kubur dan dibakar di atas tumpukan kayu sementara para imam membacakan doa.
long_description.en: A district history quoted by Lawson says an evil spirit enters the body of a dead man who lived badly or was excommunicated and so becomes a vrykolakas or man-demon. Its common practice is to sit upon sleepers, causing an agonizing sense of oppression. The report of a gun can put it to flight, and according to Allatius the body is taken from the grave and burned on a pyre while priests recite prayers.

description.id: Menurut Leo Allatius dalam karya Lawson, ia dapat membunuh orang hanya dengan penampakannya, tanpa bicara atau sentuhan.
description.en: According to Leo Allatius in Lawson's work, it kills people by its mere aspect without speech or touch.

short_description.id: Waitoreke adalah makhluk kecil mirip berang-berang (otter) dalam cerita rakyat Selandia Baru yang dilaporkan hidup di Pulau Selatan; identitas aslinya masih diperdebatkan.
short_description.en: The waitoreke is a small otter-like creature of New Zealand folklore reported from the South Island; its true identity is still debated.

long_description.id: Waitoreke, juga disebut berang-berang Pulau Selatan, adalah makhluk mirip berang-berang (otter) atau berang-berang kastor (beaver) dalam cerita rakyat Selandia Baru. Dalam laporan-laporannya yang jarang ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai hewan kecil mirip berang-berang yang hidup di Pulau Selatan. Bukti keberadaannya terutama berupa laporan sporadis tentang "hewan amfibi tak dikenal" selama lebih dari 200 tahun.
long_description.en: The waitoreke, also called the South Island otter, is an otter- or beaver-like creature in New Zealand folklore. In its rare sightings it is usually described as a small otter-like animal living in the South Island. Evidence for it is mainly sporadic accounts of an "unidentified amphibious animal" spanning well over 200 years.

long_description.id: Menurut Tarawhata dalam catatan 1848 yang dikutip Pollock, hewan itu panjangnya dua kaki dari hidung ke pangkal ekor, tinggal di lubang, berbulu cokelat kelabu, berkaki pendek tebal, dan berekor lebat; ada dua jenis, jenis air yang makan ikan dan jenis darat yang makan kadal. Orang Māori juga mengatakan bahwa dahulu mereka memelihara waitoreke, dan Maopo memegang tradisi bahwa leluhurnya memeliharanya.
long_description.en: In Tarawhata's 1848 account as quoted by Pollock, the animal was two feet from nose to root of tail, lived in holes, and had grisly-brown fur, short thick legs and a bushy tail; there were two kinds, a water kind living on fish and a land kind living on lizards. The Māori also said that in old times they kept waitoreke as pets, and Maopo held the tradition that his forefathers kept one.

long_description.id: Haast menulis bahwa pada 1861 ia menemukan jejak mirip berang-berang tetapi sedikit lebih kecil di hulu Sungai Ashburton, dan ia dilaporkan memperoleh kulit pada 1868 yang berbulu cokelat berbintik putih serta tak berselaput jari; bukti itu tidak meyakinkan karena kulitnya tampak menyerupai kulit quoll. Laporan lebih baru, misalnya dari Sungai Waihopai dan Sungai Eglinton, melukiskan hewan gelap berkepala bulat kecil yang berenang atau berlari merunduk.
long_description.en: Haast wrote that in 1861 he found tracks similar to an otter's but a bit smaller on the upper Ashburton river, and he is reported to have obtained a pelt in 1868 that was brown with white spots and lacked webbing; the evidence is inconclusive because the pelt seems to have resembled a quoll's. Later accounts, for example from the Waihopai and Eglinton rivers, describe a dark animal with a small round head that swam or ran in a crouch.

long_description.id: Ada banyak teori tentang identitasnya, misalnya berang-berang (otter), berang-berang kastor (beaver), atau pinnipedia. Pollock menyimpulkan bahwa waitoreke tradisi Māori adalah hewan nyata, berang-berang genus Lutra dari spesies Asia yang belum teridentifikasi, yang didatangkan berabad-abad lalu oleh pelaut atau nelayan dari Asia Tenggara; ia mencatat para zoolog umumnya menepisnya sebagai mitos. Satu-satunya mamalia darat endemik Selandia Baru yang diakui adalah kelelawar.
long_description.en: There are many theories about its identity, such as an otter, beaver or pinniped. Pollock concludes that the waitoreke of Māori tradition is an actual animal, an otter of genus Lutra of some Asian species yet to be identified, introduced centuries ago by mariners or fishermen from South-east Asia; he notes that zoologists have generally dismissed it as a myth. New Zealand's only recognised endemic land mammals are bats.

literal_meaning.id: Asal namanya tidak terdokumentasi dengan baik; Pollock mengusulkan "waitorengi", "menghilang di dalam air".
literal_meaning.en: The origin of the name is not well documented; Pollock proposes "waitorengi", "disappearing in the water".

claims.quote: My friend Haast wrote me about vaitoteke (sic) on June 6, 1861: '3500 feet above the sea level I found, on the upper part of Ashburton river (South Island, Canterbury province), in a part of the country which no man has ever visited before me, its tracks. claims.quote: Tarawhata himself in 1848 gave Mantell a description which is full of otter-like detail. It was, he said. two feet from nose to root of tail, lived in holes, had grislybrown fur, short thick legs. bushy tail and a head between that of a dog and cat.

statement.en: According to Pollock, Tarawhata in 1848 gave Mantell a description full of otter-like detail: two feet from nose to root of tail, living in holes, with grisly-brown fur, short thick legs, a bushy tail and a head between that of a dog and a cat.

claims.quote: added the interesting if puzzling information that there were two kinds - a water kind living on fish. a land kind on lizards

statement.en: The account added the interesting if puzzling information that there were two kinds, a water kind living on fish and a land kind living on lizards.

claims.quote: G. l. Moffett in April 1924, while fishing in the Eglinton River. saw one morning, about 100 yards off, a small animal of a dark colour running rather rapidly in a crouching manner. It had apparently come up out of the river, to which it swiftly returned on Moffett's approach.

statement.en: Moffett, fishing in the Eglinton River in April 1924, saw a small dark animal running rather rapidly in a crouching manner; it had apparently come up out of the river and swiftly returned to it as he approached.

statement.en: Pollock concludes that the waitoreke of Maori tradition is an actual, not a mythical, animal; that it is an otter (genus Lutra) of some Asian species yet to be identified; and that it was introduced centuries ago by storm-driven mariners or fishermen from South-east Asia.

short_description.id: Zhu adalah burung pertanda buruk mirip burung hantu dengan tangan manusia dalam Kitab Gunung dan Laut.
short_description.en: Zhu is an ominous owl-like bird with human hands in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

long_description.id: Zhu adalah burung pertanda buruk mirip burung hantu dengan tangan manusia dalam Kitab Gunung dan Laut. Bagian pegunungan selatan menempatkannya di Gunung Ju.
long_description.en: Zhu is an ominous owl-like bird with human hands in the Classic of Mountains and Seas. The southern-mountains section places it at Mount Ju.

long_description.id: Suaranya menyerupai puyuh betina dan penampakannya meramalkan pengasingan pejabat. Pembacaan harfiah membedakan burung bertangan manusia dari burung berwajah manusia.
long_description.en: Its call resembles a female quail and its sighting portends officials’ exile. A literal reading distinguishes a human-handed bird from a human-faced bird.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, burung zhu adalah jelmaan Danzhu, putra Yao, yang memberontak setelah ayahnya menyerahkan dunia kepada Shun; setelah kalah, ia menceburkan diri ke Laut Selatan karena malu dan berubah menjadi burung ini. Keturunannya konon mendirikan negeri Danzhu yang penduduknya berwajah manusia dan bersayap burung.
long_description.en: According to legend, the zhu bird is the transformed Danzhu, son of Yao, who rebelled after his father gave the realm to Shun; defeated, he drowned himself in the Southern Sea out of shame and became this bird. His descendants are said to have founded the Danzhu country, whose people have human faces and bird wings.

long_description.id: Teks Nanshan Jing menggambarkannya seperti burung hantu bertangan manusia, dengan suara seperti puyuh betina; komentarnya menjelaskan bahwa kakinya seperti tangan manusia.
long_description.en: The Nanshan Jing text describes it as like an owl with human hands and a voice like a female quail; the commentary explains that its feet are like human hands.

note.id: Menurut legenda, burung zhu adalah jelmaan Danzhu.
note.en: According to legend, the zhu bird is the transformed Danzhu.

claims.quote: 鴸（しゅ）は、『山海経』「南山経」に記載される怪鳥。梟に似た人間の手を持つ鳥で、鴸が現れた場所では多くの官吏が追放されるという不吉な鳥。

statement.id: Zhu adalah burung pertanda buruk mirip burung hantu dengan tangan manusia dalam Kitab Gunung dan Laut.
statement.en: Zhu is an ominous owl-like bird with human hands in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

claims.quote: 形状は 鴟 （ フクロウ ） に似て、人の手をもつ怪鳥が、 柜山 （ くさん ） （「ヤナギ」の意の山）に棲んでいると『南山経』に記される。

statement.id: Bagian pegunungan selatan menempatkannya di Gunung Ju.
statement.en: The southern-mountains section places it at Mount Ju.

claims.quote: その鳴き声は痺（ウズラの雌）に似ており、その鴸と言う名称も、鳴き声にちなむ。人の目にふれることあれば、それはその県で多くの放士（官吏の放逐）がされる予兆だとしている。

statement.id: Suaranya menyerupai puyuh betina dan penampakannya meramalkan pengasingan pejabat.
statement.en: Its call resembles a female quail and its sighting portends officials’ exile.

claims.quote: あくまで『山海経』じたいの文にしたがうならば、人の手を持つ鳥には属すが、人面鳥には属さない。

statement.id: Pembacaan harfiah membedakan burung bertangan manusia dari burung berwajah manusia.
statement.en: A literal reading distinguishes a human-handed bird from a human-faced bird.

claims.quote: 有鳥焉，其狀如鴟而人手。〈其腳如人手，鴟音處脂反〉其音如痺，〈未詳〉其名曰鴸

statement.id: Teks Nanshan Jing (南山經): ada burung seperti burung hantu (鴟) dengan tangan manusia (人手) — komentarnya menjelaskan kakinya seperti tangan manusia — suaranya seperti puyuh betina (痺), dan namanya Zhu (鴸).
statement.en: The Nanshan Jing (南山經) text: there is a bird like an owl (鴟) with human hands (人手) — the commentary explains its feet are like human hands — its voice is like a female quail (痺), and its name is Zhu (鴸).

claims.quote: 傳說是堯的兒子丹朱所化成的動物。堯把天下讓給舜後，丹朱和三苗國人聯合起兵反對，堯便派兵打敗了他們，丹朱因為感到羞愧，自投南海淹死而化作鴸鳥。

statement.id: Menurut legenda, burung zhu adalah jelmaan Danzhu (丹朱), putra Yao (堯): setelah Yao menyerahkan dunia kepada Shun (舜), Danzhu bersama orang Sanmiao memberontak, dikalahkan, lalu karena malu menceburkan diri ke Laut Selatan (南海) dan berubah menjadi burung zhu.
statement.en: According to legend, the zhu bird is the transformed Danzhu (丹朱), son of Yao (堯): after Yao gave the realm to Shun (舜), Danzhu rose with the Sanmiao people, was defeated, and out of shame drowned himself in the Southern Sea (南海) and became the zhu bird.

claims.quote: 傳說丹朱的子孫在南海建立了一個丹朱國，這裏的人長相很奇特，長著人的臉，鳥的翅膀。

statement.id: Legenda juga menyebut keturunan Danzhu mendirikan negeri Danzhu (丹朱國) di Laut Selatan, yang penduduknya berwajah manusia dan bersayap burung.
statement.en: Legend also says Danzhu’s descendants founded the Danzhu country (丹朱國) in the Southern Sea, whose people have human faces and bird wings.

short_description.id: Baxia (𧈢𧏡, sering keliru ditulis 蚣蝮) adalah salah satu putra naga dalam tradisi Tionghoa; ia gemar air, dan sosoknya diukir pada pilar, talang, jembatan, serta saluran keluar air.
short_description.en: Baxia (𧈢𧏡, often wrongly written 蚣蝮) is one of the dragon's sons in Chinese tradition; it is fond of water and its likeness is carved on pillars, gutters, bridges and water outlets.

long_description.id: Baxia (𧈢𧏡, pinyin Bāxià, juga ditulis 覇下) termasuk sembilan putra naga. Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyatakan bahwa namanya sering keliru ditulis 蚣蝮 (gōngfù).
long_description.en: Baxia (𧈢𧏡, pinyin Bāxià, also written 覇下) is counted among the dragon's nine sons. Chinese Wikipedia says that its name is often wrongly written 蚣蝮 (gōngfù).

long_description.id: Ia gemar air. Sosoknya diukir sebagai hiasan pada tiang, talang, jembatan, dan bagian keluar saluran air; kepala-kepala menyerupai naga yang menjulur dari pagar bangunan di Kota Terlarang menjadi contohnya. Dalam daftar yang dikutip Yŏrha ilgi dari 楊用修丹鉛錄, 𧈢𧏡 adalah putra keenam yang bersifat gemar air dan berdiri di tiang jembatan.
long_description.en: It is fond of water. Its likeness is carved as decoration on pillars, gutters, bridges and water outlets; the dragonlike heads projecting from the railings of buildings in the Forbidden City are an example. In the list quoted by the Yŏrha ilgi from 楊用修's 丹鉛錄, 𧈢𧏡 is the sixth son, which by nature likes water and stands on bridge pillars.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber tidak sepakat tentang hubungannya dengan 贔屭 (Bixi). Dalam daftar dari 丹鉛錄, 贔屭 adalah putra pertama yang berbentuk kura-kura dan pandai memikul beban. Kamus Kangxi, mengutip Bencao, menyebut 贔屭 kura-kura besar yang gemar memikul beban "atau bernama 𧈢𧏡". Yŏrha ilgi juga mengutip Zonggui yang menyebut 覇夏 gemar memikul beban sehingga menjadi alas prasasti, lalu mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui.
long_description.en: Sources disagree about its relationship to 贔屭 (Bixi). In the list from the 丹鉛錄, 贔屭 is the first son, turtle-shaped and good at bearing heavy loads. The Kangxi Dictionary, quoting the Bencao, calls 贔屭 a large turtle that likes bearing heavy loads "or named 𧈢𧏡". The Yŏrha ilgi also quotes the Zonggui, which says 覇夏 likes bearing heavy loads and so serves as a stele base, and then asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known.

who.id: Salah satu dari sembilan putra naga, bernama 𧈢𧏡 (Baxia).
who.en: One of the dragon's nine sons, named 𧈢𧏡 (Baxia).

origin.id: Dicatat dalam daftar putra naga yang dikutip dari 楊用修丹鉛錄.
origin.en: Recorded in a list of the dragon's sons quoted from 楊用修's 丹鉛錄.

role.id: Putra naga yang gemar air dan menjadi motif ukiran pada pilar, talang, jembatan, dan saluran air.
role.en: A son of the dragon fond of water, used as a carved motif on pillars, gutters, bridges and water outlets.

famous_for.id: Dikenal sebagai putra naga penjaga tiang jembatan yang gemar air.
famous_for.en: Known as the water-loving dragon's son of the bridge pillar.

note.id: Kamus Kangxi, mengutip Bencao, menyebut 贔屭 (Bixi) "atau bernama 𧈢𧏡", sedangkan daftar dari 丹鉛錄 menempatkan keduanya sebagai putra yang berbeda.
note.en: The Kangxi Dictionary, quoting the Bencao, says 贔屭 (Bixi) is "or named 𧈢𧏡", while the list from the 丹鉛錄 treats the two as different sons.

claims.quote: 𧈢𧏡（はか、拼音：Bāxià）は、竜生九子の一つ。覇下とも書かれる。

statement.id: Baxia termasuk sembilan anak naga.
statement.en: Baxia is counted among the nine offspring of the dragon.

claims.quote: 水を好み、柱や雨樋、橋や、水路の出口の意匠として彫られる。中国の故宮などの建物の欄干からたくさん頭を突き出した龍に似た動物がこれである。

statement.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan air dan diukir pada pilar, talang, jembatan, serta saluran keluar.
statement.en: It is associated with water and carved on pillars, gutters, bridges and outlets.

claims.quote: 水を好み、柱や雨樋、橋や、水路の出口の意匠として彫られる。中国の故宮などの建物の欄干からたくさん頭を突き出した龍に似た動物がこれである。

statement.id: Kepala menyerupai naga yang menonjol dari pagar Kota Terlarang merupakan contoh motif itu.
statement.en: Dragonlike heads projecting from Forbidden City railings exemplify the motif.

claims.quote: 楊用修丹鉛錄曰。龍產九子不成龍。一曰贔屭。 ... 六曰𧈢𧏡。性好水。立橋柱。

statement.id: Dalam Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記) dikutip daftar dari 楊用修丹鉛錄: sembilan putra naga tidak menjadi naga; putra pertama adalah 贔屭, dan putra keenam adalah 𧈢𧏡, yang bersifat gemar air (性好水) dan berdiri di tiang jembatan (立橋柱).
statement.en: The Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記) quotes a list from 楊用修's 丹鉛錄: the dragon's nine sons did not become dragons; the first is 贔屭, and the sixth is 𧈢𧏡, which by nature likes water (性好水) and stands on bridge pillars (立橋柱).

claims.quote: 楊用修丹鉛錄曰。龍產九子不成龍。一曰贔屭。形似龜。善負重。今碑龜趺是也。

statement.id: Dalam daftar yang sama, putra pertama adalah 贔屭, berbentuk kura-kura dan pandai memikul beban; sosoknya adalah alas prasasti berbentuk kura-kura (碑龜趺).
statement.en: In the same list the first son is 贔屭, shaped like a turtle and good at bearing heavy loads; its likeness is the turtle base of steles (碑龜趺).

claims.quote: 又總龜云。龍之九子。一名覇夏。好負重。故爲碑座。贔屭。好文故在碑文兩旁。諸說亦各不同。龍子名號及性情。何以知之。古說傅會多此類。

statement.id: Teks yang sama mengutip Zonggui (總龜): salah satu putra naga, 覇夏, gemar memikul beban sehingga menjadi alas prasasti, dan 贔屭 gemar sastra sehingga berada di sisi tulisan prasasti. Penulisnya menyimpulkan bahwa pendapat-pendapat itu berbeda-beda, mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
statement.en: The same text cites the Zonggui (總龜): one of the dragon's sons, 覇夏, likes bearing heavy loads and so serves as a stele base, and 贔屭 likes literature and is found at the sides of the inscription. The author concludes that the accounts differ, asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and says old theories of this kind are mostly embellishment.

claims.quote: 《本草》贔屭，大龜，蟕蠵之屬，好負重。或名𧈢𧏡。今石𥓓下龜跌象其形。

statement.id: Kamus Kangxi, dalam entri 贔, mengutip Bencao (本草): 贔屭 (Bixi) adalah kura-kura besar sejenis 蟕蠵 yang gemar memikul beban, "atau bernama 𧈢𧏡", dan kini alas prasasti berbentuk kura-kura meniru bentuknya.
statement.en: The Kangxi Dictionary, in its entry 贔, quotes the Bencao (本草): 贔屭 (Bixi) is a large turtle of the 蟕蠵 kind that likes bearing heavy loads, "or named 𧈢𧏡".

claims.quote: 常被误写作 蚣 （ gōng ） 蝮 （ fù ） ，传说中龙生九子之一，性喜水，被雕成桥柱、建筑上滴水的兽形。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyatakan bahwa 𧈢𧏡 (bā xià) sering keliru ditulis 蚣蝮 (gōng fù); ia salah satu putra naga yang gemar air dan diukir sebagai tiang jembatan serta bentuk binatang penyalur air pada bangunan.
statement.en: Chinese Wikipedia says that 𧈢𧏡 (bā xià) is often wrongly written 蚣蝮 (gōng fù); it is one of the dragon's sons, fond of water, carved as bridge pillars and as drain-spout beasts on buildings.

topic.id: Apakah 𧈢𧏡 sama dengan 贔屭 (Bixi), dan apa sifatnya
topic.en: Whether 𧈢𧏡 is the same as 贔屭 (Bixi), and what its nature is

summary.id: Daftar dari 丹鉛錄: 𧈢𧏡 putra keenam yang gemar air dan berdiri di tiang jembatan; 贔屭 putra pertama yang berbentuk kura-kura dan memikul beban.
summary.en: List from the 丹鉛錄: 𧈢𧏡 is the sixth son, fond of water and standing on bridge pillars; 贔屭 is the first son, turtle-shaped and bearing loads.

summary.id: Kamus Kangxi mengutip Bencao: 贔屭 adalah kura-kura besar yang gemar memikul beban, atau bernama 𧈢𧏡.
summary.en: The Kangxi Dictionary quotes the Bencao: 贔屭 is a large turtle that likes bearing heavy loads, or named 𧈢𧏡.

summary.id: Zonggui seperti dikutip Yŏrha ilgi: 覇夏 gemar memikul beban dan menjadi alas prasasti; penulis menilai pendapat-pendapat itu saling berbeda.
summary.en: The Zonggui as quoted in the Yŏrha ilgi: 覇夏 likes bearing loads and serves as a stele base; the author judges that the accounts differ from one another.

short_description.id: Bibi adalah makhluk Tiongkok mirip rubah bersayap dalam Kitab Gunung dan Laut.
short_description.en: Bibi is a winged foxlike Chinese creature in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

long_description.id: Bibi adalah makhluk Tiongkok mirip rubah bersayap dalam Kitab Gunung dan Laut.
long_description.en: Bibi is a winged foxlike Chinese creature in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

long_description.id: Suara mirip angsa dan kemunculannya terkait dengan kekeringan.
long_description.en: Its goose-like cry and appearance are associated with drought.

long_description.id: Teks sumbernya, Kitab Gunung dan Laut, menempatkan binatang ini di Gunung Gufeng, tempat tanpa rumput dan pohon yang kaya emas dan batu giok. Binatang itu bernama Bibi, berbentuk seperti rubah bersayap, bersuara seperti angsa liar, dan kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan kekeringan besar. Edisi Siku Quanshu memuat kalimat yang sama dengan catatan lafal, dan Wikipedia Mandarin mencatat bahwa Bibi juga muncul dalam novel panjang akhir Dinasti Qing, Hushan ji.
long_description.en: The source text, the Classic of Mountains and Seas, places this beast on Mount Gufeng, a place without grass or trees and rich in gold and jade. The Siku Quanshu edition has the same sentence with a pronunciation note, and Chinese Wikipedia notes that Bibi also appears in the late Qing long novel Hushan ji.

long_description.en: Classical Chinese texts discuss the maoxiao (貓魈), a cat spirit associated with Jinhua. In the tale Zhoushi mai hua, a flour seller named Yu names the cause of a girl's haunting a maoxiao and slays it by ritual. In the Xu Zibuyu, Yuan Mei likens other disease-bringing spirits to the maoxiao of Jinhua, which he calls a kind of demon-spirit.
