short_description.id: Wuzhiqi adalah makhluk gaib Tiongkok yang lazim digambarkan sebagai iblis air mirip kera.
short_description.en: Wuzhiqi is a Chinese supernatural being commonly depicted as a monkey-like aquatic demon.

long_description.id: Wuzhiqi adalah makhluk gaib Tiongkok yang lazim digambarkan sebagai iblis air mirip kera. Tangguoshi Bu mencatat kera bertubuh hitam dan berkepala putih di Sungai Huai.
long_description.en: Wuzhiqi is a Chinese supernatural being commonly depicted as a monkey-like aquatic demon. The Tangguoshi Bu records a black-bodied, white-headed monkey in the Huai River.

long_description.id: Taiping Guangji, yang mengutip Yue Du Jing, menyebut Wuzhiqi sebagai dewa air Sungai Huai dan Guo yang pandai berbicara. Wujudnya seperti kera berkepala putih bermata emas, berleher panjang yang dapat memanjang, dengan tenaga melebihi sembilan gajah dan gerak yang gesit.
long_description.en: The Taiping Guangji, quoting the Yue Du Jing, names Wuzhiqi as a talkative water god of the Huai and Guo rivers. Its form is like an ape with a white head and golden eyes and a neck that can stretch, with strength surpassing nine elephants and swift movement.

long_description.id: Taiping Guangji menyebut kekalahannya oleh Yu dan penahanan di bawah Gunung Kura-kura. Zhanglü dan Niaomuyou tidak mampu menaklukkannya, hanya Gengchen yang mampu; lehernya lalu dirantai, hidungnya ditindik lonceng emas, dan ia dipindahkan ke kaki Gunung Gui di Huaiyin.
long_description.en: The Taiping Guangji describes defeat by Yu and confinement beneath Turtle Mountain. Zhanglü and Niaomuyou could not subdue it, only Gengchen could; its neck was then chained, its nose pierced with a golden bell, and it was moved to the foot of Turtle Mountain at Huaiyin.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Li Tang, para nelayan menarik sebuah rantai besi dengan lima puluh lembu lebih hingga muncul binatang berbentuk kera yang lalu menarik rantai dan lembu-lembu itu masuk ke air; teks menyatakan kisah itu cocok dengan Yue Du Jing.
long_description.en: In the Li Tang story, fishermen pulled an iron chain with more than fifty oxen until an ape-shaped beast emerged and then dragged the chain and oxen into the water; the text says the story matches the Yue Du Jing.

long_description.id: Patung besi Wuzhiqi di Museum Seni Asia Berlin diidentifikasi Poul Andersen pada 2001. Sebagian peneliti mengusulkannya sebagai model Sun Wukong, tetapi kedua tokoh tetap berbeda dalam novel.
long_description.en: Poul Andersen identified a Wuzhiqi iron statue at Berlin's Asian Art Museum in 2001. Some scholars propose it as a model for Sun Wukong, but the figures remain distinct in the novel.

description.id: Teks Taiping Guangji menyebut tenaganya melebihi sembilan gajah dan ia gesit menyerang, melompat, dan berlari.
description.en: The Taiping Guangji text says its strength surpasses nine elephants and that it strikes, leaps and runs swiftly.

description.id: Lehernya disebut dapat memanjang seratus chi.
description.en: Its neck is said to stretch a hundred chi.

description.id: Zhanglü dan Niaomuyou tidak mampu menaklukkannya; hanya Gengchen yang mampu, dan ia lalu dirantai serta dipindahkan ke kaki Gunung Gui.
description.en: Zhanglü and Niaomuyou could not subdue it; only Gengchen could, and it was then chained and moved to the foot of Turtle Mountain.

role.id: Wuzhiqi adalah dewa air Huai dan Guo yang akhirnya ditaklukkan.
role.en: Wuzhiqi is the Huai-and-Guo water god who is finally subdued.

summary.id: Menurut Yue Du Jing yang dikutip, Yu menyerahkan dewa air Huai dan Guo bernama Wuzhiqi kepada para penakluk; hanya Gengchen yang dapat menaklukkannya, lalu ia dirantai dan dipindahkan ke kaki Gunung Gui.
summary.en: According to the quoted Yue Du Jing, Yu handed the water god of the Huai and Guo named Wuzhiqi to would-be subduers; only Gengchen could subdue it, and it was chained and moved to the foot of Turtle Mountain.

title.id: Li Tang dan rantai di Gunung Gui
title.en: Li Tang and the chain at Turtle Mountain

role.id: Binatang berbentuk kera di ujung rantai, yang teks sebut sesuai dengan Yue Du Jing.
role.en: The ape-shaped beast at the end of the chain, which the text says matches the Yue Du Jing.

summary.id: Nelayan menemukan rantai besi di kaki gunung; setelah ditarik lima puluh lembu lebih, muncul binatang berbentuk kera yang kemudian menarik rantai dan lembu-lembu itu masuk ke air.
summary.en: Fishermen found an iron chain at the foot of the mountain; after more than fifty oxen pulled it, an ape-shaped beast emerged and then dragged the chain and oxen back into the water.

description.id: Tempat Wuzhiqi dikurung di kakinya dengan leher dirantai dan hidung ditindik lonceng emas.
description.en: The place at whose foot Wuzhiqi was confined with its neck chained and its nose pierced with a golden bell.

note.id: Teks menyebut Yu menyerahkan Wuzhiqi kepada para calon penakluk.
note.en: The text has Yu handing Wuzhiqi to would-be subduers.

note.id: Gengchen satu-satunya yang mampu menaklukkan Wuzhiqi.
note.en: Gengchen was the only one able to subdue Wuzhiqi.

claims.quote: Wuzhiqi (Chinese: 無支祁) is a supernatural being in Chinese mythology popularly depicted as a monkey-like aquatic demon and first described in the early 9th century.

statement.id: Wuzhiqi adalah makhluk gaib Tiongkok yang lazim digambarkan sebagai iblis air mirip kera.
statement.en: Wuzhiqi is a Chinese supernatural being commonly depicted as a monkey-like aquatic demon.

claims.quote: The earliest description of Wuzhiqi can be found in the Tangguoshi Bu, Li Zhao's 9th-century supplement to the Book of Tang. It briefly tells of a fisherman in Chuzhou (楚州) who encounters a monkey demon with a black body and a white head in the Huai River.

statement.id: Tangguoshi Bu mencatat kera bertubuh hitam dan berkepala putih di Sungai Huai.
statement.en: The Tangguoshi Bu records a black-bodied, white-headed monkey in the Huai River.

claims.quote: Wuzhiqi is also described in the Song dynasty anthology Taiping guangji as a "monkey-like demon" residing in the Huai River; it is defeated by Yu the Great and imprisoned under Turtle Mountain (龜山) as part of his effort to control the Great Flood.

statement.id: Taiping Guangji menyebut kekalahannya oleh Yu dan penahanan di bawah Gunung Kura-kura.
statement.en: The Taiping Guangji describes defeat by Yu and confinement beneath Turtle Mountain.

claims.quote: A cast-iron statue depicting Wuzhiqi was gifted to the German artist Hanna Bekker vom Rath and later housed at the Museum of Asian Art in Berlin. Described as the "most intriguing and puzzling gift" to the museum, it was only identified in 2001 by University of Hawaii professor Poul Andersen. Andersen also documented the emergence of Wuzhiqi-inspired cults in northern Anhui.

statement.id: Patung besi Wuzhiqi di Museum Seni Asia Berlin diidentifikasi Poul Andersen pada 2001.
statement.en: Poul Andersen identified a Wuzhiqi iron statue at Berlin's Asian Art Museum in 2001.

claims.quote: Wuzhiqi "has provided many scholars with a prototype of Sun Wukong" ... but that Wuzhiqi and Sun Wukong are "kept quite distinct" in the novel.

statement.id: Sebagian peneliti mengusulkannya sebagai model Sun Wukong, tetapi kedua tokoh tetap berbeda dalam novel.
statement.en: Some scholars propose it as a model for Sun Wukong, but the figures remain distinct in the novel.

claims.quote: 乃獲淮、渦水神，名無支祁，善應對言語，辨江淮之淺深，原隰之遠近。

statement.id: Teks Taiping Guangji (太平廣記) menyebut dewa air Sungai Huai (淮) dan Sungai Guo (渦) bernama Wuzhiqi (無支祁) yang pandai menjawab dan berbicara serta dapat membedakan dalam-dangkalnya sungai dan jauh-dekatnya dataran.
statement.en: The Taiping Guangji (太平廣記) text names a water god of the Huai (淮) and Guo (渦) rivers, Wuzhiqi (無支祁), skilled at answering and speaking and able to judge the depth of the rivers and the distance across the plains.

claims.quote: 名無支祁，善應對言語，辨江淮之淺深，原隰之遠近。形若猿猴，縮鼻高額，青軀白首，金目雪牙，頸伸百尺，力窬九象，搏擊騰踔疾奔，輕利倏忽，聞視不可久。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Wujudnya seperti kera dengan hidung pendek, dahi tinggi, tubuh biru kehijauan, kepala putih, mata emas, dan taring seputih salju; lehernya dapat memanjang seratus chi, tenaganya melebihi sembilan gajah, dan ia gesit menyerang, melompat, dan berlari.
statement.en: Its form is like an ape with a shrunken nose, high forehead, blue-green body, white head, golden eyes and snow-white teeth; its neck can stretch a hundred chi, its strength surpasses nine elephants, and it strikes, leaps and runs swiftly.

claims.quote: 乃獲淮、渦水神，名無支祁，善應對言語 ... 禹授之章律，不能制；授之鳥木由，不能制；授之庚辰，能制。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Yu (禹) menyerahkannya kepada Zhanglü (章律) dan Niaomuyou (鳥木由) tetapi keduanya tidak dapat menaklukkannya; hanya Gengchen (庚辰) yang mampu menaklukkannya.
statement.en: Yu (禹) handed it to Zhanglü (章律) and Niaomuyou (鳥木由), who could not subdue it; only Gengchen (庚辰) could.

claims.quote: 乃獲淮、渦水神，名無支祁，善應對言語 ... 鴟脾桓木魅水靈山妖石怪，奔號聚繞以數十載，庚辰以戰逐去。頸鎖大索，鼻穿金鈴，徙淮陰之龜山之足下，俾淮水永安流注海也。庚辰之後，皆圖此形者，免淮濤風雨之難。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Gengchen (庚辰) mengusir makhluk-makhluk gaib yang mengerumuninya lewat pertempuran; leher Wuzhiqi dirantai dan hidungnya ditindik lonceng emas, lalu ia dipindahkan ke kaki Gunung Gui (龜山) di Huaiyin (淮陰) agar Sungai Huai mengalir tenang ke laut. Sejak itu, orang yang menggambar wujud ini dikatakan terhindar dari bencana gelombang dan hujan angin Sungai Huai.
statement.en: Gengchen (庚辰) drove off the spirit-beings crowding around it in battle; its neck was chained and its nose pierced with a golden bell, and it was moved to the foot of Turtle Mountain (龜山) at Huaiyin (淮陰) so the Huai River would flow peacefully to the sea. After that, those who drew this form were said to avoid the troubles of Huai waves, wind and rain.

claims.quote: 遂告湯，湯命漁人及能水者數十，獲其鎖，力莫能制。加以牛五十餘頭，鎖乃振動，稍稍就岸。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Dalam kisah Li Tang (李湯), puluhan nelayan dan perenang menemukan rantai besi di kaki gunung dan tidak mampu menariknya sampai lebih dari lima puluh lembu ditambahkan, hingga rantai itu bergerak dan sedikit demi sedikit mendekati tepi.
statement.en: In the Li Tang (李湯) story, dozens of fishermen and swimmers got hold of an iron chain and could not control it until more than fifty oxen were added, when the chain stirred and gradually drew toward the bank.

claims.quote: 鎖之末，見一獸，狀有如猿，白首長鬐，雪牙金爪，闖然上岸，高五丈許。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Di ujung rantai itu muncul seekor binatang berbentuk seperti kera dengan kepala putih, surai panjang, taring seputih salju, dan cakar emas, yang naik ke darat dengan tinggi sekitar lima zhang.
statement.en: At the end of the chain appeared a beast shaped like an ape, with a white head, long mane, snow-white teeth and golden claws, which burst ashore about five zhang tall.

claims.quote: 久乃引頸伸欠，雙目忽開，光彩若電。顧視人焉，欲發狂怒。觀者奔走。獸亦徐徐引鎖拽牛，入水去，竟不復出。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Binatang itu akhirnya menjulurkan leher dan membuka matanya yang berkilau seperti kilat, menoleh ke orang-orang seolah hendak mengamuk sehingga para penonton lari, lalu perlahan menarik rantai beserta lembu-lembu itu masuk ke air dan tidak muncul lagi.
statement.en: The beast finally stretched its neck and opened eyes that flashed like lightning, glared at the people as if to rage so that the onlookers fled, then slowly dragged the chain and the oxen into the water and never reappeared.

claims.quote: 獸亦徐徐引鎖拽牛，入水去，竟不復出。 ... 即李湯之見，與楊衡之說，與《岳瀆經》符矣。
claims.locator: Taiping Guangji (太平廣記), juan 467, bagian Li Tang (李湯), mengutip Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經)

statement.id: Teks menyimpulkan bahwa apa yang dilihat Li Tang (李湯) cocok dengan penuturan Yang Heng (楊衡) dan dengan Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經).
statement.en: The text concludes that what Li Tang (李湯) saw matches Yang Heng's (楊衡) account and the Yue Du Jing (岳瀆經).

short_description.id: Xelhua adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Aztek yang selamat dari air bah dan, menurut legenda, membangun Piramida Besar Cholula. Sebagian peneliti menilainya tokoh sejarah Nonoalca bertubuh normal, bukan pembangun piramida itu.
short_description.en: Xelhua is a giant of Aztec mythology who escaped the flood and, according to legend, built the Great Pyramid of Cholula. Some scholars see him instead as a normal-sized Nonoalca figure who did not build the pyramid.

long_description.id: Xelhua adalah salah satu dari tujuh raksasa dalam mitologi Aztek yang lolos dari air bah dengan mendaki gunung Tlaloc, lalu membangun Piramida Besar Cholula. Ia salah satu dari enam putra raksasa Mixcoatl, dan disebut sebagai putra sulung, raksasa yang mendirikan kota-kota Itzocan, Epatlan, dan Cuauquechollan. Sumber lain menyebut nama Xelhua, Xelhuan, atau Xelua, putra Ilancueitl, dan menyatakan bahwa ia mungkin mendaki Gunung Tlaloc untuk lolos dari banjir sementara sebagian orang menganggapnya pengatur pembangunan piramida di Cholula.
long_description.en: In Aztec mythology Xelhua ranks among seven giants who survived the deluge on Tlaloc's mountain and later raised the Great Pyramid of Cholula. He is one of the six giant sons of Mixcoatl, and is called the first-born, the giant who founded the cities of Itzocan, Epatlan and Cuauquechollan. Other sources give the name as Xelhua, Xelhuan or Xelua, son of Ilancueitl, and say he may have climbed Mount Tlaloc to escape a flood while some credit him with organizing the pyramid's construction in Cholula.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda pendirian Cholula pada sebuah plakat peringatan, pada masa air bah hanya tujuh bersaudara yang selamat di gua-gua gunung Tlalocan, sedangkan banyak raksasa tewas tenggelam. Códice Ríos menyebut bahwa pada zaman pertama ada raksasa di negeri itu yang disebut tzocuilicxe. Xelhua si raksasa pergi ke Cholollan dan mulai membangun piramida dengan bata besar dari Tlalmanalco untuk mengenang gunung yang menyelamatkannya. Tonacatecutli, bapa semua dewa, marah karena bangunan itu mengancam mencapai awan lalu menewaskan banyak pembangun dengan api langit dan batu berbentuk katak. Versi Códice Ríos menyebut kapten Xelua membangun menara agar dapat menyelamatkan diri bila air bah datang lagi, lalu petir merusaknya.
long_description.en: In the founding legend on a commemorative plaque, only seven brothers were saved in the caves of the mountain of Tlalocan at the time of the flood, while many giants perished submerged. The Códice Ríos says that in the first age there were giants in that land, called tzocuilicxe. Xelhua the giant went to Cholollan and began building the pyramid with great adobes from Tlalmanalco in memory of the mountain that saved him. Tonacatecutli, father of all the gods, angered that the work threatened to reach the clouds, killed many builders with celestial fire and a toad-shaped stone. The Códice Ríos version says the captain Xelua built a tower to escape in if the flood came again, and lightning destroyed it.

long_description.id: Penulis sebuah artikel akademik menilai Xelhuan sebenarnya salah satu dari empat penguasa Nonoalca yang bermigrasi dari Tula ke Lembah Puebla pada awal abad ke-12. Menurut penulis itu, tidak ada sumber yang menyebut Xelhuan berhenti di Cholula selain Códice Vaticano A, dan ia bukan pembangun piramida yang sudah berabad-abad berdiri itu. Meski begitu, di lingkungan Cholula masih ada cerita tentang tulang raksasa yang terus bermunculan.
long_description.en: The author of an academic article judges that Xelhuan was in fact one of four Nonoalca rulers who migrated from Tula to the Puebla Valley in the early twelfth century. According to the author, no source says Xelhuan stopped in Cholula other than the Códice Vaticano A, and he was not the builder of a pyramid that had already stood for centuries. Even so, neighborhoods of Cholula still tell of giants' bones that keep appearing.

cultural_context.id: Menurut penulis artikel, tradisi lisan lingkungan Cholula masih menyebut kapten dan raksasa kuno sebagai pendiri kota, dan ada beberapa versi tentang tulang raksasa yang terus bermunculan.
cultural_context.en: According to the article's author, oral traditions of Cholula's neighborhoods still credit an ancient captain and giants with founding the city, and there are several versions about giants' bones that keep appearing.

who.id: Xelhua adalah raksasa Aztek, salah satu dari tujuh raksasa yang lolos dari air bah.
who.en: Xelhua is an Aztec giant, one of the seven giants who escaped the flood.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari mitologi Aztek dan kisah asal-usul Nahua, tokoh putra Mixcoatl atau Ilancueitl menurut sumber berbeda.
origin.en: He comes from Aztec mythology and Nahua origin stories, a son of Mixcoatl or Ilancueitl according to different sources.

role.id: Dalam legenda ia raksasa pembangun yang memulai piramida di Cholula untuk mengenang gunung penyelamatnya.
role.en: In legend he is the giant builder who began the pyramid at Cholula in memory of the mountain that saved him.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal sebagai pembangun Piramida Besar Cholula menurut legenda.
famous_for.en: He is known as the builder of the Great Pyramid of Cholula according to legend.

did_you_know.id: Menurut kutipan Códice Ríos, menara di Cholula itu dibangun agar penghuninya dapat selamat bila air bah datang lagi.
did_you_know.en: According to the Códice Ríos passage, the tower at Cholula was built so that one could escape in it if the flood came again.

role.id: Raksasa yang selamat dari air bah dan memulai pembangunan piramida.
role.en: The giant who survived the flood and began building the pyramid.

summary.id: Setelah selamat dari air bah di gua-gua gunung Tlalocan, Xelhua membangun piramida di Cholollan dengan bata besar yang dioper dari tangan ke tangan. Tonacatecutli marah karena bangunan mengancam mencapai awan, lalu menewaskan banyak pembangun; versi Códice Ríos menyebut petir yang menghancurkan menara itu.
summary.en: After surviving the flood in the caves of the mountain of Tlalocan, Xelhua built the pyramid at Cholollan with great adobes passed from hand to hand. Tonacatecutli, angered that it threatened to reach the clouds, killed many builders; the Códice Ríos version has lightning destroy the tower.

description.en: The pyramid said in legend to have been built by Xelhua; an academic article judges its ceremonial center had stood for many centuries before the Nonoalcas arrived.

description.id: Tempat tujuh bersaudara selamat di gua-guanya dari air bah menurut legenda.
description.en: Where, in the legend, seven brothers were saved from the flood in its caves.

statement.en: The passage quoted in the article says that in the first age there were giants in this country, whom they called tzocuilicxe.

claims.quote: solo siete hermanos se salvaron en las grutas de la montaña del Tlalocan.

statement.id: Menurut legenda itu, hanya tujuh bersaudara yang selamat di gua-gua gunung Tlalocan.
statement.en: According to the legend, only seven brothers were saved in the caves of the mountain of Tlalocan.

claims.quote: Xelhua, el gigante, fue al sitio que después se le llamó Cholollan y con grandes adobes fabricados en Tlalmanalco y conducidos de mano en mano por una fila de hombres

statement.id: Menurut legenda pendirian pada sebuah plakat peringatan, Xelhua si raksasa pergi ke tempat yang kemudian disebut Cholollan, dengan bata besar buatan Tlalmanalco yang dioper dari tangan ke tangan oleh barisan orang.
statement.en: According to the founding legend on a commemorative plaque, Xelhua the giant went to the place later called Cholollan, with great adobes made in Tlalmanalco and passed from hand to hand by a line of men.

claims.quote: comenzó a construir la pirámide en memoria de la montaña en que fue salvado. Irritado Tonacatecutli, padre de todos los dioses, que la obra amenazaba con llegar a las nubes lanzó al fuego celeste y con una piedra en forma de sapo mató a muchos de los constructores

statement.id: Menurut legenda itu, ia mulai membangun piramida untuk mengenang gunung tempat ia diselamatkan; Tonacatecutli, bapa semua dewa, marah karena bangunan itu mengancam mencapai awan, lalu melemparkan api langit dan batu berbentuk katak yang menewaskan banyak pembangun.
statement.en: According to the legend, he began building the pyramid in memory of the mountain where he was saved; Tonacatecutli, father of all the gods, angered that the work threatened to reach the clouds, hurled celestial fire and a toad-shaped stone that killed many of the builders.

claims.quote: en la época del diluvio moraban sobre la tierra los gigantes, muchos perecieron sumergidos en las aguas

statement.id: Menurut legenda itu, pada masa air bah raksasa-raksasa tinggal di bumi dan banyak yang tewas tenggelam.
statement.en: According to the legend, giants dwelt on the earth in the time of the flood and many perished submerged in the waters.

claims.quote: Uno de aquellos siete, que dicen haber escapado del diluvio, dicen que multiplicándose [...] se fue a Cholula y ahí comenzó edificar una torre que es aquella de la cual ahora aparece la base de ladrillos. El nombre de este capitán era Xelua. La edificaba para, en caso de venir el diluvio otra vez, poder escapar en ella.

statement.id: Menurut kutipan yang dimuat artikel itu, salah satu dari tujuh orang yang konon lolos dari air bah pergi ke Cholula dan mulai membangun sebuah menara; nama kapten itu Xelua, dan ia membangunnya agar dapat menyelamatkan diri bila air bah datang lagi.
statement.en: According to the passage quoted in the article, one of the seven said to have escaped the flood went to Cholula and began building a tower; the captain's name was Xelua, and he built it to escape in it if the flood came again.

claims.quote: Y estando ya en gran altura, cayó del cielo un rayo y la destruyó matando mucha gente.

statement.id: Menurut kutipan itu, ketika menara sudah sangat tinggi, petir jatuh dari langit, merusaknya, dan menewaskan banyak orang.
statement.en: According to the passage, when the tower had reached a great height a lightning bolt fell from the sky and destroyed it, killing many people.

claims.quote: Este de su mujer llamada Ilancueitl hobo seis hijos. El primero llamaron Gelhua [...] o Xelua [...] este pobló a Cuauhquechulan (Huaquechula) y a Itzucan (Izúcar), Tzepatlan (Epatlán), Teopantlan

statement.id: Menurut kutipan dari sebuah kronik awal, Ilancueitl memiliki enam anak; yang pertama bernama Gelhua atau Xelua, yang mendirikan permukiman di Cuauhquechulan (Huaquechula), Itzucan (Izúcar), Tzepatlan (Epatlán), dan Teopantlan.
statement.en: According to the passage from an early chronicle, Ilancueitl had six sons; the first was called Gelhua or Xelua, who settled Cuauhquechulan (Huaquechula), Itzucan (Izúcar), Tzepatlan (Epatlán) and Teopantlan.

claims.quote: Xelhuan es uno entre los cuatro gobernantes nonoalcas (Ueuetzin, Quauhtzin, Citlalmacuetzin son los otros), que emigraron desde Tula hacia el Valle de Puebla a principios del siglo XII.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, Xelhuan adalah salah satu dari empat penguasa Nonoalca yang bermigrasi dari Tula ke Lembah Puebla pada awal abad ke-12.
statement.en: According to the article, Xelhuan is one of four Nonoalca rulers who migrated from Tula to the Puebla Valley in the early twelfth century.

claims.quote: en un año 1 tecpal, es decir, en 1116, Xelhua emigra con su pueblo

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, pada tahun 1 tecpal, yaitu 1116, Xelhua bermigrasi bersama rakyatnya.
statement.en: According to the article, in the year 1 tecpal, that is 1116, Xelhua migrates with his people.

claims.quote: según lo anotó Kirchhoff, ninguna fuente menciona que Xelhuan se detuvo en Cholula salvo el Códice Vaticano A, que lo ubica como constructor de la pirámide en Cholula en la improbable fecha de 1194.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, tidak ada sumber yang menyebut Xelhuan berhenti di Cholula kecuali Códice Vaticano A, yang menempatkannya sebagai pembangun piramida di Cholula pada tahun 1194 yang dinilai tidak mungkin.
statement.en: According to the article, no source says Xelhuan stopped in Cholula except the Códice Vaticano A, which places him as builder of the pyramid in Cholula in the "improbable" year 1194.

claims.quote: Xelhuan no fue, entonces, un “capitán”, como narra la leyenda de Veytia en la placa “conmemorativa de su fundación” en Cholula, siguiendo el Códice Ríos; menos aún el constructor de la pirámide cholulteca

statement.id: Menurut penulis artikel, Xelhuan bukan seorang "kapten" seperti dikisahkan legenda Veytia pada plakat itu, apalagi pembangun piramida Cholula.

short_description.id: Xiangliu adalah monster ular berbisa berkepala sembilan yang membawa banjir dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Xiangliu is a venomous nine-headed serpent monster bringing floods in Chinese mythology.

long_description.id: Xiangliu adalah monster ular berbisa berkepala sembilan yang membawa banjir dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Dalam Shanhaijing, ia dikenal sebagai Xiangyao.
long_description.en: Xiangliu is a venomous nine-headed serpent monster bringing floods in Chinese mythology. In the Shanhaijing, it is known as Xiangyao.

long_description.id: Cetakan kayu lama menempatkan kepala-kepalanya mengelompok pada satu leher. Shanhaijing menyebut Xiangliu sebagai bawahan dewa air Gonggong. Tempat yang disentuh atau diembusnya menjadi rawa berair pahit beracun. Penafsiran yang dikutip Eberhard membandingkan Xiangliu dengan belut dalam kisah banjir.
long_description.en: Older woodcuts cluster its heads on a single neck. The Shanhaijing describes Xiangliu as a subordinate of the water deity Gonggong. Places it touches or breathes upon become bogs of poisonous bitter water. An interpretation quoted by Eberhard compares Xiangliu with an eel in flood tales.

long_description.id: Shanhaijing bagian Haiwai bei jing menyebut Xiangliu sebagai menteri Gonggong yang berkepala sembilan dan makan di sembilan gunung. Tempat yang dijangkaunya menjadi rawa, dan Yu membunuhnya; darahnya amis sehingga lima jenis biji-bijian tak dapat ditanam. Makhluk itu digambarkan berwajah manusia dan bertubuh ular berwarna biru.
long_description.en: The Haiwai bei jing section of the Shanhaijing calls Xiangliu a minister of Gonggong with nine heads that eats from nine mountains. Where it reaches become marshes, and Yu killed it; its blood was foul, so the five grains could not be planted. It is described with human faces and a blue snake body.

long_description.id: Bagian Dahuang bei jing menamai menteri Gonggong yang serupa sebagai Xiangyao, berkepala sembilan dan bertubuh ular yang melingkar sendiri. Tempat yang dikenainya menjadi mata air dan rawa berair pahit, dan tak ada binatang yang dapat tinggal di sana. Yu membendung banjir dan membunuhnya, namun darahnya membuat tanah tak dapat menumbuhkan biji-bijian.
long_description.en: The Dahuang bei jing section names a similar minister of Gonggong Xiangyao, with nine heads and a snake body that coils itself. The places it touched became springs and marshes of bitter water, and no beast could live there. Yu dammed the floods and killed it, but its blood left the land unable to grow grain.

statement.id: Shanhaijing (山海經), Haiwai bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong (共工) bernama Xiangliu (相柳氏) berkepala sembilan (九首) yang makan di sembilan gunung; tempat yang dijangkaunya (所抵) menjadi rawa dan lembah berair (澤谿); Yu (禹) membunuhnya dan darahnya berbau amis sehingga lima jenis biji-bijian tidak dapat ditanam di sana.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing (山海經), Haiwai bei jing, says Gonggong's (共工) minister is named Xiangliu (相柳氏), has nine heads (九首) and eats from nine mountains; where it reaches (所抵) there become marshes and watery valleys (澤谿); Yu (禹) killed it and its blood was foul, so the five grains could not be planted there.

claims.quote: 相柳者，九首人面，蛇身而青。不敢北射，畏共工之臺。臺在其東，臺四方，隅有一蛇，虎色，首衝南方。

statement.id: Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, menggambarkan Xiangliu sebagai makhluk berkepala sembilan dan berwajah manusia (九首人面), bertubuh ular berwarna biru (蛇身而青); teks menambahkan frasa "tidak berani memanah ke utara" (不敢北射) karena segan pada menara Gonggong (共工之臺); menara itu persegi empat dan di sudutnya ada seekor ular berwarna harimau yang kepalanya menghadap ke selatan.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, describes Xiangliu as nine-headed with human faces (九首人面) and a blue snake body (蛇身而青); the text adds the phrase "dares not shoot northward" (不敢北射), in awe of Gonggong's terrace (共工之臺); the terrace is square and at a corner there is a tiger-coloured snake whose head faces south.

claims.quote: 共工臣名曰相繇，九首蛇身，自環，食于九土。其所歍所尼，即為源澤，不辛乃苦，百獸莫能處。禹湮洪水，殺相繇，其血腥臭，不可生榖；其地多水，不可居也。

statement.id: Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong bernama Xiangyao (相繇) berkepala sembilan dan bertubuh ular, melingkar sendiri (自環) dan makan di sembilan negeri (九土); tempat yang dikenainya menjadi mata air dan rawa yang rasanya pahit (不辛乃苦) sehingga tak satu pun binatang dapat tinggal di sana. Yu membendung banjir dan membunuhnya; darahnya amis dan busuk, biji-bijian tak dapat tumbuh, dan tanahnya terlalu berair untuk dihuni.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, names a minister of Gonggong as Xiangyao (相繇), with nine heads and a snake body, coiling itself (自環) and eating from nine lands (九土); where it passes the places become springs and marshes whose water is bitter (不辛乃苦), so no beast can live there. Yu dammed the floods and killed it; its blood was rank, grain could not grow, and the land was too watery to inhabit.

short_description.id: Xiao adalah nama yang digunakan untuk beberapa makhluk Tiongkok, termasuk kera berlengan panjang dan burung bersayap empat.
short_description.en: Xiao is a name used for several Chinese creatures, including a long armed ape and a four winged bird.

long_description.id: Xiao adalah nama yang digunakan untuk beberapa makhluk Tiongkok, termasuk kera berlengan panjang dan burung bersayap empat. Kata xiao mencakup makna gaduh atau bising.
long_description.en: Xiao is a name used for several Chinese creatures, including a long armed ape and a four winged bird. The word xiao includes meanings of noise and clamor.

long_description.id: Shan Hai Jing memakai nama Xiao untuk sungai, gunung, dan dua makhluk mitos. Salah satu Xiao menyerupai kera, berlengan panjang, dan mahir melempar benda. Xiao lain digambarkan sebagai burung dengan empat sayap, satu mata, dan ekor anjing. Komentar Guo Pu menyebut varian Jufu pada bagian yang membandingkan burung Xiao dengan Kuafu.
long_description.en: The Shan Hai Jing uses Xiao as a name for a river, a mountain, and two mythical creatures. One Xiao resembles an ape, has long arms, and is skilled at throwing things. Another Xiao is described as a bird with four wings, one eye, and a dog's tail. Guo Pu's commentary records the variant Jufu in the passage comparing the Xiao bird with Kuafu.

long_description.id: Teks primer Shanhaijing memperlihatkan kedua makhluk itu. Di bagian Barat, binatang bernama 嚻 berbentuk seperti kera berlengan panjang dan pandai melempar; catatan menyebutnya ada dalam lukisan binatang menakutkan. Di bagian Utara, burung bernama 嚻 berwujud empat sayap, satu mata, dan ekor anjing, bersuara seperti magpie, dan memakannya dikatakan menyembuhkan sakit perut.
long_description.en: The primary text of the Shanhaijing shows both creatures. In the Western section, the beast named 嚻 is shaped like a long-armed ape and good at throwing; an annotation says it appears in paintings of dreaded beasts. In the Northern section, the bird named 嚻 has four wings, one eye and a dog's tail, cries like a magpie, and eating it is said to cure bellyache.

claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, the xiao is the name of several creatures, including the xiao (Chinese: 囂; pinyin: xiāo; Wade–Giles: hsiao1) "a long-armed ape" or "a four-winged bird" and shanxiao (Chinese: 山魈; pinyin: shānxiāo) "mischievous, one-legged mountain spirit". Furthermore, some Western sources misspell and misconstrue the older romanization hsiao as "hsigo" [sic] "a flying monkey".

text.id: Motif penting terutama pada era pra-Kolumbus; tampil dalam kodeks Mixtec Pascaklasik.
text.en: An important motif especially in the pre-Columbian era; appears in Postclassic Mixtec codices.

short_description.id: Yahui adalah sosok gaib berwujud campuran hewan dan manusia dalam budaya Mixtec, motif penting dalam ikonografi kodeks pra-Kolumbus.
short_description.en: The yahui is a supernatural figure of mixed animal and human forms in Mixtec culture, an important motif of pre-Columbian codex iconography.

long_description.id: Yahui adalah sosok gaib yang mengambil berbagai campuran wujud hewan dan manusia dalam budaya dan sistem kepercayaan Mixtec. Ia merupakan motif penting yang berulang dalam ikonografi dan pemikiran Mixtec, terutama pada masa pra-Kolumbus. Dalam kodeks Mixtec Pascaklasik ia tampil mengenakan ekor dan hiasan kepala ular atau reptil serta cangkang kura-kura, dan sosoknya muncul dalam beberapa kodeks termasuk Codex Zouche-Nuttall, Vindobonensis Mexicanus I, Selden, Bodley, Egerton, dan Becker I/II.
long_description.en: The yahui is a supernatural being shown in many blends of animal and human shape within Mixtec culture and belief. It is a significant, often repeated motif of Mixtec iconography and thought, above all in the pre-Columbian era. In Postclassic Mixtec codices it appears wearing a serpent or reptilian tail and headdress and the carapace of a turtle, and its figures occur in several codices including the Zouche-Nuttall, Vindobonensis Mexicanus I, Selden, Bodley, Egerton and Becker I/II.

long_description.id: Yahui tampil dalam dua bentuk utama: nahual, sosok gabungan manusia dan hewan, dan sosok hewan. Pada wujud hewan, kepala reptil digabung dengan tubuh bercangkang kura-kura, lengan dan kaki reptil, cakar, dan motif api-batu api pada ujung ekor dan hidung; yahui hewan muncul dalam adegan kosmogoni tentang asal-usul ritual. Pada wujud nahual, citra hewan dipadukan dengan kepala manusia laki-laki, dan sosok nahual kadang memegang pisau kurban serta melakukan ritus kurban atau kegiatan upacara lain.
long_description.en: The yahui appears in two main forms: the nahual, a man-animal composite figure, and the animal figure. In its animal form a reptile's head sits on a tortoise-shell body with reptilian limbs and claws, and the flint-fire motif marks the tail and nose tips; the animal yahui turns up in scenes of cosmic origins that explain the beginnings of ritual. In nahual form the animal imagery is combined with a male human head, and nahual figures at times hold sacrificial knives and perform sacrificial rites or other ceremonial activities.

long_description.id: Beberapa citra yahui juga ditemukan di luar kodeks, salah satunya di sebuah makam Zapotek di Zaachila. Sebagai tokoh sejarah nyata, yahui kemungkinan melakukan ritus kosmologis di gua dan di puncak bukit. Mary Elizabeth Smith menyebutnya "xiuhcoatl-kura-kura-pelaku kurban". Dalam uraian Pohl atas Codex Selden, seorang imam ular api yang disebut yahui tampil bersama jaguar, coyote, dan elang, dan bersama seekor elang mempersembahkan jantung manusia kepada Dewa Matahari di depan Kuil Jaltepec.
long_description.en: The yahui is also depicted outside the codices, in one case in a Zapotec tomb at Zaachila. Taken as a real historical figure, the yahui probably carried out cosmological rites in caves and on hilltops. Mary Elizabeth Smith called it the "xiuhcoatl-turtle-sacrificer". In Pohl's description of the Codex Selden, a fire-serpent priest called a yahui appears with a jaguar, a coyote and an eagle, and with an eagle delivers human hearts to the Sun God before the Temple of Jaltepec.

short_description.id: Yumboes adalah makhluk gaib mirip peri dalam kepercayaan orang Jaloff (Wolof) di seberang Pulau Goree, digambarkan setinggi sekitar dua kaki, berwarna putih, dan disebut Bakhna Rakhna atau orang baik.
short_description.en: Yumboes are fairy-like supernatural beings of Jaloff (Wolof) belief on the mainland opposite Goree, pictured as about two feet tall and white, and called Bakhna Rakhna, the Good People.

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah kumpulan mitologi peri, orang Jaloff di daratan seberang Pulau Goree percaya pada makhluk yang sangat mirip peri Gotik. Mereka menyebutnya Yumboes, tingginya sekitar dua kaki, dan berwarna putih seperti semua hal gaib menurut kepercayaan setempat. Yumboes juga dijuluki Bakhna Rakhna, yang berarti orang baik, dan kadang dikatakan berambut perak.
long_description.en: A collection of fairy lore reports that the Jaloff living on the mainland across from Goree believe in beings strikingly like the Gothic fairies. They name them Yumboes, about two feet tall and white, as all supernatural things are held to be there. The Yumboes are also called Bakhna Rakhna, meaning good people, and are sometimes given silver hair.

long_description.id: Yumboes dianggap roh orang mati, dan orang Moor menganggapnya jiwa sahabat yang telah wafat. Mereka melekat pada keluarga tertentu, meratapi anggota keluarga yang meninggal, dan menari di atas kuburnya. Pakaian dan tingkah laku mereka meniru penduduk setempat.
long_description.en: The Yumboes are regarded as spirits of the dead, and the Moors take them for the souls of departed friends. They attach themselves to certain families, mourn any member who dies and dance on the grave. Their clothing and behaviour copy those of the local people.

long_description.id: Kediaman utama Yumboes adalah hunian bawah tanah di Paps, perbukitan sekitar tiga mil dari pantai. Tamu yang diterima di sana bercerita tentang meja penuh hidangan yang ditata dan diangkat oleh tangan dan kaki tanpa tubuh. Pada malam hari Yumboes terlihat menangkap ikan dengan kano, mencuri tepung coos-coos dari lesung para perempuan, dan setelah mabuk tuak sawit menabuh genderang Jaloff di perbukitan.
long_description.en: The Yumboes chiefly live in an underground home on the Paps, hills some three miles inland. Guests received there told of tables of food set and cleared by hands and feet with no visible bodies. At night the Yumboes are seen fishing from canoes, stealing coos-coos meal from the women's mortars and, once drunk on palm-wine, drumming on the hills.

long_description.id: Satu-satunya sumber yang diketahui untuk legenda yumboes adalah buku Thomas Keightley, yang memperoleh kisahnya dari seorang perempuan yang semasa kecil tinggal di Pulau Goree dan mendengarnya dari pelayan Wolof. Yumboes juga dibandingkan dengan arwah leluhur yang dikenal di banyak negara Afrika.
long_description.en: The only known source for yumboe lore is Thomas Keightley's book, which drew on a woman who had lived on Goree Island as a child and heard the tales from a Wolof maid. Yumboes have also been likened to the ancestral ghosts known in many African countries.

statement.id: Mereka melekat pada keluarga tertentu; bila anggota keluarga itu meninggal, Yumboes terdengar meratapinya dan menari di atas kuburnya (graves).
statement.en: They attach themselves to particular families; when a member dies, the Yumboes are heard lamenting and dancing on the graves.

claims.quote: The Moors believe the Yumboes to be the souls of their deceased friends.

statement.id: Orang Moor (Moors) percaya Yumboes adalah jiwa sahabat mereka yang telah meninggal.
statement.en: The Moors believe the Yumboes are the souls of their deceased friends.

claims.quote: The chief abode of the Yumboes is a subterraneous dwelling on the Paps, the hills about three miles distant from the coast.

statement.id: Tempat tinggal utama Yumboes adalah hunian bawah tanah di Paps, perbukitan (hills) sekitar tiga mil (three miles) dari pantai.
statement.en: The Yumboes' chief abode is an underground dwelling on the Paps, hills about three miles from the coast.

claims.quote: how nothing but hands and feet were to be seen, which laid and removed the various dishes

statement.id: Di sana yang terlihat hanya tangan dan kaki (hands and feet) yang menata dan mengangkat hidangan.
statement.en: There nothing but hands and feet could be seen, laying and removing the dishes.

claims.quote: They steal to the huts, where the women are pounding in mortars the coos-coos, or corn,

statement.id: Mereka mengendap ke gubuk tempat para perempuan menumbuk coos-coos atau jagung (corn) di lesung.
statement.en: They creep to the huts where the women are pounding coos-coos, or corn, in mortars.

claims.quote: They are also seen at night in their canoes, out fishing in the bay.

statement.id: Mereka juga terlihat pada malam hari (at night) di kano, menangkap ikan di teluk.
statement.en: They are also seen at night in their canoes, fishing in the bay.

claims.quote: They bury palm-wine, and when it becomes sour they drink of it till it intoxicates them, and then make a great noise, beating Jaloff drums on the hills.

statement.id: Mereka mengubur tuak sawit (palm-wine), meminumnya setelah masam sampai mabuk, lalu membuat keributan dengan menabuh genderang Jaloff di perbukitan.
statement.en: They bury palm-wine, drink it when sour until drunk, and then make a great noise beating Jaloff drums on the hills.

claims.quote: Innde maɓɓe nde ɓe kuutortoo nde Bakhna Rakhna firti ko yimɓe moƴƴuɓe.

statement.id: Nama yang mereka pakai, Bakhna Rakhna, berarti orang-orang baik (yimɓe moƴƴuɓe).
statement.en: Their name Bakhna Rakhna means good people (yimɓe moƴƴuɓe).

short_description.id: Aim adalah roh ke-23 dalam Goetia, adipati agung berkepala tiga yang menunggang ular beludak dan membawa obor menyala.
short_description.en: Aim is the twenty-third spirit in the Goetia, a great duke with three heads who rides a viper and carries a burning firebrand.

long_description.id: Aim adalah roh ke-23 dalam Goetia, sebuah teks demonologi. Teks itu menyebutnya adipati agung yang kuat, tampil sebagai pria berbadan sangat tampan dengan tiga kepala.
long_description.en: Aim is the twenty-third spirit in the Goetia, a demonological text. The text calls him a great and strong duke, appearing as a very handsome man in body with three heads.

long_description.id: Kepala pertama seperti ular, yang kedua seperti manusia dengan dua bintang di dahi, dan yang ketiga seperti kucing. Ia menunggang ular beludak sambil membawa obor menyala, yang dipakainya untuk membakar kota, kastil, dan tempat-tempat besar.
long_description.en: The first head is like a serpent, the second like a man with two stars on his forehead, and the third like a cat. He rides a viper carrying a burning firebrand, with which he sets cities, castles and great places on fire.

long_description.id: Goetia menyebut Aim membuat orang cerdik dalam segala hal, memberi jawaban benar tentang hal-hal tersembunyi, dan memimpin 26 legiun roh. Namanya juga tertulis Aym, Haborym, atau Haborim, dan Fred Gettings menduga asalnya dari mitologi Mesir dengan kaitan pada Bastet.
long_description.en: The Goetia says Aim makes one witty in all manner of ways, gives true answers to private matters, and governs 26 legions of spirits. His name is also written Aym, Haborym or Haborim, and Fred Gettings conjectures an Egyptian-mythology origin with a link to Bastet.

short_description.id: Amalanhig adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Visayas, aswang yang gagal mewariskan sifat monsternya sehingga bangkit dari kubur untuk membunuh manusia dengan menggigit leher.
short_description.en: The amalanhig is a being of Visayan mythology, an aswang that failed to transfer its monstrosity and so rises from the grave to kill humans by biting their necks.

long_description.id: Amalanhig, juga disebut maranhig atau amaranhig, adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Visayas, terutama di kalangan penutur Hiligaynon. Mereka adalah aswang yang gagal mewariskan sifat monsternya, sehingga bangkit dari kubur dan membunuh manusia dengan menggigit leher.
long_description.en: The amalanhig, also called maranhig or amaranhig, is a being of Visayan mythology, particularly among Hiligaynon speakers. They are aswangs that failed to transfer their monstrosity, so they rise from their graves and kill humans by biting their necks.

long_description.id: Amalanhig digambarkan tampak sama dengan manusia, meski pada kebanyakan individu taring atas membesar, dan merupakan varian vampir asli Filipina. Seorang penulis menyebut maranhig sebagai versi asli Filipina dari mayat hidup: lebih mirip zombi daripada aswang, dengan kehadiran yang ditandai bau busuk daging membusuk. Ciri fisik bal-bal juga disebut diadopsi ke kisah amalanhig.
long_description.en: The amalanhig are depicted as looking identical to humans, though most have enlarged upper canines, and are a variant of the vampire native to the Philippines. One writer calls the maranhig the native Philippine version of the undead: more zombie than aswang, its presence announced by the stench of rotting flesh. The physical attributes of the bal-bal are also said to have been adopted into tales of the amalanhig.

long_description.id: Penulis yang sama mengingatkan bahwa cerita penampakan maranhig biasanya jarang dapat diandalkan; ayahnya hanya mendengar tentangnya sejak kecil, sedangkan seorang mantan tentara mengaku melihat sekelompok maranhig berjalan berbaris di Mindanao, telanjang dengan daging membusuk bergelantungan dari tulang. Ia juga mencatat bahwa deskripsi daring tentang amaranhig didasarkan pada daftar makhluk mitos dalam Pedro Penduko, dan dalam daftar televisi itu korban dapat lolos dengan berlari zigzag, memanjat tempat tinggi, atau masuk ke perairan dalam.
long_description.en: The same writer warns that stories of maranhig sightings are rarely reliable; his father only heard of it as a child, while a former soldier claims to have seen a group of maranhig walking in a line in Mindanao, naked with rotting flesh hanging from their bones. He also notes that the online description of the amaranhig was based on a list of mythical creatures in Pedro Penduko, and in that television list victims can escape by zigzag running, climbing to a high place or running into deep water.

long_description.id: Sebuah artikel jurnal mencatat maranhig (ejaan sumber: Hiliganynon) sebagai satu jenis aswang yang kerap diterjemahkan menjadi bruja oleh para kronikus Spanyol dan menjadi "penyihir" oleh sarjana folklor yang menulis dalam bahasa Inggris; penyihir semacam itu dapat laki-laki atau perempuan dan dapat berwujud burung, babi hutan, atau anjing besar. Gambaran ini berbeda dari gambaran mayat hidup di atas.
long_description.en: A journal article records the maranhig (Hiliganynon in the source) as one type of aswang that Spanish chroniclers and folklore scholars writing in English render as bruja and "witch" respectively; such witches may be male or female and can take the form of birds, wild pigs or large dogs. This differs from the undead picture above.

claims.quote: According to Wikipedia, the Amaranhig is an aswang who has “failed to transfer their monstrosity causing them to rise from their graves to kill humans by biting their necks.” The description was based on a list of mythical creatures as depicted in “Pedro Penduko,” a popular Philippines comic book superhero which had been portrayed many times in TV and cinema.

statement.id: Menurut penulis, deskripsi Wikipedia tentang amaranhig didasarkan pada daftar makhluk mitos sebagaimana digambarkan dalam "Pedro Penduko", pahlawan super komik populer Filipina yang berkali-kali tampil di TV dan bioskop.
statement.en: According to the writer, Wikipedia's description of the amaranhig was based on a list of mythical creatures as depicted in "Pedro Penduko", a popular Philippine comic-book superhero portrayed many times on TV and in cinema.

claims.quote: Usual stories about Maranhig sightings usually fall under the “my-uncle’s-cousin’s-grandpa saw it” category and are rarely reliable and informative.

statement.id: Menurut penulis, cerita penampakan maranhig biasanya tergolong cerita "pamanku-sepupu-kakeknya melihatnya" dan jarang dapat diandalkan atau informatif.
statement.en: According to the writer, stories of Maranhig sightings usually fall into the "my uncle's cousin's grandpa saw it" category and are rarely reliable or informative.

claims.quote: My father described hearing about it as a child growing up in his home province but he never mentioned seeing anything that remotely fits the description above and otherwise. He says based on accounts of people who allegedly “saw” it.

statement.id: Penulis menuturkan bahwa ayahnya mendengar tentang maranhig sejak kecil di provinsi asalnya, tetapi tidak pernah menyebut melihat sesuatu yang cocok dengan deskripsi itu; ia berbicara berdasarkan cerita orang yang konon pernah "melihatnya".
statement.en: The writer says his father heard about it as a child in his home province but never mentioned seeing anything that fits the description; he speaks from accounts of people who allegedly "saw" it.

claims.quote: They are more zombie than aswang – undead corpses whose presence is announced by the overpowering stench of decaying flesh.

statement.id: Menurut penuturan itu, maranhig lebih mirip zombi daripada aswang: mayat hidup yang kehadirannya ditandai bau busuk daging membusuk yang menyengat.
statement.en: According to that account the maranhig are more zombie than aswang: undead corpses whose presence is announced by the overpowering stench of decaying flesh.

claims.quote: that they saw a group of Maranhigs on one of their Mindanao sorties. He said the way these things walk were somehow similar to the way zombies are portrayed in the movies.

statement.id: Seorang mantan tentara menuturkan kepada penulis bahwa ia dan rekannya melihat sekelompok maranhig dalam salah satu operasi di Mindanao, dan cara mereka berjalan mirip zombi di film.
statement.en: A former soldier told the writer that his unit saw a group of maranhig on one of their Mindanao sorties and that the way they walked resembled zombies in the movies.

claims.quote: Based on his description, the Maranhigs were walking quietly in a line. They were naked but rotting flesh and skin hung from their bones like old curtains.

statement.id: Menurut gambaran tentara itu, para maranhig berjalan diam-diam berbaris, telanjang, dengan daging dan kulit membusuk bergelantungan dari tulang seperti tirai tua.
statement.en: By the soldier's description the maranhig walked quietly in a line, naked, with rotting flesh and skin hanging from their bones like old curtains.

claims.quote: The physical attributes of the Bal-Bal have been adopted into many other tales of flesh eating creatures throughout the Philippines – such as the Visayan version of the Aswang, the Amalanhig, and the Busaw.

statement.id: Ciri fisik bal-bal telah diadopsi ke banyak kisah makhluk pemakan daging lain di Filipina, termasuk versi Visayas dari aswang, amalanhig, dan busaw.
statement.en: The physical attributes of the bal-bal have been adopted into many other tales of flesh-eating creatures in the Philippines, including the Visayan version of the aswang, the amalanhig and the busaw.

claims.quote: One type of aswang, called mangkukulam in Tagalog, maranhig in Hiliganynon, manggagamod in Ilokano, and barangan or ongo by Visayans, is often translated as bruja by Spanish chroniclers and as “witch” by folklore scholars writing in English.

statement.id: Artikel jurnal ini menyebut satu jenis aswang yang disebut maranhig dalam bahasa Hiliganynon (ejaan sumber), mangkukulam dalam bahasa Tagalog, dan nama lain di tempat lain, yang sering diterjemahkan sebagai bruja oleh para kronikus Spanyol dan sebagai "penyihir" oleh sarjana folklor berbahasa Inggris.
statement.en: This journal article names one type of aswang called maranhig in Hiliganynon, mangkukulam in Tagalog and other names elsewhere, often translated as bruja by Spanish chroniclers and as "witch" by folklore scholars writing in English.

claims.quote: Such witches may be male or female, and can take various forms, especially the guise of animals: birds, wild pigs or large dogs (called sigbin in Cebuano).

statement.en: According to the article such witches may be male or female and can take various forms, especially animals: birds, wild pigs or large dogs (called sigbin in Cebuano).

short_description.id: Ame no Wakahiko adalah dewa padi-padian (amatsukami) dalam mitologi Jepang yang diutus ke bumi, tidak melapor, dan mati terkena anak panah yang dilemparkan kembali.
short_description.en: Ame no Wakahiko is a god of grains (amatsukami) in Japanese mythology who is sent to earth, fails to report, and dies from an arrow thrown back at him.

long_description.id: Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 atau 天若日子) adalah dewa padi-padian dan amatsukami dalam mitologi Jepang, putra Amatsukunitama. Namanya berarti "anak muda di surga", dan ia dianggap pemuda yang sangat tampan. Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menambahkan bahwa "Wakahiko" berarti pemuda dan menyebut teori bahwa nama ini kata benda umum, sehingga tanpa gelar kehormatan seperti 神, 命, atau 尊.
long_description.en: Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 or 天若日子), son of Amatsukunitama, is counted in Japanese mythology as a grain god and an amatsukami. His name is explained as "a young boy in heaven", and he is believed to have been a remarkably good-looking youth. Japanese Wikipedia adds that "Wakahiko" means a young man and notes a theory that it is a common noun, which would explain the lack of an honorific such as 神, 命 or 尊.

long_description.id: Dalam banyak versi, ketika Ame no Hohi tidak mengirim kabar selama tiga tahun, para dewa memilih Ame no Wakahiko untuk menguasai bumi. Dalam sebagian versi ia jatuh cinta kepada Shitateruhime; delapan tahun kemudian burung Nakime dikirim menengoknya, tetapi ia memanah burung itu dan anak panahnya melesat ke surga. Takamimusubi melemparkannya kembali sehingga mengenai Ame no Wakahiko yang sedang tidur dan membunuhnya; versi lain menyebut Amaterasu yang melakukannya.
long_description.en: In many versions, when Ame no Hohi sent no word for three years, the gods chose Ame no Wakahiko to rule the earth. In some versions he fell in love with Shitateruhime; eight years later the bird Nakime was sent to check on him, but he shot the bird and the arrow flew to heaven. Takamimusubi threw it back so that it hit Ame no Wakahiko as he lay in bed and killed him; other versions say Amaterasu did this.

long_description.id: Setelah ia wafat, orang tuanya membangun gubuk duka. Ajisukitakahikone yang datang melayat disangka dirinya yang hidup kembali karena kemiripannya; tersinggung, ia menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya hingga jatuh di Mino dan menjadi Gunung Moyama. Mitos ini disebut sebagai asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali, dan mungkin juga mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaan atas negara tetangga.
long_description.en: After his death his parents built a mourning hut. Ajisukitakahikone, who came to pay respects, was mistaken for him brought back to life because of their resemblance; offended, he destroyed the hut and kicked it so that it landed in Mino and became Mount Moyama. This myth is named as the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow, and is likely also a mythicisation of the Yamato state's attempts to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

long_description.id: Ia dimuliakan di Kuil Abiko di Aishō, Shiga, dan Kuil Iwakura di Shinshiro, Aichi. Sebuah kisah Otogi-zōshi zaman Muromachi, Ame no Wakahiko sōshi, juga menampilkan pangeran bernama sama yang berwujud ular dan menjadi kisah asal-usul Tanabata.
long_description.en: Shrines that honor him include Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga, and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi. A Muromachi-period Otogi-zōshi story, Ame no Wakahiko sōshi, also features a prince of the same name who takes the form of a serpent and serves as an origin tale for Tanabata.

cultural_context.id: Mitos ini adalah asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali, dan kemungkinan juga mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaan atas negara-negara tetangga.
cultural_context.en: The myth is given as the source of a Japanese proverb about the returning arrow, and probably also a mythic retelling of Yamato's efforts to assert its authority over neighbouring states.

statement.en: Another story of Ame no Wakahiko appears in medieval Japanese literature of the Muromachi period (Otogi-zōshi), in a narrative very similar to tale type ATU 425, "The Search for the Lost Husband", or to the Graeco-Roman story of Cupid and Psyche by Apuleius.

claims.quote: The story is alternatively known as Ame no Wakahiko sōshi or Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (The Tale of Ame no Wakahiko), and serves as another etiological tale for the Tanabata festival.

statement.id: Kisah ini juga dikenal sebagai Ame no Wakahiko sōshi atau Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (Kisah Ame no Wakahiko), dan menjadi kisah asal-usul lain bagi festival Tanabata.
statement.en: The story is also known as Ame no Wakahiko sōshi or Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (The Tale of Ame no Wakahiko), and serves as another etiological tale for the Tanabata festival.

claims.quote: In this tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent.

statement.id: Dalam kisah ini, Pangeran Ame no Wakahiko menjelma menjadi ular.
statement.en: In this tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent.

claims.quote: At the end of this tale, the oni father  lets his son and the wife meet once a month, but she mistakes it for "once a year" and thus, the lovers can only reunite during the Tanabata.

statement.id: Di akhir kisah, ayah oni mengizinkan putranya dan sang istri bertemu sebulan sekali, tetapi sang istri salah mengira "setahun sekali", sehingga sepasang kekasih itu hanya bisa bersatu saat Tanabata.
statement.en: At the end of the tale the oni father lets his son and the wife meet once a month, but she mistakes it for "once a year", so the lovers can only reunite at Tanabata.

claims.quote: アメノワカヒコ（天若日子、天稚彦）は、日本神話に登場する神。アメワカヒコ、アマノワカヒコともする。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang: アメノワカヒコ (天若日子, 天稚彦) adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang, juga ditulis アメワカヒコ dan アマノワカヒコ.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia: アメノワカヒコ (天若日子, 天稚彦) is a deity in Japanese mythology, also written アメワカヒコ and アマノワカヒコ.

claims.quote: 名前の「ワカヒコ」は若い男の意味である。これが神名ではなく普通名詞だったため、「神」「命」「尊」の尊称が付かないとする説がある。また、天津神に反逆したためであるとする説もある。

statement.id: "Wakahiko" dalam namanya berarti pemuda; ada teori bahwa karena itu kata benda umum, bukan nama dewa, ia tidak diberi gelar kehormatan seperti 神, 命, atau 尊, dan teori lain karena ia memberontak kepada para amatsukami.
statement.en: "Wakahiko" in his name means a young man; one theory says that because it was a common noun rather than a divine name he carries no honorific such as 神, 命 or 尊, while another says it is because he rebelled against the amatsukami.

claims.quote: 天若日子の喪屋は『古事記』では地上に作ったとあるが、『日本書紀』では疾風（はやち）に遺体を上げさせて、喪屋は天に作ったとある。

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, gubuk duka Ame no Wakahiko dibuat di bumi, sedangkan Nihon Shoki menyebut jenazah dinaikkan oleh angin kencang dan gubuk duka dibuat di surga.
statement.en: In the Kojiki the mourning hut of Ame no Wakahiko was built on earth, whereas in the Nihon Shoki a gale lifted the body and the hut was built in heaven.

claims.quote: 天若日子と阿遅鉏高日子根神がそっくりだったということで、本来同一の神であったとする説もある。すなわち、アメノワカヒコの死とアヂスキタカヒコネとしての復活であり、これは穀物が秋に枯れて春に再生する、または太陽が冬に力が弱まり春に復活する様子を表したものであるとする。

statement.id: Karena Ame no Wakahiko dan Ajisukitakahikone sangat mirip, ada teori bahwa mereka pada mulanya dewa yang sama: kematian Ame no Wakahiko dan kebangkitannya sebagai Ajisukitakahikone, yang melambangkan padi-padian yang layu di musim gugur lalu tumbuh kembali di musim semi, atau matahari yang melemah di musim dingin lalu bangkit di musim semi.
statement.en: Because Ame no Wakahiko and Ajisukitakahikone looked so alike, one theory holds they were originally the same god: Ame no Wakahiko's death and his revival as Ajisukitakahikone, representing grain withering in autumn and reviving in spring, or the sun weakening in winter and reviving in spring.

claims.quote: Ame-waka-hiko, son of Ame no Kuni-dama. He is a valorous person. Let him be tried.

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan Aston atas Nihongi, para dewa berkata: "Ame-waka-hiko, putra Ame no Kuni-dama. Ia orang yang gagah berani. Biarlah ia dicoba."
statement.en: In Aston's translation of the Nihongi, the gods say: "Ame-waka-hiko, son of Ame no Kuni-dama. He is a valorous person. Let him be tried."

claims.quote: This God also was disloyal, and as soon as he arrived took to wife Shita-teru-hime

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, dewa ini juga tidak setia dan begitu tiba ia mengambil Shita-teru-hime sebagai istri.
statement.en: In the Nihongi this god too was disloyal and as soon as he arrived took Shita-teru-hime to wife.

claims.quote: Then Ame-waka-hiko took the heavenly deer-bow and the heavenly feathered arrows which had been given him by Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto, and shot the pheasant, so that it died.

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko mengambil busur rusa surgawi dan anak panah berbulu surgawi pemberian Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto, lalu memanah burung pegar itu hingga mati.
statement.en: In the Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko took the heavenly deer-bow and heavenly feathered arrows given him by Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto and shot the pheasant so that it died.

claims.quote: Ame-waka-hiko was lying down after the feast of first-fruits, and when hit by the arrow died immediately.

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko sedang berbaring setelah pesta buah pertama, dan ketika terkena anak panah itu ia langsung meninggal.
statement.en: In the Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko was lying down after the feast of first-fruits and died immediately when hit by the arrow.

claims.quote: and sent down a swift wind. to bring the body up to Heaven. Forthwith a mortuary house was made

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, angin kencang dikirim turun untuk membawa jenazah naik ke Surga, lalu segera dibuat rumah duka.
statement.en: In the Nihongi a swift wind was sent down to bring the body up to Heaven, and a mortuary house was promptly made.

short_description.id: Anchimayen adalah makhluk kecil Mapuche berwujud anak-anak yang dapat menjadi bola api terbang, pelayan penyihir kalku [anchimayen-c01, anchimayen-c02].
short_description.en: The Anchimayen is a small Mapuche creature in child form that becomes a flying fireball, servant of a kalku sorcerer [anchimayen-c01, anchimayen-c02].

long_description.id: Anchimayen adalah makhluk mitos Mapuche berwujud anak kecil yang dapat berubah menjadi bola api terbang bercahaya [anchimayen-c01]. Mereka melayani kalku, sejenis penyihir [anchimayen-c02], dan kadang disamakan dengan Kueyen, dewi bulan, karena cahayanya [anchimayen-c03].
long_description.en: The Anchimayen is a Mapuche creature in child form that can become a bright flying fireball [anchimayen-c01]. They serve a kalku, a sorcerer [anchimayen-c02], and are sometimes confused with Kueyen, the moon goddess, because of their light [anchimayen-c03].

long_description.id: Menurut satu sumber, anchimallén dikatakan terdengar seperti tangisan bayi baru lahir [anchimayen-c04]. Ia makan susu, darah, atau madu, dan tugasnya melindungi serta menaati pemiliknya, berbuat baik atau jahat sesuai keinginan pengendalinya [anchimayen-c05]. Bila dibuat oleh seorang calcu, ia diciptakan dari jasad anak yang meninggal mendadak [anchimayen-c06].
long_description.en: According to one source, the anchimallén is said to be heard like the crying of a newborn baby [anchimayen-c04]. It feeds on milk, blood or honey, and its mission is to protect and obey its owner, doing good or evil as the controller wishes [anchimayen-c05]. When made by a calcu, it is created from the remains of a child who died suddenly [anchimayen-c06].

long_description.id: Bila dilihat dari dekat, cahayanya dapat membingungkan dan membuat orang terpana, bahkan buta atau gagap [anchimayen-c07]. Hanya upacara Machitún dan machi yang baik yang dapat mengeluarkannya dari tubuh [anchimayen-c08], dan dalam tradisi rakyat kreol bunyi logam dari taji dikatakan mengusirnya [anchimayen-c09].
long_description.en: Seen up close, its light can confuse and stun a person, even causing blindness or stuttering [anchimayen-c07]. Only Machitún ceremonies and a good machi can make it leave the body [anchimayen-c08], and in Creole popular tradition metallic noises from spurs are said to drive it away [anchimayen-c09].

short_description.id: Apukohai adalah monster laut dalam mitologi pulau Kauaʻi yang dikalahkan oleh raksasa Kawelo setelah pergulatan sengit.
short_description.en: Apukohai is a sea monster from the myths of Kauaʻi island, slain by the giant Kawelo after a hard fight.

long_description.id: Apukohai adalah monster laut dalam mitologi pulau Kauaʻi. Ia dikenal terutama dari kisah Kawelo, raksasa berkekuatan luar biasa, yang bertemu dengannya dalam perjalanan.
long_description.en: Apukohai is a sea monster belonging to the myths of Kauaʻi island. It is known chiefly from the tale of Kawelo, a giant of great strength, who encounters it on a journey.

long_description.id: Menurut satu ringkasan, setelah pergulatan sengit Kawelo membunuh Apukohai dengan memohon bantuan dewa burung hantu dan ikan Ulu-makaikai. Dalam versi lain yang dicatat dalam sebuah kajian ilmiah, Kawelo disambut Kakuhihewa, diam-diam menghimpun pasukan, lalu berangkat dan bertemu "monster jahat" berwujud monster laut Apukohai; ia menyeru dewa burung hantu dan ikan Uhu-makaikai yang ia jerat dalam jaring.
long_description.en: One summary says that after a fierce struggle Kawelo kills Apukohai, having called on the owl god and the fish Ulu-makaikai. Another version, recorded in a scholarly study, has Kawelo welcomed by Kakuhihewa and secretly gathering an expedition; he sets out and meets "evil monsters in the shape of the marine monster Apukohai", calling upon the owl god and netting the fish Uhu-makaikai.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya populer modern, serial komik Sherman's Lagoon menampilkan Apukohai sebagai sosok bertopeng tiki raksasa yang melepaskan petir dari awan.
long_description.en: In modern popular culture, the comic series Sherman's Lagoon shows Apukohai as a figure in a huge Tiki mask who fires lightning bolts from the clouds.

short_description.id: Ascapart adalah raksasa legenda dalam folklor Inggris yang ditaklukkan Bevis dari Hampton, cukup besar untuk mengepit Bevis, istrinya dan kudanya.
short_description.en: Ascapart is a legendary giant of English folklore conquered by Bevis of Hampton, big enough to carry Bevis, his wife and his horse under one arm.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Inggris, Ascapart (juga Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard) adalah raksasa legenda yang konon ditaklukkan Bevis dari Hampton, begitu besar hingga dapat mengepit Bevis, istrinya dan kudanya. Tingginya 30 kaki tetapi ia yang terkecil di negerinya. Ia kalah setelah gadanya, sebatang pohon utuh, diayunkan ke arah Sir Bevis dan tertancap di tanah lunak; Bevis tidak membunuhnya melainkan menjadikannya pengawal.
long_description.en: In English folklore Ascapart (also Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard) is a legendary giant said to have been overcome by Bevis of Hampton, so huge he could carry Bevis, his wife and his horse under his arm. He was 30 feet tall, yet the smallest in his land. He lost when his club, a whole tree, was swung at Sir Bevis and stuck fast in soft ground; Bevis spared him and made him his squire.

long_description.id: Kemudian Ascapart mengkhianati Bevis dan membawa lari istrinya Josiane, lalu dibunuh sahabat-sahabat Bevis. Ia konon dikubur di bawah Bevis Mount, atau tubuhnya menjadi bagian South Downs saat ia jatuh. Raksasa ini juga muncul dalam folklor Hampshire dan New Forest; panel lukisan abad pertengahan Sir Bevis dan Ascupart ada di Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.
long_description.en: Later Ascapart betrayed Bevis and carried off his wife Josiane, and Bevis's friends killed him. He is said to lie under Bevis Mount, or his body became part of the South Downs when he fell. The giant also figures in the folklore of Hampshire and the New Forest; medieval painted panels of Sir Bevis and Ascupart hang in the Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.

long_description.id: Halaman Taman Nasional South Downs menyebut Ascapart tergolong kecil dibanding raksasa zamannya, hanya sekitar 30 kaki, tetapi sangat mampu menakut-nakuti desa-desa di sekitar Southampton. Menurut sebagian penutur, ia hidup hanya karena Josain, istri Bevis, membujuk Bevis. Beberapa catatan menyebut ia memang mengkhianati Bevis dan menculik istrinya, lalu tewas di tangan para pendukung Bevis, dan tubuhnya menjadi bagian dari Downs.
long_description.en: The South Downs National Park page says Ascapart was small for the giants of his day, a mere 30 feet tall, yet more than capable of terrifying the villages around Southampton. Some tellers say he lived only because Josain, Bevis's wife, persuaded Bevis. Some records say he did betray Bevis and kidnapped his wife, and met his death at the hands of Bevis's supporters, his body becoming part of the Downs.

short_description.id: Atavaka adalah yaksa dalam tradisi Buddhis yang dipandang sebagai Wisdom King dalam tradisi esoteris.
short_description.en: Atavaka is a yaksha in Buddhist tradition regarded as a Wisdom King in esoteric tradition.

long_description.id: Atavaka adalah yaksa dalam tradisi Buddhis yang dipandang sebagai Wisdom King dalam tradisi esoteris. Dalam kisahnya, ia adalah yaksa pemakan manusia yang menghuni hutan Atavi. Ia dianggap yaksa duniawi paling kuat pada masa Sang Buddha.
long_description.en: Atavaka is a yaksha in Buddhist tradition regarded as a Wisdom King in esoteric tradition. In the tale he is a man-eating yaksha dwelling in the Atavi forest. He is considered the most powerful earthly yaksha at the time of the Buddha.

long_description.id: Vaisravana memberinya izin memangsa orang yang masuk ke bayangan tempat tinggalnya. Kekurangan tawanan membuat keluarga di wilayah itu dipaksa menyerahkan anak sebagai korban. Salah satu kekuatannya: tatapan kepadanya dapat melemaskan tubuh seseorang selembut mentega. Buddha memasuki kediamannya meski diperingatkan oleh penjaga pintu.
long_description.en: Vaisravana permits him to devour anyone entering the shadow of his dwelling. A shortage of prisoners forces households in the area to provide children as sacrifices. Among his powers, looking at him could soften a person's body like butter. Buddha enters his dwelling despite the doorkeeper's warning.

long_description.id: Meski memiliki kekuatan gaib, ia tidak mampu menggeser Sang Buddha dari singgasananya, dan senjata kain Dussāvudha miliknya jatuh di kaki Sang Buddha seperti permadani; dan, menurut sumber itu, ia mungkin tumbuh sangat besar. Dalam Alavaka Sutta, yakkha itu mengusir dan memanggil Sang Buddha berulang kali, mengancam akan merasuki pikirannya, merobek jantungnya, atau melemparnya melintasi Sungai Gangga; Sang Buddha menjawab bahwa tak seorang pun di kosmos dapat melakukannya. Akhirnya Alavaka berikrar mengembara memberi hormat kepada Sang Buddha dan Dhamma.
long_description.en: Despite his supernormal powers he could not dislodge the Buddha from his throne, and his cloth weapon Dussāvudha simply fell at the Buddha's feet as a rug; he may, according to the source, have grown enormous. In the Alavaka Sutta the yakkha orders the Buddha out and back repeatedly and threatens to possess his mind, rip open his heart or hurl him across the Ganges; the Buddha replies that no one in the cosmos could do so. In the end Alavaka vows to wander paying homage to the Buddha and the Dhamma.

Āṭavaka mengusir dan memanggilnya kembali berkali-kali, mengancam akan merasuki pikirannya, merobek jantungnya, atau melemparnya melintasi Gangga, lalu mengajukan pertanyaan. statement.id: Dalam kisahnya, ia adalah yaksa pemakan manusia yang menghuni hutan Atavi.
statement.en: In the tale he is a man-eating yaksha dwelling in the Atavi forest.

claims.quote: The yakṣa was granted permission by King Vaiśravaṇa that he could seize and devour anyone who came within the shadow of his abode.

statement.id: Vaisravana memberinya izin memangsa orang yang masuk ke bayangan tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: Vaisravana permits him to devour anyone entering the shadow of his dwelling.

claims.quote: due to a shortage of criminals, each household in the vicinity was forced to sacrifice one child to satiate the demon.

statement.id: Kekurangan tawanan membuat keluarga di wilayah itu dipaksa menyerahkan anak sebagai korban.
statement.en: A shortage of prisoners forces households in the area to provide children as sacrifices.

claims.quote: Gadrabha warned the Buddha of the demon's wrathful nature, but the Buddha fearlessly entered Āṭavaka's abode and sat upon his throne.

statement.id: Buddha memasuki kediamannya meski diperingatkan oleh penjaga pintu.
statement.en: Buddha enters his dwelling despite the doorkeeper's warning.

claims.quote: I have heard that on one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Alavi in the haunt of the Alavaka yakkha. Then the Alavaka yakkha went to the Blessed One and on arrival said to him: "Get out, contemplative!"

statement.id: Dalam Alavaka Sutta, pada suatu ketika Sang Bhagavā tinggal di Alavi, di tempat kediaman yakkha Alavaka; yakkha itu mendatanginya dan berkata, "Keluar, pertapa!"
statement.en: In the Alavaka Sutta, on one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Alavi in the haunt of the Alavaka yakkha; the yakkha went to him and said, "Get out, contemplative!"

claims.quote: I will ask you a question, contemplative. If you can't answer me, I will possess your mind or rip open your heart or, grabbing you by the feet, hurl you across the Ganges.

statement.id: Dalam Alavaka Sutta, yakkha itu mengancam: bila pertapa tidak dapat menjawab pertanyaannya, ia akan merasuki pikirannya, merobek jantungnya, atau memegang kakinya dan melemparkannya melintasi Sungai Gangga.
statement.en: In the Alavaka Sutta the yakkha threatens that if the contemplative cannot answer his question he will possess his mind, rip open his heart or, grabbing him by the feet, hurl him across the Ganges.

claims.quote: My friend, I see no one in the cosmos with its devas, Maras & Brahmas, its contemplatives & brahmans, its royalty & commonfolk, who could possess my mind or rip open my heart or, grabbing me by the feet, hurl me across the Ganges.

statement.id: Dalam Alavaka Sutta, sang pertapa menjawab bahwa ia tidak melihat siapa pun di kosmos, baik dewa, Māra, Brahmā, pertapa, brahmana, bangsawan, maupun rakyat, yang dapat merasuki pikirannya, merobek jantungnya, atau melemparkannya melintasi Sungai Gangga.
statement.en: In the Alavaka Sutta the contemplative replies that he sees no one in the cosmos, whether devas, Maras, Brahmas, contemplatives, brahmans, royalty or commonfolk, who could possess his mind, rip open his heart or hurl him across the Ganges.

claims.quote: It was truly for my well-being that the Awakened One came to stay in Alavi. Today I understand where what is given bears great fruit. I will wander from village to village, town to town, paying homage to the Self-awakened One & the true rightness of the Dhamma.

statement.id: Dalam Alavaka Sutta, setelah mendengar jawaban-jawaban itu yakkha Alavaka berkata bahwa kedatangan Sang Buddha di Alavi sungguh demi kesejahteraannya dan ia akan mengembara dari desa ke desa dan kota ke kota memberi hormat kepada Sang Buddha dan Dhamma.
statement.en: In the Alavaka Sutta, after hearing the answers the Alavaka yakkha says the Awakened One's coming to stay at Alavi was truly for his well-being and that he will wander from village to village and town to town paying homage to the Self-awakened One and the Dhamma.

short_description.id: Ayida Wedo adalah loa (roh ilahi) berwujud ular pelangi dalam Vodou Haiti, pasangan Damballa, yang juga dihormati di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey dan wilayah lain di Afrika.
short_description.en: Ayida Wedo is a rainbow-serpent loa, or divine spirit, of Haitian Vodou and the partner of Damballa, also honoured in the former Dahomey kingdom and nearby parts of Africa.

long_description.id: Ayida Wedo, juga ditulis Ayida-Weddo atau Aida Wedo, adalah lwa yang kuat dalam vodou Haiti dan dihormati baik di Karibia maupun di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey/Benin, Togo, dan Ghana tenggara. Ia adalah dewi langit, awan, dan badai, dengan lambang ular dan pelangi. Ia dikaitkan dengan warna biru dan putih, warna langit dan awan.
long_description.en: Ayida Wedo, also spelled Ayida-Weddo or Aida Wedo, is a mighty lwa of Haitian vodou who is honoured in the Caribbean as well as in the former Dahomey kingdom/Benin, Togo and southeastern Ghana. She rules sky, clouds and storms, and the snake and the rainbow are her emblems. Blue and white, the hues of sky and cloud, belong to her.

long_description.id: Ia adalah istri Damballa dan melambangkan kekayaan, keberuntungan, serta kebahagiaan. Seperti suaminya ia tinggal dekat sungai dan menyukai pepohonan. Ia dianggap dewi yang jarang berbelas kasih dalam vaudou, yang kerap melawan Mami Wata untuk mencabut kutukannya atas orang yang tidak setia.
long_description.en: She is Damballa's wife and stands for wealth, luck and happiness. Like him she dwells near rivers and is fond of trees. She is counted a rare merciful deity of vodou, often opposing Mami Wata to undo the curses laid on the unfaithful.

long_description.id: Menurut mitos penciptaan, para dewa ini sudah ada sebelum Bumi, dan Ayida Wedo membantu Mawu-Lisa membentuk dunia: ular itu membawa sang dewi di mulutnya, dan tubuhnya meninggalkan ngarai, sungai, lembah, dan gunung. Di Haiti dikisahkan bahwa ia menyeberangi samudra bersama Damballa; Damballa merayap di bawah laut sementara Ayida Wedo terbang di langit sebagai pelangi hingga keduanya bertemu lagi di Haiti.
long_description.en: In the creation myth these deities predate the Earth, and Ayida Wedo helped Mawu-Lisa form the world: the serpent bore the goddess in its mouth, and its body carved out canyons, rivers, valleys and mountains. Haitian lore tells that she crossed the ocean with Damballa, he gliding beneath the sea while she flew overhead as a rainbow, until they met again in Haiti.

long_description.id: Dalam Vodou Haiti ia disinkretiskan dengan Our Lady of Immaculate Conception. Dalam ritual kerasukan, mediumnya berpakaian putih dengan hiasan kepala berpermata dan merayap di tanah seperti ular.
long_description.en: Haitian Vodou identifies her with Our Lady of Immaculate Conception. In possession rites her medium dresses in white with a jeweled headdress and slithers along the ground like a snake.

long_description.id: Ellis mencatat bahwa orang Ewe memuja Anyi-ewo, dewa pelangi berwujud ular yang muncul ketika haus dan meminum air dalam jumlah besar sehingga tumpahannya turun sebagai hujan. Di Whydah dan Porto Novo, menurutnya, dewa ini punya nama lain yang ditulis Captain Burton sebagai Aydo-whe-do. Manik-manik Popo dipercaya dibuat olehnya.
long_description.en: Ellis records that the Ewe honoured Anyi-ewo, a rainbow-god in serpent form who appears when thirsty and drinks so much that what he spills comes down as rain. In Whydah and Porto Novo, he notes, the god seems to bear another name, written by Captain Burton as Aydo-whe-do. Popo beads were believed to be his work.
