short_description.id: Barak adalah anjing suci dalam mitologi Turk: anjing legendaris yang dianggap bukan anjing biasa, yang dalam sebagian legenda menetas dari telur burung Kerkes dan ditunggangi para dukun menuju langit.
short_description.en: Barak is the sacred dog of Turkic mythology: a legendary hound held to be no ordinary dog, which in some legends hatches from an egg of the bird Kerkes and is ridden by shamans up to the sky.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turk, Barak dikenal sebagai anjing suci. Kedua sumber menyebutnya jenis anjing legendaris yang tidak dianggap anjing biasa, melainkan makhluk yang diberkati. Di Anadolu, nama yang sama juga dipakai untuk anjing pemburu yang berbulu lebat dan sangat cepat larinya.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Barak is known as the sacred dog. Both sources describe it as a legendary kind of dog that is not regarded as an ordinary animal but as a blessed being. In Anadolu the same name is also used for shaggy hunting dogs that run very fast.

long_description.id: Menurut sebagian legenda, ketika burung Kerkes menjadi tua ia meninggalkan dua telur: dari salah satunya lahir Barak, dari yang lain seekor anak burung. Para dukun dipercaya naik ke langit dengan menunggangi Barak dan konon mengenakan lambang-lambangnya di leher mereka.
long_description.en: According to some legends, when the bird Kerkes grows old it leaves two eggs: Barak emerges from one of them and a chick from the other. Shamans are believed to rise to the sky mounted on Barak and are said to wear its symbols around their necks.

long_description.id: Nama Barak juga dikenakan pada manusia berkepala anjing dalam legenda. Artikel pertama mencatat bahwa adanya seorang wali bernama Barak Ata atau Barak Baba di Anadolu tidak dianggap kebetulan.
long_description.en: The name Barak is also applied to legendary dog-headed people. The first article notes that the presence of a saint called Barak Ata or Barak Baba in Anadolu is not regarded as a coincidence.

literal_meaning.id: Akar Bar memuat makna sukacita dan kebanggaan; dalam bahasa Mongol Bar berarti harimau dan Barah berarti perdamaian.
literal_meaning.en: The root Bar carries meanings of joy and pride; in Mongolian Bar means tiger and Barah means peace.

short_description.id: Beast of Bodmin adalah hewan mirip kucing besar yang konon terlihat di Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, Inggris, dan dianggap sebagai salah satu "British big cats".
short_description.en: The Beast of Bodmin is a big-cat-like animal reportedly seen on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall, England, counted among the 'British big cats'.

long_description.id: Beast of Bodmin (atau Beast of Bodmin Moor) adalah salah satu kucing besar Britania (British big cats) yang paling terkenal, yang dituduh membunuh ternak. Menurut artikel ru, hewan mirip kucing besar ini terlihat lebih dari 60 kali sejak 1983 di Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, Inggris, dan diduga panther atau puma yang lepas dari kebun binatang atau koleksi pribadi. Penyelidikan pemerintah pada 1995 tidak menemukan bukti keberadaan hewan semacam itu, meski laporan penampakan terus berlanjut. Menurut artikel it, makhluk itu konon mirip puma berwarna abu-abu gelap hingga hitam dan juga terlihat di Devon dan Somerset.
long_description.en: The Beast of Bodmin (or Beast of Bodmin Moor) is one of the best-known British big cats, blamed for killing livestock. According to the ru article this big-cat-like animal has been seen more than 60 times since 1983 on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall, England, and is thought to be a panther or puma escaped from a zoo or private collection. A government inquiry in 1995 found no evidence of such animals, though sightings continued. According to the it article it is said to look like a puma, dark grey to black, and has also been reported in Devon and Somerset.

long_description.id: Ketika sebuah tengkorak yang ditemukan di Sungai Fowey diserahkan kepada Natural History Museum sebagai bukti keberadaannya, tengkorak itu ternyata dipotong dari permadani kulit macan tutul. Menurut artikel ru, tengkorak yang ditemukan pada 1995 itu memang milik macan tutul jantan muda, tetapi hewan itu tidak dibunuh di Inggris. Para ilmuwan menyatakan laporan semacam itu biasanya tidak dapat dipercaya, karena kelangsungan populasi memerlukan jumlah individu yang tak masuk akal, sedangkan iklim dan sulitnya mencari makan membuat hewan yang lepas sulit bertahan.
long_description.en: When a skull found in the River Fowey was offered to the Natural History Museum as proof of the beast, it turned out to have been cut from a leopard-skin rug. According to the ru article that skull, found in 1995, did belong to a young male leopard, but the animal had not been killed in England. Scientists say such reports are usually unreliable, since a lasting population would need an implausible number of animals, while the climate and scarce prey make survival of escaped cats unlikely.

long_description.en: The Beast of Exmoor is one of the best-known British big cat stories: a cryptozoological cat with dark grey or black fur reported in rural Exmoor, especially Devon and Somerset. Sightings were reported from 1970, and the story became national news in 1983 when more than a hundred sheep were killed with torn throats at South Molton.

long_description.en: It was thought to be an illegally released black leopard or puma, but no big cat has ever been confirmed, and the 1983 killings are now attributed to causes such as large dogs. A carcass once reported as the Beast of Exmoor proved to be a dead seal.

cultural_context.id: Menurut sebuah kajian, narasi tentang begu yang diteliti berfungsi sebagai narasi persuasif untuk mencegah perilaku buruk dan merugikan, dan isu begu ganjang cenderung beredar ketika terjadi kematian mendadak tanpa sebab yang tampak. Suku Batak Toba juga meyakini bahwa arwah orang yang telah wafat tetap bisa mengawasi, melindungi, dan merawat anak cucunya.
cultural_context.en: According to one study, the begu narratives it examines serve as persuasive narratives to prevent bad and harmful behavior, and rumors of begu ganjang tend to spread when a sudden death has no visible cause. The Batak Toba people also believe the spirits of the dead can still watch over, protect and look after their descendants.

did_you_know.en: In a Batak Toba turi-turian, begu ganjang is one of six names Datu Tala gave to his grandchildren, while the seventh grandchild was called jolma (human).

short_description.id: Begu ganjang, atau hantu panjang, adalah roh jahat dalam kepercayaan Batak yang digambarkan besar, kurus, dan gelap seperti bayangan, tampak makin tinggi bila dipandang lebih lama, dan dipercaya dapat dipelihara untuk mencelakai orang.
short_description.en: Begu ganjang, the long ghost, is an evil spirit of Batak belief described as large, thin and shadow-dark, appearing to grow taller the longer it is looked at, and believed to be keepable to harm others.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan masyarakat Batak, begu ganjang termasuk jenis roh jahat yang digambarkan ganas. Tugasnya mencelakai orang, dan korbannya konon ditinggali lebam kebiruan di tenggorokan. Di kalangan Batak Karo ia dinamai begu jinujung, dan pemiliknya harus memberinya sajian berupa darah ayam merah.
long_description.en: In Batak belief, the begu ganjang is counted among the evil spirits and is described as fierce. Its task is to harm people, and its victims are said to be left with a bluish bruise in the throat. Among the Karo Batak it is called begu jinujung, and its owner must give it offerings of red chicken blood.

long_description.id: Secara harfiah begu berarti roh atau hantu dan ganjang berarti panjang atau tinggi. Dalam berbagai cerita rakyat Batak ia dipaparkan besar, kurus, dan memanjang, gelap seperti bayangan, dan tampak makin tinggi serta besar bila dipandang lebih lama. Dalam kajian di Sumatra Utara, sebagian informan menyebut ia tampak seperti bayangan yang makin tinggi bila dilihat ke atas, sementara deskripsi populer lain menyebut bentuknya besar dan hitam, atau bahwa ia dipelihara untuk tujuan tertentu seperti menjaga ladang, atau bahwa ia tidak punya bentuk khusus.
long_description.en: Literally, begu means spirit or ghost and ganjang means long or tall. In various Batak folk tales it is depicted as large, thin and elongated, dark like a shadow, and appearing to grow taller and bigger the longer it is looked at. In a study in North Sumatra, some informants described it as a shadow that grows taller when looked up at, while other popular descriptions say its form is large and black, or that it is kept for certain purposes such as guarding fields, or that it has no particular form.

long_description.id: Menurut budaya Batak, begu ganjang termasuk makhluk gaib yang dipercaya bermula dari manusia ataupun tempat tertentu. Menurut pemahaman Batak Toba, roh orang yang meninggal berubah menjadi begu, dan begu ganjang adalah salah satu jenisnya. Dalam sejumlah tradisi lisan ia dipercaya sebagai roh penjaga lahan pertanian; dalam perkembangan berikutnya ia lebih sering dikaitkan dengan ilmu hitam yang destruktif dan dengan dukun yang dipercaya dapat memanggil atau memeliharanya. Sebuah turi-turian Batak Toba menyebut begu ganjang sebagai satu dari nama yang diberikan Datu Tala kepada cucu-cucunya.
long_description.en: In Batak culture, begu ganjang is a supernatural being believed to originate from humans or certain places. In Batak Toba understanding, the spirits of the dead become begu, and begu ganjang is one kind. In some oral traditions it is believed to be a guardian spirit of farmland; in later developments it is more often linked with destructive black magic and with shamans believed able to summon or keep it. A Batak Toba turi-turian lists begu ganjang among the names Datu Tala gave to his grandchildren.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan ini dipakai untuk menjelaskan kejadian yang sulit dipahami, seperti penyakit misterius, kondisi fisik yang memburuk tanpa sebab jelas, dan kematian mendadak. Isu begu ganjang cenderung beredar ketika ada kematian mendadak tanpa penyebab yang tampak. Masyarakat mencurigai orang tertentu sebagai sigumoang, yang dianggap memiliki dan mengendalikannya, dan orang yang dicurigai memeliharanya pernah menjadi sasaran kekerasan; sebuah kajian menyatakan narasinya awalnya dihormati sebagai warisan budaya tetapi sering disalahgunakan untuk membenarkan tindakan kriminal.
long_description.en: The belief is used to explain events that are hard to understand, such as mysterious illness, unexplained physical decline and sudden death. Rumors of begu ganjang tend to spread when a sudden death has no visible cause. People suspect certain persons of being sigumoang, regarded as owning and controlling it, and people suspected of keeping it have been targets of violence; one study states that the narrative was first respected as cultural heritage but is often misused to justify criminal acts.

Dalam masyarakat Batak, begu ganjang digambarkan sebagai roh ganas karena bertugas untuk mencelakakan orang lain dan menyisakan bekas biru di kerongkongan korbannya. Masyarakat Batak Karo menyebut begu ganjang sebagai "begu jinujung", yaitu roh yang harus diberikan sajian darah ayam merah oleh pemiliknya.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan Batak, begu ganjang adalah roh jahat yang ganas, bertugas mencelakakan orang dan meninggalkan bekas biru di kerongkongan korban; orang Batak Karo menyebutnya begu jinujung yang harus diberi sajian darah ayam merah oleh pemiliknya.
statement.en: In Batak belief, the begu ganjang is a fierce evil spirit tasked with harming people and leaving a bruise on the victim's throat; the Karo Batak call it begu jinujung, which its owner must feed with red-chicken blood.

claims.quote: Dalam budaya Batak, Begu Ganjang adalah makhluk gaib yang diyakini berasal dari manusia atau tempat tertentu. Manusia dianggap memiliki dua unsur yaitu jasad atau fisik, yang disebut pamatang, dan roh, yang disebut tondi. Setelah kematian, roh dipercaya berubah menjadi begu. Begu kemudian pergi ke parbeguan, tempat gaib di mana berkumpul roh-roh orang yang telah meninggal.

statement.id: Dalam budaya Batak, Begu Ganjang adalah makhluk gaib yang diyakini berasal dari manusia atau tempat tertentu; manusia dianggap punya jasad (pamatang) dan roh (tondi), dan setelah kematian roh dipercaya menjadi begu yang pergi ke parbeguan, tempat berkumpulnya roh orang yang telah meninggal.
statement.en: In Batak culture, Begu Ganjang is a supernatural being believed to originate from humans or certain places; a person is considered to have a body (pamatang) and a soul (tondi), and after death the soul is believed to become a begu that goes to the parbeguan, where the spirits of the dead gather.

claims.quote: Secara harfiah, istilah begu berarti “roh” atau “hantu”, sedangkan ganjang berarti “panjang” atau “tinggi”, sehingga keseluruhan namanya sering diterjemahkan sebagai hantu panjang

statement.id: Secara harfiah begu berarti "roh" atau "hantu" dan ganjang berarti "panjang" atau "tinggi", sehingga nama itu sering diterjemahkan sebagai hantu panjang.
statement.en: Literally, begu means "spirit" or "ghost" and ganjang means "long" or "tall", so the name is often translated as long ghost.

statement.id: Dalam sejumlah tradisi lisan, Begu Ganjang dipercaya sebagai roh penjaga lahan pertanian.
statement.en: In some oral traditions, Begu Ganjang is believed to be a guardian spirit of farmland.

claims.quote: Kepercayaan terhadap Begu Ganjang dalam masyarakat Batak umumnya digunakan untuk menjelaskan berbagai peristiwa yang dianggap tidak lazim atau sulit dipahami secara rasional. Kemunculan penyakit misterius, kondisi fisik yang memburuk tanpa sebab yang jelas, hingga kematian mendadak kerap diasosiasikan dengan keberadaan atau gangguan entitas ini.

statement.id: Kepercayaan terhadap Begu Ganjang dalam masyarakat Batak umumnya dipakai untuk menjelaskan peristiwa yang dianggap tidak lazim atau sulit dipahami secara rasional; penyakit misterius, kondisi fisik yang memburuk tanpa sebab jelas, hingga kematian mendadak kerap dikaitkan dengan entitas ini.
statement.en: Belief in Begu Ganjang in Batak society is generally used to explain events seen as unusual or hard to understand rationally; mysterious illness, unexplained physical decline and sudden death are often associated with this entity.

statement.en: According to this study, the begu ganjang myth is an oral tradition that still exists among the Batak Toba people.

statement.en: In the tale, Datu Tala called his grandchildren and struck seven lidi (palm ribs) on them while naming six of them porhas, sibalik hunik, begu ngurngur, sombaon di laut, patuallang ni aji and begu ganjang, while the seventh grandchild was called jolma (human).

statement.en: The Batak Toba people believe a relationship remains between the spirits of the dead and the living; the spirits of the dead can still watch over, protect and look after their descendants.

statement.en: In various Batak folk tales, Begu Ganjang is depicted as a large, thin, elongated figure with a dark, shadow-like color, and its notable trait is that it appears to grow taller and bigger the longer it is looked at.

statement.id: Begu ganjang dikaitkan dengan sistem kepercayaan agraris, yaitu sebagai kekuatan gaib yang diyakini mampu melindungi ladang dari pencurian atau gangguan yang merugikan hasil panen.
statement.en: Begu ganjang is linked with the agrarian belief system, as a supernatural force believed able to protect fields from theft or disturbances that harm the harvest.

statement.id: Dalam perkembangan berikutnya, entitas ini lebih sering dikaitkan dengan ilmu hitam yang destruktif, digambarkan sebagai roh yang dapat dihadirkan atau dikendalikan lewat ritual tertentu untuk mencelakai orang lain atau memperoleh keuntungan material dengan cepat.

short_description.id: Bi’an adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Bi’an is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese lore.

long_description.id: Bi'an adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Ia menyerupai harimau tua dan disebut berkekuatan, dan konon menjunjung kesetiakawanan, gemar perkara hukum, serta mampu membedakan benar dari salah.
long_description.en: Bi'an is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese lore. It resembles an aged tiger and is said to have power, and is said to value loyalty, to be fond of litigation, and to be able to tell right from wrong.

long_description.id: Makhluk itu dikaitkan dengan perkara hukum. Gambarnya menghiasi pintu penjara dan balai pemerintahan, dan namanya menjadi sebutan lain bagi penjara. Sebuah catatan lama menyebut sosok di atas pintu penjara sebagai singa, bukan harimau.
long_description.en: The creature is associated with lawsuits. Its image decorates prison doors and government halls, and its name became another name for a prison. An old record calls the figure above prison gates a lion rather than a tiger.

long_description.id: Pencatatan tertua daftar sembilan putra naga yang diketahui adalah karya Lu Rong. Satu teks menuturkan bahwa daftar itu diperoleh dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui, dan penulisnya menilai keterangan itu tidak berdasar. Menurut satu ulasan, sebagian besar makhluk dalam daftar itu hanya dipakai sebagai nama struktur hiasan.
long_description.en: The oldest known record of the list of the dragon's nine sons is by Lu Rong. One text relates that the list was obtained from an old record of unknown origin, and its author judged the account unfounded. According to one overview, most creatures in the list are merely used as names for decorative structures.

description.id: Konon Bi'an mampu membedakan benar dari salah dan berani bersuara demi keadilan.
description.en: Bi'an is said to be able to tell right from wrong and to speak out for justice.

description.en: Bi'an's image is placed at prison gates or on both sides of the main hall of government offices.

note.id: Bi'an disebut salah satu dari sembilan putra naga.
note.en: Bi'an is named as one of the nine sons of the dragon.

note.id: Disebut bersama Bi'an dalam daftar sembilan putra naga.
note.en: Named alongside Bi'an in the list of the dragon's nine sons.

note.id: Salah satu putra naga yang daftarnya memuat Bi'an; disebut berdasar hewan mitologi yang lebih tua.
note.en: One of the dragon's sons in lists that include Bi'an; said to be based on an earlier mythological beast.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa makhluk hiasan seperti Bi'an dikaitkan dengan fungsi bangunan tertentu seperti penjara dan kantor pemerintah?
learning_questions.en: Why might a decorative creature such as Bi'an be tied to the function of particular buildings such as prisons and government offices?

statement.id: Bi’an adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Bi’an is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese lore.

claims.quote: 姿は老いた虎に似ていて威力があり、訴訟を好む。故に監獄の扉や、官庁の正面の広間の両側の格子窓の意匠となり、監獄の異称となった。

statement.id: Ia menyerupai harimau tua.

statement.en: Its image decorates prison doors and government halls.

claims.quote: 龍生九子,不成龍,各有所好。囚牛,好音樂,以飾胡琴。 ... 狴犴,好訟,為獄門。

statement.id: Dalam teks ini, "sembilan putra naga" disebut tidak menjadi naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran; Bi'an (狴犴) digambarkan gemar perkara hukum dan dipakai untuk pintu penjara.
statement.en: In this text the "nine sons of the dragon" are said not to become dragons and each has its own liking; Bi'an (狴犴) is described as fond of litigation and used for the prison gate.

claims.quote: 弘治間,泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽,李不能悉,詢於吏部劉員外績,乃得其說,於故冊面上所錄,然亦不知所從出,因據以復。

statement.id: Teks ini menuturkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi, Tailing (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim istana menanyakan nama sembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang; Li tidak dapat menjawab lengkap, lalu bertanya kepada Liu Ji dan memperoleh daftarnya dari catatan lama, tetapi asal-usul daftar itu tidak diketahui.
statement.en: This text relates that in the Hongzhi era Tailing (泰陵) had a court eunuch ask Li Dongyang for the names of the nine sons of the dragon; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji, and obtained the list from an old record, but the origin of the list was unknown.

claims.quote: 余憶十一、二時,曾見其說於《對類總龜》中,近因歴考傳記,乃知其說為不經。

statement.id: Penulis teks ini mengingat pernah melihat daftar itu dalam "Duilei Zonggui" pada usia sebelas atau dua belas tahun, dan setelah menelaah catatan lama menyimpulkan bahwa keterangan itu tidak berdasar.
statement.en: The author of this text recalls having seen the list in the "Duilei Zonggui" at about eleven or twelve, and after examining old records concluded that the account is unfounded.

claims.quote: 一曰狻猊，好坐，今佛座獅子是。一曰狴犴，好訟，今獄門上獅子是。一曰贔贔，好文，今石碑兩旁龍是。

statement.id: Dalam catatan ini, putra yang disebut Bi'an (狴犴) gemar perkara hukum, dan sosok di atas pintu penjara disebut singa (shizi).
statement.en: In this record, the son called Bi'an (狴犴) is fond of litigation, and the figure above prison gates is said to be a lion (shizi).

claims.quote: 傳說其重義氣、好訴訟，能明辨是非、仗義執言《潛確居類書》有：「狴犴，其形似虎，有威力，故立於獄門上。」的敘述。故獄門或官衙正堂兩側立其形象，後為牢獄的代稱。

statement.id: Konon Bi'an menjunjung kesetiakawanan, gemar perkara hukum, mampu membedakan benar dari salah, dan berani bersuara demi keadilan.

statement.id: "Qianqueju Leishu" menyebut Bi'an berbentuk mirip harimau dan berkekuatan, sehingga dipasang di atas pintu penjara; karena itu rupanya dipasang di pintu penjara atau kedua sisi aula utama kantor pemerintah, dan kemudian menjadi sebutan lain bagi penjara.
statement.en: The "Qianqueju Leishu" says Bi'an resembles a tiger and has power, hence it is set above prison gates; so its image is placed at prison gates or on both sides of the main hall of government offices, and later became another name for a prison.

claims.quote: The oldest known attestation of the children of the dragon list is found in the Miscellaneous records from the bean garden (菽園雜記) by Lu Rong (1436–1494); however, he noted that the list enumerates mere synonyms of various antiques, not children of a dragon.

short_description.id: Burrokeet adalah karakter "manusia-keledai" tradisional dalam Karnaval Trinidad dan Tobago; kostumnya membuat penari tampak menunggang keledai kecil.
short_description.en: The Burrokeet is a traditional "donkey-man" character of Trinidad and Tobago Carnival whose costume makes the dancer appear to ride a small donkey.

long_description.id: Burrokeet (ejaan lain: Burroquite, borokit, borokite, bourriquite) adalah karakter "manusia-keledai" yang secara tradisional ditampilkan dalam Karnaval Trinidad dan Tobago. Namanya berasal dari kata Spanyol burroquito (keledai kecil), dan kostumnya dirancang agar tampak seperti penari yang menunggang keledai kecil. Pertunjukan topeng ini dibawa ke Trinidad oleh para pemukim Venezuela.
long_description.en: The Burrokeet, also spelled Burroquite, borokit, borokite or bourriquite, is a traditional Trinidad and Tobago Carnival character in the form of a "donkey-man". The name comes from the Spanish burroquito (little donkey), and the costume is built so that the dancer seems to be riding a small burro. Settlers from Venezuela brought this masquerade to Trinidad.

long_description.id: Kostumnya berupa kepala keledai berhias dari kertas berwarna pada rangka bambu. Penari masuk lewat lubang di belakang leher "keledai" dan memegang tali kekang, dengan tubuh keledai terpasang di pinggulnya sehingga tampak seperti penunggangnya. Tubuh keledai ditutup rok satin panjang dan berekor tali sisal yang kadang dihiasi bunga, sedangkan kekangnya dibuat dari tali berwarna.
long_description.en: The costume has an ornate donkey head of coloured paper fixed to a bamboo frame. The performer steps in through an opening behind the donkey's neck and grips the reins, with the animal's body worn around the hips, so that he looks like its rider. A long satin skirt covers the body, a sisal rope serves as the tail (at times decorated with flowers), and the bit and bridle are made of coloured cord.

long_description.id: "Penunggang" mengenakan kemeja satin dan topi jerami matador besar, lalu menari menirukan tingkah keledai yang melonjak dan membungkuk. Tarian bernama Burriquite yang berasal dari Venezuela juga dibawakan.
long_description.en: The "rider" is dressed in a satin shirt and a big matador straw hat, and dances so as to imitate a donkey's antics, making the animal caper and bow. The Burriquite, a dance that originated in Venezuela, is also performed.

long_description.id: Mas burrokeet, yang dikaitkan dengan daratan Amerika Selatan dan orang Spanyol Venezuela, telah terkait dengan tokoh "Sou-Marie" yang berasal dari budaya India Timur yang dibawa buruh kontrak ke Trinidad.
long_description.en: The burrokeet masquerade, tied to the South American mainland and to Venezuelan Spaniards, has become connected with the "Sou-Marie" character, which stems from East Indian culture that indentured labourers brought to Trinidad.

short_description.id: Cadborosaurus, dijuluki Caddy, adalah ular laut dalam cerita rakyat pesisir Pasifik Amerika Utara. Namanya berasal dari Cadboro Bay di Victoria, British Columbia.
short_description.en: Cadborosaurus, nicknamed Caddy, is a sea serpent in the folklore of the Pacific Coast of North America. Its name derives from Cadboro Bay in Victoria, British Columbia.

long_description.id: Cadborosaurus dijuluki Caddy oleh jurnalis Archie Wills dan dikenal sebagai ular laut dalam cerita rakyat pesisir Pasifik Amerika Utara. Namanya berasal dari Cadboro Bay di Victoria, British Columbia, dan kata Yunani saûros yang berarti kadal atau reptil. Para saksi dikatakan menggambarkannya sebagai ular dengan lekukan atau punuk vertikal di belakang kepala mirip kuda dan leher panjang.
long_description.en: Cadborosaurus was nicknamed Caddy by the journalist Archie Wills and is known as a sea serpent in the folklore of the Pacific Coast of North America. The name combines Cadboro Bay in Victoria, British Columbia, with the Greek saûros (lizard or reptile). Witnesses reportedly describe a serpent with vertical humps trailing a horse-like head and long neck.

long_description.id: Disebutkan lebih dari 300 klaim penampakan dalam 200 tahun terakhir. Pada Oktober 1937, sebuah bangkai yang disebut-sebut sebagai Cadborosaurus diambil dari perut paus sperma di Naden Harbour dan difoto; direktur BC Provincial Museum, Francis Kermode, mengidentifikasinya sementara sebagai janin paus balin. Sampelnya kini sudah lama hilang, dan banyak ilmuwan menilai foto-foto itu hanya memperlihatkan hiu penjemur yang membusuk.
long_description.en: More than 300 sightings are claimed over the past 200 years. In October 1937 a carcass said to be Cadborosaurus was taken from inside a sperm whale at Naden Harbour and photographed; Francis Kermode, director of the BC Provincial Museum, tentatively identified a sample as a fetal baleen whale. The samples have long since disappeared, and many scientists say the photographs simply show a decomposing basking shark.

long_description.id: Penjelasan ilmiah diperdebatkan. LeBlond dan Blousfield menyatakan tidak ada makhluk yang dikenal cocok dengan ciri-ciri dalam lebih dari 200 penampakan, sedangkan Darren Naish menilai mereka keliru menganggap laporan saksi mata yang saling bertentangan sebagai satu spesies. Berbagai hewan memanjang, termasuk belut Conger, paus bungkuk, anjing laut gajah, oarfish, hiu penjemur, dan singa laut, telah diajukan sebagai penjelasan untuk Caddy.
long_description.en: The scientific interpretation is disputed. LeBlond and Blousfield state that no known creature matches the characteristics in over 200 sightings, while Darren Naish contends they wrongly assume conflicting eyewitness reports describe one species. A diverse array of elongated animals, including Conger eels, humpback whales, elephant seals, oarfish, basking sharks, and sea lions, has been put forward as explanations for Caddy.

short_description.id: Cagrino adalah roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat Rom, berwujud landak kuning, yang menunggangi kuda pada malam hari sampai kelelahan.
short_description.en: The Cagrino is an evil spirit of the folklore of the Roma, shaped like a yellow hedgehog, that rides horses to exhaustion at night.

long_description.id: Cagrino atau Guecubu adalah roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat orang Rom di daratan Eropa, yang mitosnya berasal dari barat laut India dengan nama Harginn. Ia berwujud landak kuning sepanjang sekitar 50 cm. Pada malam hari ia menunggangi kuda sampai kelelahan, sehingga esok harinya kuda itu sakit, surainya kusut, dan basah oleh keringat. Sebagai penangkal, kuda diikat pada tiang yang digosok bawang putih dengan benang merah berbentuk salib.
long_description.en: The Cagrino or Guecubu is an evil spirit in the folklore of the continental Roma whose myth comes from north-western India, where it is called Harginn. It has the form of a yellow hedgehog about 50 cm long. At night it rides horses to exhaustion, so the next day they are sick, tangled-maned and drenched in sweat. As a remedy, horses are tied to a garlic-rubbed stake with a red thread laid in a cross.

long_description.id: Sebuah ensiklopedia okultisme mencatat Chagrin atau Cagrino sebagai roh jahat yang berbentuk landak kuning sepanjang satu setengah kaki dan selebar sejengkal. Kuda adalah mangsa khususnya: ia menungganginya sampai kelelahan, seperti halnya Guecubu dari Chili, sehingga keesokan harinya kuda tampak sakit, bersurai kusut, dan bersimbah keringat. Penangkalnya antara lain mengikat kuda pada tiang yang digosok sari bawang putih dengan benang merah berbentuk salib di tanah.
long_description.en: An encyclopaedia of occultism records the Chagrin or Cagrino as an evil spirit shaped like a yellow hedgehog a foot and a half long and a span wide. Horses are its special prey: it rides them to exhaustion, as does the Guecubu of Chili, so that the next day they appear sick, tangle-maned and bathed in sweat. Remedies include tethering the horse to a garlic-rubbed stake with a red thread laid in a cross on the ground.

text.id: Dalam mitologi Maya Pasca-Klasik Akhir dalam Popol Vuh
text.en: In the Late Post-Classic Maya mythology of the Popol Vuh

short_description.id: Camazotz ('kelelawar maut') adalah roh kelelawar dalam Popol Vuh yang melayani para penguasa dunia bawah dan merenggut kepala Hunahpu di House of Bats.
short_description.en: Camazotz ('death bat') is a bat spirit in the Popol Vuh who serves the lords of the underworld and snatched off Hunahpu's head in the House of Bats.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Maya dalam Popol Vuh, Camazotz adalah roh kelelawar yang melayani para penguasa dunia bawah. Namanya, dari kata Kʼicheʼ kame ('kematian') dan sotz' ('kelelawar'), berarti 'kelelawar maut'. Di Mesoamerika secara umum, kelelawar sering dikaitkan dengan malam, kematian, dan pengorbanan; bangsa Zapotec percaya hal itu, kemungkinan karena kelelawar menghuni gua di sekitar cenote suci yang dianggap gerbang ke dunia bawah.
long_description.en: In the Maya mythology of the Popol Vuh, Camazotz is a bat spirit serving the lords of the underworld. His name, from the Kʼicheʼ words kame ('death') and sotz' ('bat'), means 'death bat'. Across Mesoamerica bats are often linked with night, death, and sacrifice; the Zapotecs believed so, likely because bats inhabited caves around sacred cenotes seen as portals to the underworld.

long_description.id: Dalam Popol Vuh, Camazotz adalah roh mirip kelelawar yang ditemui Kembar Pahlawan Hunahpu dan Xbalanque dalam ujian mereka di Xibalba. Kedua saudara itu harus bermalam di House of Bats dan menyelipkan diri ke dalam sumpit mereka untuk melindungi diri dari kelelawar yang berputar. Ketika Hunahpu menjulurkan kepala untuk melihat apakah matahari telah terbit, Camazotz langsung merenggut kepalanya dan membawanya ke lapangan bola untuk digantung sebagai bola bagi para dewa dalam pertandingan berikutnya.
long_description.en: In the Popol Vuh, Camazotz are the bat-like spirits met by the Hero Twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque during their trials in Xibalba. The brothers had to spend the night in the House of Bats and squeezed into their blowguns to protect themselves from the circling bats. When Hunahpu poked his head out to see whether the sun had risen, Camazotz at once snatched it off and carried it to the ballcourt to hang as the ball for the gods' next game.

long_description.id: Camazotz digambarkan sebagai kelelawar berhidung daun berwujud manusia yang lazim memegang pisau korban dan jantung atau korban manusia. Kemudian dalam Popol Vuh, seorang utusan dunia bawah berwujud kelelawar mirip manusia, yang diyakini Camazotz, menengahi kesepakatan antara manusia dan Tuan Tohil.
long_description.en: Camazotz is described as a human-like leaf-nosed bat commonly shown holding a sacrificial knife and a human heart or victim. Later in the Popol Vuh, an underworld messenger in the form of a humanoid bat, believed to be Camazotz, brokers a deal between humanity and Lord Tohil.

long_description.id: Ikonografi Maya Klasik sering menampilkan kelelawar sebagai roh pendamping pembawa penyakit, tetapi roh kelelawar Klasik itu jarang tampil dalam konteks naratif dan tampaknya tidak memerankan tokoh yang digambarkan Popol Vuh. Brady dan Coltman membantah pandangan lama yang menafsirkan citra kelelawar Maya sebagai Camazotz dan mengusulkan agar identifikasi itu ditinggalkan. Mereka tidak menemukan penggambaran kuno Kembar Pahlawan di ruang camazotz, dan menurut sebagian besar epigraf makhluk wahy adalah wujud hewani dari penyakit yang dipersonifikasikan.
long_description.en: Classic Maya iconography often shows bats as disease-bringing way-spirits, but the Classic bat spirit is rarely part of a narrative context and does not appear to play the role assigned by the Popol Vuh. Brady and Coltman dispute the older view that read Maya bat imagery as Camazotz and propose dropping the identification. They found no ancient images of the Hero Twins in the camazotz chamber, and most epigraphers now think wahy beings were bestial forms of personified diseases.

sources.title: Bats and the Camazotz: Correcting a Century of Mistaken Identity
sources.author: James E. Brady and Jeremy D. Coltman

claims.quote: In Mesoamerica generally, the bat is often associated with night, death, and sacrifice.

statement.id: Di Mesoamerika secara umum kelelawar diasosiasikan dengan malam, kematian, dan pengorbanan.
statement.en: In Mesoamerica generally, the bat is often associated with night, death, and sacrifice.

claims.quote: The twins had to spend the night in the House of Bats, where they squeezed themselves into their own blowguns in order to defend themselves from the circling bats.

statement.id: Pahlawan kembar harus bermalam di House of Bats untuk melindungi diri dari kelelawar yang berputar.
statement.en: The twins had to spend the night in the House of Bats, where they squeezed themselves into their own blowguns in order to defend themselves from the circling bats.

claims.quote: Hunahpu stuck his head out of his blowgun to see if the sun had risen and Camazotz immediately snatched off his head and carried it to the ballcourt to be hung up as the ball to be used by the gods in their next ballgame.

statement.id: Camazotz memenggal kepala Hunahpu dan membawanya ke lapangan bola dewa.
statement.en: Hunahpu stuck his head out of his blowgun to see if the sun had risen and Camazotz immediately snatched off his head and carried it to the ballcourt to be hung up as the ball to be used by the gods in their next ballgame.

claims.quote: However, the Classic bat spirit is rarely, if ever, part of a narrative context, nor does it appear to play the role assigned to it by the Popol Vuh.

statement.id: Roh kelelawar era Klasik jarang berada dalam konteks narasi Popol Vuh.
statement.en: However, the Classic bat spirit is rarely, if ever, part of a narrative context, nor does it appear to play the role assigned to it by the Popol Vuh.

claims.quote: In the Late Post-Classic Maya mythology of the Popol Vuh, Camazotz ... (alternate spellings Cama-Zotz, Sotz, Zotz) is a bat spirit at the service of the lords of the underworld.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Maya Pasca-Klasik Akhir dalam Popol Vuh, Camazotz (ejaan lain Cama-Zotz, Sotz, Zotz) adalah roh kelelawar yang melayani para penguasa dunia bawah.
statement.en: In the Late Post-Classic Maya mythology of the Popol Vuh, Camazotz (alternate spellings Cama-Zotz, Sotz, Zotz) is a bat spirit at the service of the lords of the underworld.

claims.quote: Camazotz is formed from the Kʼicheʼ words kame, meaning "death", and sotz', meaning "bat".

statement.id: Camazotz dibentuk dari kata Kʼicheʼ kame yang berarti 'kematian' dan sotz' yang berarti 'kelelawar'.
statement.en: Camazotz is formed from the Kʼicheʼ words kame, meaning 'death', and sotz', meaning 'bat'.

claims.quote: In the Popol Vuh, Camazotz are the bat-like spirits encountered by the Maya Hero Twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque during their trials in the underworld of Xibalba.

statement.id: Dalam Popol Vuh, Camazotz adalah roh mirip kelelawar yang ditemui Kembar Pahlawan Maya, Hunahpu dan Xbalanque, selama ujian mereka di dunia bawah Xibalba.
statement.en: In the Popol Vuh, Camazotz are the bat-like spirits encountered by the Maya Hero Twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque during their trials in the underworld of Xibalba.

claims.quote: In Classic Maya iconography, the (leaf-nosed) bat, exhaling unhealthy vapours, is often depicted as a person's nahual or way-spirit bringing disease over an enemy.

statement.id: Dalam ikonografi Maya Klasik, kelelawar (berhidung daun) yang mengembuskan uap tak sehat sering digambarkan sebagai nahual atau roh pendamping seseorang yang membawa penyakit kepada musuh.
statement.en: In Classic Maya iconography, the (leaf-nosed) bat, exhaling unhealthy vapours, is often depicted as a person's nahual or way-spirit bringing disease over an enemy.

claims.quote: Brady and Coltman dispute the earlier scholarly view that interpreted Maya bat imagery as representations of Camazotz. Maya bat imagery appears in different forms and contexts, so scholars should distinguish among those representations.

statement.id: Brady dan Coltman membantah pandangan ilmiah terdahulu yang menafsirkan citra kelelawar Maya sebagai penggambaran Camazotz; citra kelelawar Maya muncul dalam beragam bentuk dan konteks sehingga para ahli perlu membedakannya.
statement.en: Brady and Coltman dispute the earlier scholarly view that interpreted Maya bat imagery as representations of Camazotz; Maya bat imagery appears in different forms and contexts, so scholars should distinguish among them.

claims.quote: The name Camazotz translates to either ‘death bat’ or ‘snatch bat’. This deity appears in the Popol Vuh and is still a very prominent figure in the continuing Maya religion.

statement.id: Nama Camazotz diterjemahkan sebagai 'kelelawar maut' atau 'kelelawar perenggut'. Dewa ini muncul dalam Popol Vuh dan masih menjadi tokoh yang sangat menonjol dalam agama Maya yang berlanjut.
statement.en: The name Camazotz translates to either 'death bat' or 'snatch bat'; this deity appears in the Popol Vuh and is still a very prominent figure in the continuing Maya religion.

claims.quote: Camazotz is described as an anthropomorphized leaf-nosed bat. ... The god is also commonly depicted holding a sacrificial knife in one hand and a human heart or sacrificial victim in the other.

statement.id: Camazotz digambarkan sebagai kelelawar berhidung daun yang berwujud manusia; sang dewa juga lazim digambarkan memegang pisau korban di satu tangan dan jantung manusia atau korban di tangan lain.
statement.en: Camazotz is described as an anthropomorphized leaf-nosed bat, and the god is also commonly depicted holding a sacrificial knife in one hand and a human heart or sacrificial victim in the other.

claims.quote: The Zapotecs believed bats represented night, death, and sacrifice. This was likely due to the fact that the bats would inhabit the caves around the sacred cenotes, which the Mesoamericans believed were portals to the underworld.

statement.id: Bangsa Zapotec percaya kelelawar melambangkan malam, kematian, dan pengorbanan, kemungkinan karena kelelawar menghuni gua-gua di sekitar cenote suci yang dipercaya orang Mesoamerika sebagai gerbang ke dunia bawah.
statement.en: The Zapotecs believed bats represented night, death, and sacrifice, likely because the bats inhabited the caves around the sacred cenotes, which the Mesoamericans believed were portals to the underworld.

claims.quote: Later in the Popol Vuh, a messenger from the underworld in the form of a humanoid bat (believed to be Camazotz) appears to broker a deal between humanity and Lord Tohil, the patron god of the K’iche’.

statement.id: Kemudian dalam Popol Vuh, seorang utusan dari dunia bawah berwujud kelelawar mirip manusia (diyakini Camazotz) muncul untuk menengahi kesepakatan antara umat manusia dan Tuan Tohil, dewa pelindung bangsa K’iche’.
statement.en: Later in the Popol Vuh, a messenger from the underworld in the form of a humanoid bat (believed to be Camazotz) appears to broker a deal between humanity and Lord Tohil, the patron god of the K’iche’.

claims.quote: At the end of the nineteenth century, Eduard Seler identified the bats depicted on a ceramic vessel excavated by Erwin Dieseldorff at the site of Chama, Guatemala, as the camazotz, or death bat, from the K’iche’ Maya myth, the Popol Vuh. The attribution was never critically reviewed.

statement.id: Pada akhir abad ke-19, Eduard Seler mengidentifikasi kelelawar pada bejana keramik yang digali Erwin Dieseldorff di situs Chama, Guatemala, sebagai camazotz atau kelelawar maut dari mitos Maya K’iche’, Popol Vuh; atribusi itu tidak pernah ditinjau secara kritis.
statement.en: At the end of the nineteenth century, Eduard Seler identified the bats on a ceramic vessel excavated by Erwin Dieseldorff at Chama, Guatemala, as the camazotz, or death bat, of the K’iche’ Maya myth, the Popol Vuh; the attribution was never critically reviewed.

claims.quote: We have located no ancient depictions of the Hero Twins in the chamber of the camazotz, which calls into question the salience of this scene for the ancient Maya.

statement.id: Para penulis tidak menemukan penggambaran kuno Kembar Pahlawan di ruang camazotz, yang mempertanyakan arti penting adegan ini bagi bangsa Maya kuno.
statement.en: The authors located no ancient depictions of the Hero Twins in the chamber of the camazotz, which calls into question the salience of this scene for the ancient Maya.

claims.quote: We argue that the identification with the camazotz should be dropped altogether and that the associations proposed by Seler need to be rethought.

statement.id: Para penulis berpendapat bahwa identifikasi dengan camazotz sebaiknya ditinggalkan sama sekali dan bahwa asosiasi yang diusulkan Seler perlu dipikirkan ulang.
statement.en: The authors argue that the identification with the camazotz should be dropped altogether and that the associations proposed by Seler need to be rethought.

claims.quote: The last and largest category is wahy beings, which most epigraphers now think were bestial forms of personified diseases.

statement.id: Kategori peran terakhir dan terbesar bagi kelelawar adalah makhluk wahy, yang menurut sebagian besar epigraf kini adalah wujud hewani dari penyakit yang dipersonifikasikan.
statement.en: The last and largest category of bat roles is wahy beings, which most epigraphers now think were bestial forms of personified diseases.

short_description.id: Cenocroca adalah hewan legendaris bersuara manusia, berahang singa dan bertubuh keledai, yang meniru suara orang untuk memikat mangsa.
short_description.en: The Cenocroca is a legendary beast with a human voice, a lion's jaws and an ass's body, that mimics people to lure prey.

long_description.id: Cenocroca adalah hewan legendaris yang sering tertukar dengan Crocotta. Ia bersuara manusia, giginya satu tulang utuh, mulutnya terbelah sampai telinga, berahang dan berdada singa, bertubuh keledai, dan bertanduk ibex. Pupilnya tak pernah bergerak, dan ia meniru panggilan orang atau suara hewan untuk memikat mangsa.
long_description.en: The Cenocroca is a legendary beast often confused with the Crocotta. It has a human voice, a solid bone for teeth, a mouth slit to its ears, a lion's jaws and chest, an ass's body and ibex horns. Its pupils never move, and it imitates human calls or animal cries to lure prey.

long_description.id: Sebutan tertua makhluk bernama Krokottas ada dalam Geografi karya Strabo, sebagai persilangan anjing dan serigala dari Etiopia. Makhluk ini juga digambarkan dalam Il nome della rosa karya Umberto Eco.
long_description.en: The oldest mention of a creature called Krokottas is in Strabo's Geography, as a dog-wolf cross from Ethiopia. The creature also appears in Umberto Eco's Il nome della rosa.

long_description.id: Karena cenocroca sering dikacaukan dengan crocotta, teks klasik tentang crocotta ikut relevan. Pliny menggambarkan crocotta sebagai hewan yang tampak seolah lahir dari perkawinan serigala dan anjing, mampu mematahkan apa pun dengan giginya. Ia juga menggambarkan leucrocotta, binatang buas yang luar biasa cepat dengan mulut terbelah sampai ke telinga dan bergigi satu tulang menerus, yang konon dapat menirukan suara manusia.
long_description.en: Because the cenocroca is often confused with the crocotta, the classical text on the crocotta is relevant. Pliny describes the crocotta as an animal that seems born of a wolf and a dog, able to break anything with its teeth. He also describes the leucrocotta, a wild beast of extraordinary swiftness with a mouth split back to the ears and a single unbroken bone in place of teeth, which is said to imitate the human voice.

statement.en: It never moved its pupils and always stared straight ahead, and with its human voice it imitated people's calls or animal cries to lure prey and devour it.

long_description.id: Chakor adalah burung mitologis India yang terpesona oleh bulan purnama. Ia digambarkan tetap diam sepanjang malam sambil mengikuti gerakan bulan dengan kepalanya. Artikel menghubungkannya dengan ayam hutan chukar.
long_description.en: Chakor is an Indian mythological bird captivated by the full moon. It is portrayed remaining still all night while following the moon's movement with its head. The article connects it with the chukar partridge.

long_description.id: Entri glosarium menyebut cakora sebagai burung yang hidup semata-mata dari cahaya bulan, dan sebuah kamus Hindi-Inggris menyebutnya ayam hutan berkaki merah India yang konon juga memakan bara. Sebuah teks Jain menyebutnya sejenis ayam hutan yang konon hidup dari sinar bulan. Entri glosarium lain menyebutnya hanya minum air dari Svati Naksatra.
long_description.en: Glossary entries describe the cakora as a bird that lives solely on moonlight, and a Hindi-English dictionary calls it the Indian red-legged partridge, fabled also to eat embers. A Jain text describes it as a kind of partridge said to live on moon-beams. Another glossary entry says it drinks only water from the Svati Nakshatra.

short_description.en: Chakora is a legendary bird in Hindu mythology, considered a partridge, believed to feed on moonbeams.

long_description.id: Chakora adalah burung legendaris yang dijelaskan dalam mitologi Hindu. Burung ini dianggap sejenis partridge, kemungkinan besar berdasarkan chukar partridge. Dalam teks seperti Mṛcchakaṭika, ia dipercaya memakan sinar bulan (Chandra).
long_description.en: The chakora is a legendary bird of Hindu mythology, taken to be a partridge and probably modelled on the chukar partridge. Texts such as the Mṛcchakaṭika hold that it feeds on the beams of the moon (Chandra).

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan sebuah drama, mata sang pengarang dilukiskan seperti mata burung chakora yang memakan sinar bulan. Sebuah catatan kaki dalam terjemahan sebuah kumpulan kisah menyatakan bahwa Chakora dikatakan hidup dari sinar bulan, dan dalam sebuah kisah di sana bulan bagi burung-burung partridge dijadikan perumpamaan.
long_description.en: In the translation of one play, the author's eyes are compared to those of the chakora bird, which lives on moonbeams. A footnote in the translation of a story collection says the Chakora is said to live on moonbeams, and a story there uses the moon's relation to the partridges as a simile.

short_description.id: Cheukshin adalah dewi jamban dalam mitologi Korea.
short_description.en: Cheukshin is the latrine goddess of Korean mythology.

long_description.id: Cheukshin adalah dewi jamban dalam mitologi Korea. Ia dipercaya tinggal di jamban. Ensiklopedia budaya Korea menyebutnya sebagai gasin (dewa rumah tangga) yang dipercaya bersifat jahat dan menguasai jamban, umumnya dewi berambut panjang yang berperangai kasar dan mudah murka sehingga ditakuti.
long_description.en: Cheukshin is the latrine goddess of Korean mythology. She is believed to reside in the latrine. A Korean cultural encyclopedia describes her as a household god (gasin) believed to be evil and to preside over the toilet, generally a long-haired goddess with a fierce, easily angered temper who has been feared.

long_description.id: Penggambarannya berupa perempuan muda berambut panjang yang menghitung rambutnya. Ritual tertentu dilakukan pada tanggal lunar enam, enam belas, dan dua puluh enam. Sesaji meliputi kue beras dan nasi. Sebuah kepercayaan menyebut batuk tiga kali sebelum masuk untuk menghindari serangan rambutnya. Menurut ensiklopedia itu, ia dikatakan hanya muncul pada hari bertanggal ada angka 6, dan batuk tiga kali sebelum masuk jamban ditafsirkan sebagai upaya menghindari malapetaka.
long_description.en: Her portrayal is a young long-haired woman who counts her hair. Certain rites were performed on lunar days six, sixteen, and twenty-six. Offerings included rice cakes and cooked rice. One belief describes coughing three times before entry to avoid an attack with her hair. According to the encyclopedia, she is said to appear only on days containing the number 6, and coughing three times before entering the latrine is interpreted as a measure to avoid misfortune.

long_description.id: Asal-usulnya muncul dalam Munjeon Bonpuri dari Pulau Jeju, tentang putri seorang selir yang menjadi Cheukdo Buin setelah gantung diri di jamban. Karena istri sah Jowang dan Cheukdo Buin disebut bermusuhan, orang membangun dapur dan jamban berjauhan dan tidak membawa barang dari satu ke yang lain. Penyakit atau kecelakaan di jamban dipercaya sebagai ulahnya, dan di Gangwon diadakan ritual setelah jamban dibangun.
long_description.en: Her origin appears in the Munjeon Bonpuri of Jeju Island, about a concubine's daughter who became Cheukdo Buin after hanging herself in the latrine. Because the first wife Jowang and Cheukdo Buin are said to be enemies, people build the kitchen and latrine far apart and do not carry things from one to the other. Illness or accidents in the toilet are believed to be her doing, and in Gangwon a rite is held after a latrine is built.

summary.en: A concubine's daughter kills the first wife and tries to kill her seven sons, but her plot is exposed; she flees to the latrine, hangs herself, and becomes Cheukdo Buin.

claims.quote: 측신은 150cm의 머리카락을 가진 젊은 처녀로 보인다고 믿어졌다. 최고신 천지왕과 부엌의 여신 조왕신에 의해 측간으로 유배된 것에 격분한 여신은 자신의 머리카락을 세며 시간을 보낸다고 한다.

statement.id: Penggambarannya berupa perempuan muda berambut panjang yang menghitung rambutnya.
statement.en: Her portrayal is a young long-haired woman who counts her hair.

claims.quote: 여신은 숫자 6을 포함하는 3일 안에 나타난다고 믿었다. 한국인들은 우연히 그녀의 분노를 불러일으키지 않기 위해 이 3일 동안 측간을 피했다. 그래서 한국인은 음력 6일, 16일, 26일에 신발이나 아이가 측간 구덩이에 빠지면 그녀에게 제사를 지냈다. 돼지가 병에 걸려 죽었을 때, 여신의 분노에 대한 예언이 있을 때, 또는 측간이 지어졌을 때 제사도 그녀를 위해 행해졌다.

statement.id: Ritual tertentu dilakukan pada tanggal lunar enam, enam belas, dan dua puluh enam.
statement.en: Certain rites were performed on lunar days six, sixteen, and twenty-six.

claims.quote: 측신제 때 한국인들은 가능한 모든 재료를 떡 안에 넣었는데, 이 똥떡은 여신에게 바쳐졌다. 멥쌀밥도 여신에게 바쳐졌다.

statement.id: Sesaji meliputi kue beras dan nasi.
statement.en: Offerings included rice cakes and cooked rice.

claims.quote: 누군가가 세 번 기침을 하지 않고 측간에 들어오면 측신은 긴 머리를 이용해 침입자를 공격한다고 믿었다. 측신의 머리카락이 침입자의 살갗에 닿자 침입자는 병들어 죽고 만다. 무당이라도 머리카락으로 사람을 공격하면 여신을 달래지 못한다.

statement.id: Sebuah kepercayaan menyebut batuk tiga kali sebelum masuk untuk menghindari serangan rambutnya.
statement.en: One belief describes coughing three times before entry to avoid an attack with her hair.

claims.quote: 악신으로 화장실을 관장한다는 가신(家神). 뒷간귀신·부출각시(跗出閣氏).

statement.id: Cheuksin adalah gasin (dewa rumah tangga) yang dipercaya sebagai dewa jahat (aksin) penguasa jamban; ia juga disebut "dwitgan gwisin" (뒷간귀신, hantu jamban) dan "buchul gaksi" (부출각시).
statement.en: Cheuksin is a household god (gasin) believed to be an evil god (aksin) presiding over the toilet; she is also called "dwitgan gwisin" (뒷간귀신, outhouse ghost) and "buchul gaksi" (부출각시).

claims.quote: 대개 여성 신으로 머리가 길며, 성격이 포악하고 노여움을 잘 타서 두려운 존재로 여겨져 왔다. 변소에서 병을 얻거나 사고가 나는 것은 바로 이 신의 소행이라고 믿어지고 있다.

statement.id: Cheuksin pada umumnya dewi berambut panjang yang berperangai kasar dan mudah murka sehingga ditakuti; penyakit atau kecelakaan di jamban dipercaya sebagai ulahnya.
statement.en: Cheuksin is generally a long-haired female god with a fierce, easily angered temper who has been feared; illness or accidents in the toilet are believed to be her doing.

claims.quote: 일명 ‘뒷간귀신’ · ‘부출각시(跗出閣氏)’ · ‘변소각시’ · ‘칙도부인’ · ‘측신각시’ · ‘치귀’ · ‘정낭귀신’ 등으로 불린다.

statement.id: Cheuksin dikenal pula dengan nama dwitgan gwisin (뒷간귀신), buchul gaksi (부출각시), byeonso gaksi (변소각시), chikdo buin (칙도부인), cheuksin gaksi (측신각시), chigwi (치귀), dan jeongnang gwisin (정낭귀신).
statement.en: Cheuksin is also known by the names dwitgan gwisin (뒷간귀신), buchul gaksi (부출각시), byeonso gaksi (변소각시), chikdo buin (칙도부인), cheuksin gaksi (측신각시), chigwi (치귀), and jeongnang gwisin (정낭귀신).

claims.quote: 제주도 『문전본풀이』에 그 유래가 나타나는데, 집안의 각처를 관장하고 있는 신들의 형성유래담인 이 신화에 의하면, 남(南)선비의 첩인 노일제대귀일의 딸은 본부인을 죽이고 그의 일곱 아들까지 죽이려다 흉계가 드러나 측간으로 도망가 목을 매어 죽어 측도부인이 되었다고 한다.

statement.id: Asal-usulnya muncul dalam Munjeon Bonpuri (문전본풀이) dari Pulau Jeju (제주도): putri Noiljedaegwiil (노일제대귀일), selir Nam Seonbi (남선비), membunuh istri sah dan hendak membunuh tujuh putranya, tetapi rencananya terbongkar, lalu ia lari ke jamban dan gantung diri hingga menjadi Cheukdo Buin (측도부인).
statement.en: Her origin appears in the Munjeon Bonpuri (문전본풀이) of Jeju Island (제주도): the daughter of Noiljedaegwiil (노일제대귀일), concubine of Nam Seonbi (남선비), killed the first wife and tried to kill her seven sons, but her plot was exposed and she fled to the latrine, hanged herself, and became Cheukdo Buin (측도부인).

claims.quote: 본부인 조왕(竈王) ... 시앗인 측도부인은 원수간이라 하여 부엌과 측간은 멀리 짓고, 측간의 돌멩이 하나, 나무 하나라도 부엌으로 가져오지 않으며, 부엌의 물건 역시 측간에 가져가지 않는 관습이 생겼다고 한다.

statement.id: Karena istri sah Jowang (조왕, 竈王) dan selir Cheukdo Buin (측도부인) disebut bermusuhan, muncul kebiasaan membangun dapur dan jamban berjauhan serta tidak membawa batu atau kayu dari jamban ke dapur, atau barang dapur ke jamban.
statement.en: Because the first wife Jowang (조왕, 竈王) and the concubine Cheukdo Buin (측도부인) are said to be enemies, a custom arose of building the kitchen and latrine far apart and not carrying even a stone or stick from the latrine to the kitchen, or kitchen items to the latrine.

claims.quote: 측신각시는 늘 긴 머리카락을 발 밑에 감고 세고 있다가 사람이 갑자기 변소에 들어오면 깜짝 놀라서 세던 머리카락을 뒤집어 씌운다고 한다. 머리카락에 씌어진 사람은 병을 앓게 되는데, 이 측신각시는 놀라서 화가 났다 하면 무당이 굿을 하여도 잘 풀어지지 않아 대개는 죽는다고 한다.

statement.id: Cheuksin gaksi dikatakan selalu menghitung rambut panjangnya yang digulung di bawah kaki; bila seseorang mendadak masuk jamban, ia terkejut dan menyelubungkan rambutnya ke orang itu, yang lalu jatuh sakit, dan jika ia sudah marah, ritual dukun pun sulit meredakannya sehingga orang itu umumnya meninggal.
statement.en: Cheuksin gaksi is said to be always counting her long hair coiled beneath her feet; if someone enters the latrine suddenly she is startled and throws the hair over them, and the person falls ill; once she is angry even a shaman's ritual rarely appeases her and the person usually dies.

claims.quote: 그런데 측신은 늘 변소에 있는 것이 아니고 매월 6일 · 16일 · 26일과 같이 6자가 있는 날에만 나타난다고 하여, 이 날은 근신하고 금기하는 것이 좋다고 한다.

statement.id: Cheuksin tidak selalu berada di jamban tetapi dikatakan hanya muncul pada hari bertanggal ada angka 6, yaitu tanggal 6, 16, dan 26 setiap bulan, sehingga pada hari-hari itu orang sebaiknya berhati-hati dan berpantang.
statement.en: Cheuksin is not always in the latrine but is said to appear only on days containing the number 6, the 6th, 16th, and 26th of each month, so it is considered good to be cautious and observe taboos on those days.

claims.quote: 변소 출입시에 밖에서 기침을 세 번하고 들어간다거나 ... 화를 면하기 위한 방책으로 해석된다.

statement.id: Batuk tiga kali di luar sebelum memasuki jamban ditafsirkan sebagai upaya menghindari malapetaka.
statement.en: Coughing three times outside before entering the latrine is interpreted as a measure to avoid misfortune.

claims.quote: 강원도에서는 변소를 지은 뒤에 아무 탈없이 집안을 편안하게 보살펴달라는 기원에서 길일을 택하여 변소에 불을 켜놓고 제(祭)를 지낸다.

statement.id: Di Provinsi Gangwon (강원도), setelah jamban selesai dibangun dipilih hari baik untuk menyalakan lampu di jamban dan mengadakan ritual agar rumah dijaga tanpa gangguan.
statement.en: In Gangwon Province (강원도), after a latrine is built, an auspicious day is chosen to light a lamp in the latrine and hold a rite asking for the household to be cared for without mishap.

short_description.id: Coatlicue ('Rok Ular') adalah dewi ibu bumi dalam panteon Aztec. Ia digambarkan mengenakan rok ular dan kalung jantung manusia, serta menjadi ibu dari dewa perang Huitzilopochtli.
short_description.en: Coatlicue ('Serpent Skirt') is the earth-mother goddess of the Aztec pantheon. She is shown in a skirt of snakes and a necklace of human hearts, and is mother of the war god Huitzilopochtli.

long_description.id: Coatlicue adalah dewa penting dalam panteon Aztec dan dianggap sebagai dewi ibu bumi. Ia dikenal sebagai pelindung persalinan dan dikaitkan dengan perang, pemerintahan, serta pertanian. Ia juga dianggap sebagai aspek perempuan dari dewa purba Ometeotl.
long_description.en: Coatlicue was a major deity in the Aztec pantheon and was regarded as the earth-mother goddess. She presided over childbirth and was linked to war, rule, and farming. She was also considered the female aspect of the primordial god Ometeotl.

long_description.id: Coatlicue digambarkan sebagai perempuan yang mengenakan rok ular menggeliat dan kalung dari jantung, tangan, dan tengkorak manusia. Kaki dan tangannya dihiasi cakar. Penggambarannya yang paling terkenal adalah patung basal raksasa yang ditemukan di Tenochtitlan dan kini berada di Museum Nasional Antropologi di Mexico City. Pada penggambaran itu, cakar besar di tangan dan kakinya dipakai untuk mencabik mayat manusia sebelum ia memakannya.
long_description.en: Coatlicue is shown as a woman in a skirt of writhing snakes, with a necklace of human hearts, hands, and skulls and claws on her hands and feet. Her best-known depiction is the colossal basalt statue found at Tenochtitlan, today kept in the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City. In that depiction, the large claws on her hands and feet are used to rip up human corpses before she eats them.

long_description.id: Menurut mitologi Aztec, Coatlicue adalah seorang pendeta perempuan yang merawat kuil di puncak gunung suci Coatepec. Saat ia menyapu, sebuah bola bulu jatuh dari langit dan membuatnya hamil secara ajaib. Anak itu adalah Huitzilopochtli, dewa perang. Putrinya Coyolxauhqui dan 400 saudara laki-lakinya menganggap kehamilan itu aib dan berencana membunuhnya, tetapi Huitzilopochtli lahir dengan senjata lengkap dan mengalahkan mereka.
long_description.en: According to Aztec mythology, Coatlicue was a priestess who tended the shrine on top of the sacred mountain Coatepec. As she swept, a ball of feathers fell from the sky and miraculously made her pregnant. The child was Huitzilopochtli, the god of war. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui and 400 brothers saw the pregnancy as dishonor and plotted to kill her, but Huitzilopochtli emerged fully armed and defeated them.

long_description.id: Dalam mitos lain, Coatlicue memperingatkan bangsa Mexica bahwa kota-kota Aztec akan jatuh satu per satu. Ia dipuja dalam ritual Tozozontli dan perayaan Quecholli, ketika seorang peniru sang dewi dikorbankan. Menurut satu tafsiran ilmiah, ia juga memiliki aspek penciptaan yang dapat mengimbangi tengkorak, jantung, tangan, dan cakar yang menghubungkannya dengan dewa bumi Tlaltecuhtli.
long_description.en: In another myth Coatlicue warned the Mexica that the Aztec cities would fall one by one. She was worshipped in the Tozozontli ritual and the Quecholli festival, when an impersonator of the goddess was sacrificed. One scholarly reading holds that her creative side may offset the skulls, hearts, hands, and claws that tie her to the earth deity Tlaltecuhtli.

statement.en: In Aztec mythology Coatlicue was a priestess who maintained the shrine on top of the sacred mountain Coatepec; while she was sweeping, a ball of feathers descended from the heavens and, when she tucked it into her belt, miraculously impregnated her.

claims.quote: The resulting child was none other than the powerful Aztec god of war Huitzilopochtli.

statement.id: Anak yang lahir dari kehamilan itu adalah Huitzilopochtli, dewa perang Aztec yang perkasa.
statement.en: The resulting child was the powerful Aztec god of war Huitzilopochtli.

claims.quote: Rising to his mother's defence the god sprang from the womb fully grown and fully armed as an invincible warrior.

statement.id: Untuk membela ibunya, sang dewa melompat keluar dari rahim dalam keadaan dewasa penuh dan bersenjata lengkap sebagai prajurit yang tak terkalahkan.
statement.en: Rising to his mother's defence, the god sprang from the womb fully grown and fully armed as an invincible warrior.

claims.quote: Coatlicue warned the Mexica of their future demise ... the goddess revealed that the Aztec cities would fall one by one. Then, and only then, would her son Huitzilopochtli return to her side.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah mitos lain, Coatlicue memperingatkan bangsa Mexica tentang kehancuran mereka di masa depan: kota-kota Aztec akan jatuh satu per satu, dan baru setelah itu putranya, Huitzilopochtli, akan kembali ke sisinya.
statement.en: In another myth Coatlicue warned the Mexica of their future demise: the Aztec cities would fall one by one, and only then would her son Huitzilopochtli return to her side.

claims.quote: The goddess was worshipped in the spring ritual of Tozozontli in the rainy season and in the autumnal hunting festival of Quecholli, when an impersonator of the goddess was sacrificed.

statement.id: Sang dewi dipuja dalam ritual musim semi Tozozontli pada musim hujan dan dalam perayaan berburu musim gugur Quecholli, ketika seorang peniru sang dewi dikorbankan.
statement.en: The goddess was worshipped in the spring ritual of Tozozontli in the rainy season and in the autumnal hunting festival of Quecholli, when an impersonator of the goddess was sacrificed.

claims.quote: In art, Coatlicue is most famously represented in the colossal basalt statue found at Tenochtitlan which now resides in the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City.
claims.locator: How is Coatlicue Represented in Art?

statement.id: Dalam seni, Coatlicue paling terkenal digambarkan oleh patung basal raksasa yang ditemukan di Tenochtitlan dan kini berada di Museum Nasional Antropologi di Mexico City.
statement.en: In art, Coatlicue is most famously represented in the colossal basalt statue found at Tenochtitlan, which now resides in the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City.

claims.quote: She also wears her typical skirt of entwined snakes whilst her hands and feet have the large claws which she uses to rip up human corpses before she eats them.
claims.locator: How is Coatlicue Represented in Art?

statement.id: Dalam penggambaran itu, ia mengenakan rok khasnya dari ular yang terjalin, sementara tangan dan kakinya bercakar besar yang ia pakai untuk mencabik mayat manusia sebelum memakannya.
statement.en: In that depiction she wears her typical skirt of entwined snakes, and her hands and feet have large claws which she uses to rip up human corpses before she eats them.

claims.quote: Interpreting this as dishonor, her daughter Coyolxauhqui, along with her 400 brothers, plotted to kill her. Just as the attack began, Huitzilopochtli emerged fully armed from his mother, defeated his siblings, and cast Coyolxauhqui into the sky, where she became the moon.

statement.id: Menganggap kehamilan itu sebagai aib, putrinya Coyolxauhqui bersama 400 saudara laki-lakinya merencanakan pembunuhan terhadap ibu mereka. Saat serangan dimulai, Huitzilopochtli keluar dengan senjata lengkap dari tubuh ibunya, mengalahkan saudara-saudaranya, dan melempar Coyolxauhqui ke langit, tempat ia menjadi bulan.
statement.en: Interpreting this as dishonor, her daughter Coyolxauhqui, along with her 400 brothers, plotted to kill her; as the attack began, Huitzilopochtli emerged fully armed from his mother, defeated his siblings, and cast Coyolxauhqui into the sky, where she became the moon.

Tidak dicari sumber budaya populer modern untuk entri core ini.

short_description.id: El Cuero ("kulit") adalah makhluk air dari mitologi Mapuche yang tinggal di kedalaman sungai dan laguna [cuero-legendary-creature-c01, cuero-legendary-creature-c03].
short_description.en: El Cuero ("the hide") is an aquatic creature of Mapuche mythology dwelling in the depths of rivers and lagoons [cuero-legendary-creature-c01, cuero-legendary-creature-c03].

long_description.id: El Cuero adalah makhluk air dari mitologi Mapuche yang kemudian masuk ke mitos Chile tengah dan selatan serta sebagian Argentina [cuero-legendary-creature-c01]. Ia juga disebut cuero del agua atau cuero vivo, "kulit hidup" [cuero-legendary-creature-c02], dan tinggal di kedalaman sungai dan laguna [cuero-legendary-creature-c03].
long_description.en: El Cuero is an aquatic creature of Mapuche mythology later absorbed into the myths of central and southern Chile and parts of southwest Argentina [cuero-legendary-creature-c01]. It is also called cuero del agua or cuero vivo, "live hide" [cuero-legendary-creature-c02], and dwells in the depths of rivers and lagoons [cuero-legendary-creature-c03].

long_description.id: Kebanyakan sumber menggambarkannya seperti kulit sapi terbentang yang menyelubungi mangsa, dan banyak yang menyebutnya gurita atau sotong [cuero-legendary-creature-c04]. Sebuah kamus mitologi menyebutnya hewan fantastis penghuni laguna dan sungai Chile selatan yang tampil seperti kulit sapi mengambang di antara dua lapisan air [cuero-legendary-creature-c14], dan sebagian menggambarkannya bermata di sepanjang tepinya [cuero-legendary-creature-c15]. Sebagai Manta, ia mengincar manusia dan hewan yang masuk ke air, membelit, lalu menyeretnya ke dasar [cuero-legendary-creature-c05].
long_description.en: Most sources describe it as an outstretched cowhide that envelops its prey, and many call it an octopus or cuttlefish [cuero-legendary-creature-c04]. A mythology dictionary calls it a fabulous animal of the lagoons and rivers of southern Chile that appears as a bovine hide floating between two layers of water [cuero-legendary-creature-c14], and some describe it with eyes along its edges [cuero-legendary-creature-c15]. As the Manta, it targets humans and animals entering the water, wraps around them and drags them to the bottom [cuero-legendary-creature-c05].

long_description.id: Trelquehuecuve berjemur di tepi air dan membangkitkan pusaran untuk kembali ke dalam air [cuero-legendary-creature-c06]. Dalam legenda setempat, orang yang menginjaknya merasa pusing lalu diselubungi dan dibawa ke kedalaman [cuero-legendary-creature-c07]. Untuk mengalahkannya mungkin diperlukan bantuan machi dengan semak calafate berduri [cuero-legendary-creature-c08], atau umpan semak quisco [cuero-legendary-creature-c09]; dalam satu kisah, Ñanco mengalahkannya dengan kaktus quisco yang diikat ke lengan dan kakinya [cuero-legendary-creature-c10].
long_description.en: The Trelquehuecuve sunbathes at the water's edge and raises a whirlpool to return to the water [cuero-legendary-creature-c06]. In a local legend, whoever steps on it feels dizzy, is enveloped and is carried to the depths [cuero-legendary-creature-c07]. Defeating it may require a machi's help with the thorny calafate bush [cuero-legendary-creature-c08], or a quisco bush lure [cuero-legendary-creature-c09]; in one tale, Ñanco defeats it with quisco cacti tied to his arms and legs [cuero-legendary-creature-c10].

long_description.id: Sebagian orang menduga mitos ini berasal dari fenomena remolino [cuero-legendary-creature-c11] atau terkait pari manta [cuero-legendary-creature-c12]. El Cuero kadang tertukar dengan Guirivilo [cuero-legendary-creature-c13].
long_description.en: Some suggest the myth originated from the remolino phenomenon [cuero-legendary-creature-c11] or is connected to the manta ray [cuero-legendary-creature-c12]. El Cuero is sometimes confused with the Guirivilo [cuero-legendary-creature-c13].

claims.quote: is an aquatic creature from Mapuche mythology subsequently incorporated into the myth of Central Chile (including Chiloé Islands) and Southern Chile, and certain parts of southwest Argentina.

statement.id: El Cuero adalah makhluk air dari mitologi Mapuche yang kemudian masuk ke mitos Chile tengah dan selatan serta sebagian Argentina barat daya.
statement.en: El Cuero is an aquatic creature of Mapuche mythology later absorbed into the myths of central and southern Chile and parts of southwest Argentina.

claims.quote: This also called cuero del agua or cuero de agua. or colloquially cuero vivo ("live hide").

statement.id: Ia juga disebut cuero del agua atau cuero vivo ("kulit hidup").
statement.en: It is also called cuero del agua or cuero vivo ("live hide").

claims.quote: El Cuero dwells in the depths of rivers and lagoons.

statement.id: El Cuero tinggal di kedalaman sungai dan laguna.
statement.en: El Cuero dwells in the depths of rivers and lagoons.

claims.quote: Most sources agree in describing El Cuero as resembling an outstretched cowhide (or calfskin, or donkey hide come to life) which envelops its prey, and many sources call it an octopus (Spanish: pulpo), or cuttlefish (Spanish: jibia).

statement.id: Kebanyakan sumber menggambarkan El Cuero seperti kulit sapi yang terbentang (atau kulit anak sapi, atau kulit keledai yang hidup) yang menyelubungi mangsanya, dan banyak sumber menyebutnya gurita (pulpo) atau sotong (jibia).
statement.en: Most sources describe El Cuero as resembling an outstretched cowhide (or calfskin, or a donkey hide come to life) that envelops its prey, and many sources call it an octopus (pulpo) or cuttlefish (jibia).

claims.quote: The Manta targets humans and animals entering water, wraps around, and drags its prey to the bottom of the water.

statement.id: Manta mengincar manusia dan hewan yang masuk ke air, membelit, lalu menyeret mangsanya ke dasar air.
statement.en: The Manta targets humans and animals entering the water, wraps around them and drags its prey to the bottom.

claims.quote: The "Trelquehuecuve" evidently engages in sunbathing on the beach: it crawls out to the edge of a river or lagoon to receive the warmth of sunlight, and when it wishes to return, it raises a whirwind or whirpool which will shove it back into water.

statement.id: "Trelquehuecuve" tampaknya berjemur: ia merangkak ke tepi sungai atau laguna untuk menerima hangat matahari, dan bila ingin kembali ia membangkitkan angin puyuh atau pusaran yang mendorongnya kembali ke air.
statement.en: The "Trelquehuecuve" evidently sunbathes: it crawls to the edge of a river or lagoon to receive the sun's warmth, and when it wishes to return it raises a whirlwind or whirlpool that shoves it back into the water.

claims.quote: When one steps on it, there is a mossy feel, but then experiences dizziness (or drowsiness), and the pelt monster flips up its sides equipped with numerous sharp nails and claws, and envelops the victim, carrying him to the depths.

statement.id: Menurut legenda setempat, orang yang menginjaknya merasakan sensasi berlumut lalu pusing (atau mengantuk), dan monster kulit itu membalikkan sisi-sisinya yang berkuku dan bercakar tajam, menyelubungi korban, dan membawanya ke kedalaman.
statement.en: In a local legend, whoever steps on it feels something mossy and then dizziness (or drowsiness), and the pelt monster flips up its sides, which have numerous sharp nails and claws, envelops the victim and carries him to the depths.

claims.quote: But to defeat a cuero, the help of a machi wise woman may be required. The machi will use a method similar to the one already described, plunging the thorny bush of the calafate  (Berberis microphylla, Magellan barberry) and the cuero will pounce on it mistaking it for food prey, is damaged by the thorns as it squeezes, and it dies.

statement.id: Untuk mengalahkan cuero mungkin diperlukan bantuan seorang machi, perempuan bijak; machi menancapkan semak berduri calafate, cuero menerkamnya karena mengira itu mangsa, terluka oleh durinya saat meremas, lalu mati.
statement.en: Defeating a cuero may require the help of a machi, a wise woman; the machi plunges in the thorny calafate bush, the cuero pounces on it mistaking it for prey, is damaged by the thorns as it squeezes, and dies.

claims.quote: The traditional capturing method use a sort of natural fishing lure using a "thorny bush" known in Chile as quisco, which usually refers to the cactus Echinopsis chiloensis

statement.id: Cara penangkapan tradisional memakai semacam umpan alami berupa "semak berduri" yang di Chile disebut quisco, yang biasanya merujuk pada kaktus Echinopsis chiloensis.
statement.en: The traditional capturing method uses a sort of natural fishing lure made of a "thorny bush" known in Chile as quisco, which usually refers to the cactus Echinopsis chiloensis.

claims.quote: In the story "The indio and the cuero", the hero Ñanco defeats the cuero by fighting it with bunches of quisco cacti tied to his arms and legs, and the monster bled out to death.

statement.id: Dalam kisah "The indio and the cuero", sang pahlawan Ñanco mengalahkan cuero dengan melawannya memakai ikatan kaktus quisco di lengan dan kakinya, dan monster itu mati kehabisan darah.
statement.en: In the story "The indio and the cuero", the hero Ñanco defeats the cuero by fighting it with bunches of quisco cacti tied to his arms and legs, and the monster bleeds to death.

claims.quote: The myth may have originated from the phenomenon of the remolino (whirpool, whirlwind).

statement.id: Mitos ini mungkin berasal dari fenomena remolino (pusaran air atau angin puyuh).
statement.en: The myth may have originated from the phenomenon of the remolino (whirlpool, whirlwind).

claims.quote: Some have suggested the myth of "La Manta" may be connected to the manta ray or some other large ray.

statement.id: Sebagian orang mengusulkan bahwa mitos "La Manta" mungkin terkait dengan pari manta atau pari besar lain.
statement.en: Some have suggested the myth of "La Manta" may be connected to the manta ray or some other large ray.

claims.quote: El Cuero is sometimes confused with the Guirivilo (nguruvilu), the "fox-serpent".

statement.id: El Cuero kadang tertukar dengan Guirivilo (nguruvilu), "ular-rubah".
statement.en: El Cuero is sometimes confused with the Guirivilo (nguruvilu), the "fox-serpent".

statement.en: According to this mythology dictionary, the manta is a fabulous animal that lives in lagoons and rivers of southern Chile and appears as the hide of a bovine floating between two layers of water.

claims.quote: Algunos lo describen con ojos en todos sus bordes.

statement.id: Menurut kamus mitologi ini, sebagian orang menggambarkannya bermata di sepanjang tepinya.

short_description.id: Dakuwaqa adalah dewa hiu dalam mitologi Fiji yang tampil sebagai monster laut garang, menjaga kepulauan, dan dihormati nelayan karena melindungi mereka dari bahaya di laut.
short_description.en: Dakuwaqa is a shark god of Fijian mythology who appears as a fierce sea monster, guards the islands, and was respected by fishermen as their protector at sea.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Fiji, Dakuwaqa (juga ditulis Dakuwanga) adalah dewa hiu yang sering tampil sebagai monster laut yang garang dan menjaga kepulauan. Ia sangat dihormati nelayan karena melindungi mereka dari setiap bahaya di laut dan para penghuninya. Namanya berarti "bagian belakang perahu"; sebuah museum menyebutnya salah satu dari dua dewa hiu leluhur Fiji yang namanya dikaitkan dengan perahu dan layar.
long_description.en: In Fijian mythology Dakuwaqa (also written Dakuwanga) is a shark god who often appears as a fierce sea monster guarding the islands. Fishermen held him in great respect because he protected them from every danger at sea and its creatures. His name means "back of the boat"; a museum lists him as one of two ancestral shark gods of Fiji whose names are linked to boats and sails.

long_description.id: Dakuwaqa dapat mengubah wujud menjadi apa pun, tetapi wujud aslinya adalah lelaki Fiji yang berotot dengan tubuh bagian atas hiu. Seorang warga desa menuturkan bahwa setiap kali Dakuwaqa datang ke desa, ia menjelma manusia.
long_description.en: Dakuwaqa can take any shape, but his real form is a muscular Fijian man with the upper body of a shark. A villager says that whenever Dakuwaqa comes to the village he turns himself into a human.

long_description.id: Dalam satu mitos penciptaan, Dakuwaqa berencana menaklukkan Pulau Kadavu lewat sungai, tetapi dewi Rokobakaniceva menantangnya dalam wujud gurita. Gurita itu mencabut giginya dengan delapan lengan, menahan serangannya, dan memaksa Dakuwaqa berjanji tidak menyerang Kadavu lagi; demikianlah Dakuwaqa menjadi dewa dan pelindung Kadavu.
long_description.en: In one creation myth Dakuwaqa planned to take Kadavu Island by way of the river, but the goddess Rokobakaniceva challenged him as an octopus. She pulled out his teeth with her arms, held off his assault, and made him promise never to attack Kadavu again; so Dakuwaqa became the god and protector of Kadavu.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan itu hidup di masa modern. Sebuah catatan abad kedua puluh menggambarkan ikan besar berkepala hiu dan berekor paus yang nyaris membalikkan sebuah kapal; awak Fiji menuangkan kava ke laut dan menyebutnya Dakuwaqa. Menurut museum itu, Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, presiden pertama Fiji setelah kemerdekaan, adalah keturunan Dakuwaqa, dan para pelayat melaporkan kawanan hiu mengiringi kapal pemakamannya ke laut.
long_description.en: The belief has stayed alive. A twentieth-century account describes a huge fish, shark-headed and whale-tailed, nearly capsizing a ship; the Fijian crew poured kava into the sea and called it Dakuwaqa. According to the museum, Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, Fiji's first president after independence, descends from Dakuwaqa, and mourners reported sharks escorting the vessel carrying him out to sea.

cultural_context.id: Menurut seorang warga desa, hiu telah menjadi bagian budaya mereka sejak sebelum Kristen, dan desanya memilih hiu sebagai dewa laut yang disembah saat mereka membutuhkan sesuatu.
cultural_context.en: A villager says that sharks have been part of their culture since before Christianity and that his village chose the shark as a sea god worshipped when they need something.
