short_description.id: Daramulum adalah pahlawan langit dalam budaya Aboriginal di Australia tenggara yang dikaitkan dengan Baiame; suaranya diyakini terdengar lewat bullroarer dalam upacara inisiasi.
short_description.en: Daramulum is a sky hero of the Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, associated with Baiame; his voice is said to be heard through the bullroarer at initiation ceremonies.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya Aboriginal di Australia tenggara, Daramulum adalah pahlawan langit yang dikaitkan dengan Baiame dan seorang istri emu, serta disebut pengubah wujud. Menurut catatan Howitt, kepercayaan kepada Daramulun, sang "bapa", dan Biamban, sang "tuan", dimiliki semua suku yang menghadiri Kuringal Yuin, dan agama yang berpusat pada Darhumulan menjadi ciri pengenal bangsa Yuin.
long_description.en: In the Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, Daramulum is a sky hero associated with Baiame and an emu-wife, and is described as a shapeshifter. In Howitt's record, belief in Daramulun, the "father", and Biamban, the "master", is shared by all the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal, and the Yuin nation is marked out by a religion built around Darhumulan.

long_description.id: Suaranya terdengar melalui bullroarer yang diputar di udara dalam upacara inisiasi. Suku Yuin percaya guntur adalah suara Daramulun, dan anak-anak laki-laki diberi tahu bahwa ia akan melukai atau membunuh mereka jika membocorkan rahasia upacara.
long_description.en: His voice can be heard through the bullroarer whirled through the air during initiation ceremonies. The Yuin believe thunder is the voice of Daramulun, and boys are warned that he will harm or kill them should they reveal the secrets.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu catatan Howitt, figur Daramulun digambar di tanah sebagai "anak" Baiame yang berkaki satu, lengkap dengan kapak yang ia jatuhkan dan jejak kaki emu. Pada seni cadas di Taman Nasional Ku-ring-gai Chase ia digambarkan setengah profil dengan satu lengan, punggung emu, dan kaki besar, di dekat ukiran istri emu-nya; bagi suku Guringai ia diwakili bintang Alpha Crucis dari Salib Selatan.
long_description.en: In one of Howitt's accounts, a figure of Daramulun is cut on the ground as the one-legged "boy" of Baiame, together with the tomahawk he let fall and emu footprints. In rock art in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park he is shown in semi-profile with one arm, an emu-back and a large foot, near a carving of his emu-wife; for the Guringai he is represented by Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross.

long_description.id: Suku Ngarigo mengira roh orang mati naik ke langit dan disambut Daramulun, yang merawatnya. Dukun di mana-mana dipercaya menerima kekuatannya dari makhluk gaib seperti Baiame, Daramulun, atau Bunjil, dan satu bagian menyebut Daramulun tinggal di pohon dengan pembengkakan besar di sekeliling akarnya. Howitt sendiri menulis bahwa tidak ada pemujaan terhadap Daramulun, dan menganggap beberapa nama dewa dari berbagai suku mewakili satu sosok.
long_description.en: The Ngarigo thought the spirit of a dead person went up to the sky and was met by Daramulun, who takes care of it. Medicine-men are everywhere believed to receive their power from supernatural beings such as Baiame, Daramulun or Bunjil, and one passage says Daramulun lives in a tree with a great swelling round its roots. Howitt himself writes that there is not any worship of Daramulun, and regards several divine names from different tribes as representing one being.

statement.en: Daramulum is depicted on rock art off Elvina Track in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park, near to a carving of his emu-wife.

claims.quote: For the Guringai, Daramulum is represented by the Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross, with the remainder of the Cross representing the head of his emu wife

statement.id: Bagi suku Guringai, Daramulum diwakili oleh bintang Alpha Crucis dari Salib Selatan, dan sisa rasi itu melambangkan kepala istri emu-nya.
statement.en: For the Guringai, Daramulum is represented by Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross, with the rest of the Cross representing the head of his emu wife.

claims.quote: A religion centred on Darhumulan is an identifying feature of the Yuin nation.

statement.id: Agama yang berpusat pada Darhumulan (ejaan lain nama ini) menjadi ciri pengenal bangsa Yuin.
statement.en: A religion centred on Darhumulan (a variant spelling of the name) is an identifying feature of the Yuin nation.

claims.quote: The belief in Daramulun, the " father," and Biamban, or " master," is common to all of the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal.

statement.id: Kepercayaan kepada Daramulun, sang "bapa", dan Biamban, sang "tuan", dimiliki semua suku yang menghadiri Kuringal Yuin.
statement.en: Belief in Daramulun, the "father", and Biamban, the "master", is shared by all the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal.

claims.quote: The Yuin believe that the thunder is the voice of Daramulun.

statement.id: Suku Yuin percaya bahwa guntur adalah suara Daramulun.
statement.en: The Yuin believe that thunder is the voice of Daramulun.

claims.quote: Their neighbours the Ngarigo also thought that the spirit of a dead person ... went up to the sky, where it was met by Daramulun, who, as one of the old Ngarigo men said, takes care of it.

statement.id: Suku Ngarigo juga mengira roh orang mati naik ke langit, tempat ia disambut Daramulun, yang menurut seorang tetua Ngarigo merawatnya.
statement.en: The Ngarigo also thought that the spirit of a dead person went up to the sky, where it was met by Daramulun, who, as an old Ngarigo man said, takes care of it.

claims.quote: The general belief as to the powers of the medicine-man are much the same in all the tribes herein spoken of. He is everywhere believed to have received his dreaded power from some supernatural source, or being, such as Baiame, Daramulun, or Bunjil, or the ancestral ghosts.

statement.id: Dukun (medicine-man) di mana-mana dipercaya menerima kekuatannya dari sumber atau makhluk gaib seperti Baiame, Daramulun, atau Bunjil, atau dari hantu leluhur.
statement.en: The medicine-man is everywhere believed to have received his dreaded power from a supernatural source or being such as Baiame, Daramulun or Bunjil, or from the ancestral ghosts.

claims.quote: a tree with a great swelling round its roots. It is in such places that Daramulun lives.

statement.id: Menurut bagian ini, Daramulun tinggal di tempat-tempat semacam itu, yaitu pohon dengan pembengkakan besar di sekeliling akarnya.
statement.en: According to this passage, Daramulun lives in such places, namely a tree with a great swelling round its roots.

claims.quote: they cut on the ground the figure of Daramulun, who is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs, but the " boy," or son, of Baiame. He is always represented as having only one leg, the other terminating in a sharp point of bone.

statement.id: Dalam bagian ini, figur Daramulun digambar di tanah; ia di sini bukan Makhluk Gaib dalam kepercayaan Yuin melainkan "anak" atau putra Baiame, dan selalu digambarkan berkaki satu dengan ujung lainnya runcing dari tulang.
statement.en: In this passage a figure of Daramulun is cut on the ground; here he is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs but the "boy", or son, of Baiame, and is always shown with one leg, the other ending in a sharp point of bone.

claims.quote: There is also figured on the ground the tomahawk which Daramulun let fall as he slipped down from the tree before mentioned to the ground ; then two footprints of an emu a little distance from each other, made when trying to escape from Daramulun.

statement.id: Di tanah juga digambar kapak yang dijatuhkan Daramulun ketika ia meluncur turun dari pohon ke tanah, lalu dua jejak kaki emu yang dibuat saat mencoba lolos dari Daramulun.
statement.en: Also figured on the ground are the tomahawk Daramulun let fall as he slipped down from the tree to the ground, and two emu footprints made when the emu tried to escape from Daramulun.

claims.quote: to imitate the bursting of stones heated in the fire, with which the boys are told Daramulun will injure or kill them if they tell any of the secrets.

statement.id: Anak-anak laki-laki diberi tahu bahwa Daramulun akan melukai atau membunuh mereka dengan batu yang dipanaskan di api jika mereka membocorkan rahasia.
statement.en: The boys are told that Daramulun will injure or kill them with stones heated in the fire if they tell any of the secrets.

claims.quote: There is not any worship of Daramulun

statement.id: Howitt menulis bahwa tidak ada pemujaan terhadap Daramulun.
statement.en: Howitt writes that there is not any worship of Daramulun.

claims.quote: It seems quite clear that Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun, and Baianie all represent the same being under different names.

statement.id: Howitt menyimpulkan bahwa Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun, dan Baianie semuanya mewakili satu sosok yang sama dengan nama berbeda.
statement.en: Howitt concludes that Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun and Baianie all represent the same being under different names.

summary.id: Dalam satu catatan, Daramulun bukan Makhluk Gaib dalam kepercayaan Yuin melainkan putra Baiame.
summary.en: In one account Daramulun is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs but the son of Baiame.

summary.id: Howitt menyimpulkan beberapa nama, termasuk Daramulun dan Baianie, mewakili satu sosok yang sama.
summary.en: Howitt concludes that several names, including Daramulun and Baianie, represent one and the same being.

gaps.searched: Makna "berkaki satu" dan ejaan lain (Darhumulan, Daramulan) hanya ada di bagian Wikipedia bertanda citation needed; Howitt (1904) tidak memberi asal kata, sehingga etimologi dikosongkan.

short_description.id: Daucina (juga ditulis Ndauthina) adalah dewa pelayaran dan penangkapan ikan di Fiji, dikenal sebagai sang pembawa obor yang berkeliaran di terumbu dengan kerudung api.
short_description.en: Daucina, also written Ndauthina, is the god of seafaring and fishing in Fiji, known as the torch-bearer who roams the reefs hooded with fire.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Fiji, Daucina berarti sang pembawa obor dan dikenal sebagai dewa agung pelayaran. Menurut Thomson, yang menulis namanya Ndauthina, ia adalah dewa komunitas pelaut dan nelayan di seluruh Fiji. Nelayan yang karam dikatakan selalu dapat berlindung di kuil yang dipersembahkan kepadanya.
long_description.en: In Fijian mythology Daucina means the torch-bearer and is known as the great god of seafaring. According to Thomson, who writes the name Ndauthina, he is the god of the seafaring and fishing community throughout Fiji. A shipwrecked fisherman was said always to find refuge in a temple dedicated to him.

long_description.id: Saat masih balita ia hanya tenang bila menatap lampu, sehingga ibunya mengikatkan alang-alang bernyala di kepalanya. Sejak itu ia berkeliaran di terumbu karang, pada malam hari, berkerudung tungku menyala.
long_description.en: As a toddler he was quiet only when looking at a lamp, so his mother tied burning reeds to his head. Since then he is said to roam the reefs by night, hooded with a flaming brazier.

long_description.id: Ia disebut pelindung para pezina dan pembawa pergi perempuan pada malam hari. Ia juga menyukai serangan malam dan menyorotkan cahaya ke pertahanan untuk memandu pengepung, tetapi tidak berbuat jahil terhadap para nelayan sahabatnya, yang diberinya angin baik dan tangkapan yang bagus.
long_description.en: He is called the patron of adulterers and a carrier-off of women at night. He also loves night attacks, flashing light on defences to guide besiegers, yet plays no pranks on his friends the fishermen, to whom he gives fair winds and good catches.

short_description.id: Degei (Ndengei) adalah dewa tertinggi Fiji yang berwujud ular, pencipta dunia, buah-buahan, dan manusia, serta pengadil arwah orang mati.
short_description.en: Degei (Ndengei) is the supreme god of Fiji, enshrined as a serpent, creator of the world, fruits and men, and judge of the newly dead.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Fiji, Degei (dilafalkan Ndengei) berwujud ular dan dikenal sebagai dewa tertinggi Fiji. Ia pencipta dunia, buah-buahan, dan manusia, dan terutama berhubungan dengan wilayah Rakiraki. Satu catatan menyebut seekor burung bertelur dua yang dierami Ndengei, sang ular agung, lalu seorang anak laki-laki dan seorang anak perempuan keluar dari telur-telur itu.
long_description.en: In Fijian mythology Degei (pronounced Ndengei) is enshrined as a serpent and known as the supreme god of Fiji. He is the creator of the world, fruits and men, and is specially connected to Rakiraki. One record says a bird laid two eggs that Ndengei, the great serpent, hatched, a boy and a girl coming from them.

long_description.id: Menurut tradisi, ia mula-mula bergerak bebas, lalu dalam wujud ular tumbuh menyatu dengan bumi dan sejak itu menjadi dewa gempa bumi, badai, dan musim. Bila ia mengguncang dirinya, hujan penyubur turun dan ladang ubi berhasil; ia juga dewa murka yang menghukum umatnya dengan merusak panen atau banjir.
long_description.en: Tradition says he first moved about freely, then in snake form grew into the earth and has since been the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons. When he shakes himself fertilising rain falls and the yam fields prosper; he is also a god of wrath who punishes his people by destroying the crops or by floods.

long_description.id: Arwah orang yang baru meninggal melewati salah satu dari dua gua, Cibaciba atau Drakulu, sebelum dihakimi Degei. Beberapa arwah dikirim ke surga Burotu, dan sebagian besar lainnya dilemparkan ke danau tempat mereka akhirnya tenggelam ke dasar (Murimuria) untuk diganjar atau dihukum.
long_description.en: Newly dead souls pass through one of two caves, Cibaciba or Drakulu, before Degei judges them. He sends a few to the paradise Burotu; most others are cast into a lake and gradually sink to its bottom (Murimuria), where they are rewarded or punished as fits.

long_description.id: Sebuah catatan lain menggambarkan Ndengei sebagai wujud gagasan keberadaan abadi yang hidup monoton di gua suram dekat ujung timur laut Viti Levu, hanya makan, menjawab imamnya, dan berganti posisi. Walaupun tertinggi di antara para dewa, di luar sekitar Rakiraki ia nyaris tidak punya kuil; Tokairambe dan Tui Lakemba Randinandina disebut putra-putranya yang menjadi perantara doa. Ular adalah kuil pilihannya, dan sebagian tradisi menggambarkannya dengan kepala dan sebagian tubuh ular sedangkan sisanya batu. Adat merajah tubuh konon sesuai dengan ketetapan Ndengei.
long_description.en: Another account describes Ndengei as an impersonation of the idea of eternal existence, living a monotonous life in a gloomy cavern near the north-east end of Viti Levu, eating, answering his priest and changing position. Although supreme among the gods, he has scarcely a temple except about Rakiraki; Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina are named as his sons and mediators. The serpent is his adopted shrine, some traditions show him with the head and part of the body of a snake and the rest stone, and the custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with his appointment.

description.id: Puncak paling utara Pegunungan Nakauvandra, tempat gua ular raksasa itu menurut tradisi yang dikutip.
description.en: The northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range, near whose summit the huge snake lives in a cave according to the traditions quoted.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa ular dapat menjadi lambang keabadian dalam kepercayaan Fiji?
learning_questions.en: Why might the serpent serve as a symbol of eternity in Fijian belief?

sources.author: Thomas Williams

claims.quote: In Fijian mythology, Degei (pronounced Ndengei), enshrined as a serpent, is the supreme god of Fiji.

statement.id: Degei yang berwujud ular adalah dewa tertinggi dalam mitologi Fiji.
statement.en: Degei, enshrined as a serpent, is the supreme deity of Fiji.

claims.quote: He is the creator of the (Fijian) world, fruits, and of men and is specially connected to Rakiraki District, Fiji.

statement.id: Degei adalah pencipta bumi, buah-buahan, dan manusia di Fiji.
statement.en: He is the creator of the world, fruits, and humans in Fiji.

claims.quote: He judges newly dead souls after they pass through one of two caves: Cibaciba or Drakulu.

statement.id: Degei mengadili jiwa-jiwa yang baru wafat setelah melewati gua Cibaciba atau Drakulu.
statement.en: He judges departed souls after they pass through Cibaciba or Drakulu caves.

claims.quote: He is said to have at first moved about freely, but then in the form of a snake to have grown into the earth with his ringed tail. Since then he has become the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons.

statement.id: Ia dikatakan mula-mula bergerak bebas, tetapi lalu dalam wujud ular tumbuh menyatu dengan bumi bersama ekornya yang berlingkar; sejak itu ia menjadi dewa gempa bumi, badai, dan musim.
statement.en: He is said to have first moved about freely, but then, in snake form, to have grown into the earth with his ringed tail; since then he has become the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons.

claims.quote: Whenever Degei shakes himself fertilising rain will fall, delicious fruits hang on the trees, and the yam fields yield an excellent crop.

statement.id: Setiap kali Degei mengguncang dirinya, hujan penyubur turun, buah-buahan lezat bergantung di pohon, dan ladang ubi memberi hasil yang sangat baik.
statement.en: Whenever Degei shakes himself, fertilising rain falls, delicious fruits hang on the trees and the yam fields yield an excellent crop.

claims.quote: Degei is also a god of wrath who declares himself in terrible fashion. He punishes and chastens his people by destroying the crops or by floods; he could indeed easily wipe out mankind from the earth, for since he has lived in the bowels of the earth he has been tormented with so insatiable hunger that he would like to take in and swallow the whole world.

statement.id: Degei juga dewa murka yang menyatakan diri secara mengerikan; ia menghukum umatnya dengan merusak panen atau dengan banjir, dan karena tinggal di perut bumi ia disiksa lapar yang tak terpuaskan sehingga ingin menelan seluruh dunia.
statement.en: Degei is also a god of wrath who declares himself in terrible fashion; he punishes his people by destroying the crops or by floods, and having lived in the bowels of the earth he is tormented by so insatiable a hunger that he would like to swallow the whole world.

claims.quote: Rokola is a name of the son of Degei.

statement.id: Rokola adalah nama putra Degei.
statement.en: Rokola is a name of the son of Degei.

claims.quote: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people, but also as a huge snake, living in a cave near the summit of the mountain Uluda - the northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range.
claims.locator: In popular culture (quoting R. A. Derrick)

statement.id: Dalam tradisi-tradisi ini Degei tampil bukan hanya sebagai asal usul manusia, tetapi juga sebagai ular raksasa yang tinggal di gua dekat puncak gunung Uluda, puncak paling utara Pegunungan Nakauvandra.
statement.en: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people but also as a huge snake living in a cave near the summit of the mountain Uluda, the northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range.

claims.quote: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people, but also as a huge snake ... He took no interest in his people's affairs; his existence was no more than a round of eating and sleeping.
claims.locator: In popular culture (quoting R. A. Derrick)

statement.id: Menurut kutipan di halaman ini, ia tidak tertarik pada urusan umatnya; keberadaannya hanya berputar pada makan dan tidur.
statement.en: According to the passage quoted on this page, he took no interest in his people's affairs; his existence was no more than a round of eating and sleeping.

claims.quote: The god most generally known in Fiji is Ndengei, who seems to be an impersonation of the abstract idea of eternal existence.

statement.id: Dewa yang paling dikenal di Fiji adalah Ndengei, yang tampaknya merupakan personifikasi gagasan abstrak tentang keberadaan abadi.
statement.en: The god most generally known in Fiji is Ndengei, who seems to be an impersonation of the abstract idea of eternal existence.

claims.quote: The serpent - the world-wide symbol of eternity - is his adopted shrine. Some traditions represent him with the head and part of the body of that reptile, the rest of his form being stone

statement.id: Ular, lambang keabadian di seluruh dunia, adalah kuil pilihannya; sebagian tradisi menggambarkannya dengan kepala dan sebagian tubuh ular sedangkan sisanya batu.
statement.en: The serpent, the world-wide symbol of eternity, is his adopted shrine; some traditions represent him with the head and part of the body of that reptile, the rest of his form being stone.

claims.quote: He passes a monotonous existence in a gloomy cavern - the hollow of an inland rock near the N. E. end of Viti Levu - evincing no interest in any one but his attendant, Uto, and giving no signs of life beyond eating, answering his priest, and changing his position from one side to the other.

statement.id: Ia menjalani hidup monoton di gua suram, rongga batu pedalaman dekat ujung timur laut Viti Levu, tidak peduli pada siapa pun selain pelayannya Uto, dan hanya makan, menjawab imamnya, dan berganti posisi dari satu sisi ke sisi lain.
statement.en: He passes a monotonous existence in a gloomy cavern, the hollow of an inland rock near the north-east end of Viti Levu, showing no interest in anyone but his attendant Uto, and giving no sign of life beyond eating, answering his priest and changing his position from side to side.

claims.quote: All though Ndengei ranks as supreme among the gods ... Except about Rakiraki, he has scarcely a temple

statement.id: Meski Ndengei dianggap tertinggi di antara para dewa, di luar sekitar Rakiraki ia nyaris tidak punya kuil.
statement.en: Although Ndengei ranks as supreme among the gods, he has scarcely a temple except about Rakiraki.

claims.quote: Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina seem to stand next to Ndengei, being his sons, and acting as mediators

statement.id: Tokairambe dan Tui Lakemba Randinandina tampaknya berkedudukan tepat di bawah Ndengei sebagai putra-putranya dan bertindak sebagai perantara.
statement.en: Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina seem to stand next to Ndengei, being his sons, and act as mediators.

claims.quote: On the day of offering a priest entered the sacred cave where Ndengei dwelt, taking with him what the occasion required.

statement.id: Pada hari persembahan, seorang imam masuk ke gua suci tempat Ndengei bersemayam sambil membawa apa yang dibutuhkan upacara.
statement.en: On the day of offering a priest entered the sacred cave where Ndengei dwelt, taking with him what the occasion required.

claims.quote: If rain was wanted, the bete would return dripping with rain from Ndengei, and with a promise that he would thus bestow showers on all the district after two or four days. If they asked success in war, a fire-brand was darted from the cave ; a token that they should burn up their enemies.

statement.id: Bila hujan diminta, bete (imam) kembali basah kuyup dari Ndengei dengan janji hujan dalam dua atau empat hari; bila diminta kemenangan perang, sebatang bara dilemparkan dari gua sebagai tanda musuh akan dibakar habis.
statement.en: If rain was wanted, the bete (priest) would return dripping from Ndengei with a promise of showers on the district after two or four days; if success in war was asked, a fire-brand was darted from the cave as a token that they should burn up their enemies.

claims.quote: The custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with the appointment of Ndengei, and its neglect punished after death.

statement.id: Adat merajah tubuh konon sesuai dengan ketetapan Ndengei, dan pengabaiannya dihukum setelah mati.
statement.en: The custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with the appointment of Ndengei, and its neglect punished after death.

claims.quote: At the other extremity of Melanesia, in Fiji, it is said that a bird laid two eggs which were hatched by Ndengei, the great serpent, a boy coming from one and a girl from the other.

statement.id: Di Fiji dikatakan seekor burung bertelur dua yang dierami oleh Ndengei, sang ular agung; seorang anak laki-laki keluar dari satu telur dan seorang anak perempuan dari yang lain.
statement.en: In Fiji it is said that a bird laid two eggs that were hatched by Ndengei, the great serpent, a boy coming from one and a girl from the other.

claims.quote: A few he sends to paradise Burotu. Most others are thrown into a lake, where they will eventually sink to the bottom (Murimuria) to be appropriately rewarded or punished.

statement.id: Sebagian kecil arwah ia kirim ke surga Burotu; kebanyakan lainnya dilemparkan ke danau, tempat mereka akhirnya tenggelam ke dasar (Murimuria) untuk diganjar atau dihukum sepantasnya.
statement.en: He sends a few souls to the paradise Burotu; most others are thrown into a lake, where they eventually sink to the bottom (Murimuria) to be appropriately rewarded or punished.

short_description.id: Dilang dan Xiquan adalah anjing legenda Tiongkok yang tinggal di bawah tanah.
short_description.en: Dilang and Xiquan are Chinese legendary canines dwelling underground.

long_description.id: Dilang dan Xiquan adalah anjing legenda Tiongkok yang tinggal di bawah tanah. Shizi menyebut anjing di bawah tanah dengan nama Dilang.
long_description.en: Dilang and Xiquan are Chinese legendary canines dwelling underground. The Shizi calls an underground dog Dilang.

long_description.id: Soushen Ji mencatat penemuan dua anak Xiquan oleh Huai Yao. Kisah lain menyebut Zhang Mao menemukan dua anak anjing ketika tanah di bawah tempat tidurnya terbuka. Kitab Jin mencatat penemuan anak anjing putih oleh Sun Wuzhong. Catatan Kitab Jin lainnya menyebut He Xu menemukan dua anak anjing di bawah tanah.
long_description.en: The Soushen Ji records Huai Yao finding two Xiquan puppies. Another tale describes Zhang Mao discovering two puppies when the ground beneath his bed opens. The Book of Jin records Sun Wuzhong finding white puppies. Another Book of Jin account describes He Xu finding two puppies underground.

long_description.id: Soushen Ji mengutip Shizi: anjing di dalam tanah bernama dilang. Dalam kisah yang sama, seorang tetua menyebut anak anjing galian itu 'xiquan' dan berkata memperolehnya membawa kemakmuran bagi keluarga, sedangkan Kitab Jin, mengutip Shizi yang sama, menyebut peristiwa semacam itu sebagai bencana anjing. Kitab Jin juga mencatat kisah He Xu dan Sun Wuzhong yang menemukan anak anjing di bawah tanah.
long_description.en: The Soushen Ji quotes the Shizi: a dog in the earth is called dilang. In the same story an elder calls the dug-up puppies 'xiquan' and says obtaining them brings prosperity to the family, whereas the Book of Jin, citing the same Shizi, calls such events a 'dog calamity'. The Book of Jin also records the tales of He Xu and Sun Wuzhong finding puppies underground.

claims.quote: are  canines that, according to Chinese legend, live underground. The 4th-century BC text Shizi states: "If there be a dog under the earth, it is called ti-lang [dilang]."

statement.id: Dilang dan Xiquan adalah anjing legenda Tiongkok yang tinggal di bawah tanah.
statement.en: Dilang and Xiquan are Chinese legendary canines dwelling underground.

claims.quote: The 4th-century BC text Shizi states: "If there be a dog under the earth, it is called ti-lang [dilang]."

statement.id: Shizi menyebut anjing di bawah tanah dengan nama Dilang.
statement.en: The Shizi calls an underground dog Dilang.

claims.quote: According to Gan Bao's 4th-century story collection In Search of the Supernatural, during the yuankang period (c. 291–299) of Emperor Hui of Jin's reign, a man named Huai Yao (懷瑤) in Lou County (婁縣), Wu Commandery discovered two underground Xiquan puppies, "one male and a female, whose eyes had not yet opened", both of which were larger than normal dogs.

statement.id: Soushen Ji mencatat penemuan dua anak Xiquan oleh Huai Yao.
statement.en: The Soushen Ji records Huai Yao finding two Xiquan puppies.

claims.quote: Gan Bao's book also mentioned another discovery, that of the Grand Protector of Wu Commandery, Zhang Mao (張茂), which supposedly took place during the taixing period (c. 318–321) of Emperor Yuan of Jin's reign. Zhang had heard sounds of dogs beneath his bed but could not find the source; finally the earth cracked open and revealed two puppies.

statement.id: Kisah lain menyebut Zhang Mao menemukan dua anak anjing ketika tanah di bawah tempat tidurnya terbuka.
statement.en: Another tale describes Zhang Mao discovering two puppies when the ground beneath his bed opens.

claims.quote: A similar story is found in the official historical text Book of Jin (648) about Sun Wuzhong (孫無終), a general under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, who found two white puppies, also one gender each, under his residence in Jiyang County (既陽縣). Sun also tried but failed to rear them; he was soon killed in 402 by the rebel Huan Xuan.

statement.id: Kitab Jin mencatat penemuan anak anjing putih oleh Sun Wuzhong.
statement.en: The Book of Jin records Sun Wuzhong finding white puppies.

claims.quote: According to the same chapter in Book of Jin, in the year 434, a man named He Xu (何旭) in Qian County (灊縣) also found two puppies underground; their thin and "blue" mother escaped. He Xu also tried to rear them; the female died but the male survived and grew to be "good at devouring beasts". Later, He Xu's village was destroyed by "barbarians".

statement.id: Catatan Kitab Jin lainnya menyebut He Xu menemukan dua anak anjing di bawah tanah.
statement.en: Another Book of Jin account describes He Xu finding two puppies underground.

claims.quote: 形大於常犬。哺之，而食。左右咸往觀焉。長老或云：「此名『犀犬』，得之者，令家富昌，宜當養之。」

statement.id: Dalam Soushen Ji, seorang tetua berkata bahwa anak anjing yang digali dari tanah itu bernama 'xiquan' dan siapa yang memperolehnya akan membuat keluarganya makmur sehingga patut dipelihara.
statement.en: In the Soushen Ji, an elder says the puppies dug from the ground are called 'xiquan' and that whoever obtains them makes his family prosperous, so they should be raised.

claims.quote: 尸子曰：「地中有犬，名曰『地狼』；有人，名曰『無傷』。」夏鼎志曰：「掘地而得狗，名曰『賈』

statement.id: Soushen Ji mengutip Shizi: anjing di dalam tanah bernama dilang, dan manusia di dalam tanah bernama wushang; kutipan Xia Ding Zhi menyebut anjing yang digali dari tanah bernama jia.
statement.en: The Soushen Ji quotes the Shizi: a dog in the earth is called dilang and a person in the earth is called wushang; a quoted Xia Ding Zhi says a dog dug out of the ground is called jia.

claims.quote: 太興四年，廬江灊縣何旭家忽聞地中有犬子聲，掘之得一母犬，青釐色，狀甚羸瘦，走入草中，不知所在。視其處有二犬子，一雄一雌，哺而養之，雌死雄活。及長為犬，善噬獸。

statement.id: Kitab Jin mencatat bahwa pada tahun Taixing keempat, keluarga He Xu di Qian, Lujiang, mendengar suara anak anjing dari dalam tanah, menggali dan menemukan induk anjing kurus yang lari ke rumput serta dua anak anjing; yang betina mati, yang jantan hidup dan menjadi anjing yang pandai menerkam binatang buas.
statement.en: The Book of Jin records that in the fourth year of Taixing, the household of He Xu in Qian, Lujiang, heard puppy sounds underground, dug and found a thin mother dog that ran into the grass and two puppies; the female died, the male lived and grew into a dog good at biting beasts.

claims.quote: 是時輔國將軍孫無終家于既陽，地中聞犬子聲，尋而地坼，有二犬子，皆白色，一雄一雌，取而養之，皆死。後無終為桓玄所誅滅。

statement.id: Kitab Jin mencatat bahwa di rumah Sun Wuzhong di Jiyang, tanah terbelah dan muncul dua anak anjing putih, jantan dan betina; keduanya mati meski dipelihara, dan kemudian Sun Wuzhong dibinasakan oleh Huan Xuan.
statement.en: The Book of Jin records that at Sun Wuzhong's home in Jiyang the ground split and two white puppies, one male and one female, appeared; both died despite being raised, and Sun Wuzhong was later put to death by Huan Xuan.

claims.quote: 案《屍子》曰：「地中有犬，名曰地狼。」《夏鼎志》曰；「掘地得犬，名曰賈。」此蓋自然之物，不應出而出，為犬禍也。

statement.id: Kitab Jin, setelah mengutip Shizi bahwa anjing di dalam tanah bernama dilang, menyebut hal itu sebagai benda alami yang muncul padahal seharusnya tidak muncul, yaitu bencana anjing.
statement.en: After citing the Shizi that a dog in the earth is called dilang, the Book of Jin calls it a natural thing that appears when it should not, a 'dog calamity'.

summary.en: In the Soushen Ji, an elder says whoever obtains them makes his family prosperous and that they should be raised.

short_description.id: Dilong adalah nama naga Tiongkok yang secara harfiah berarti naga bumi.
short_description.en: Dilong is a Chinese dragon name literally denoting an earth dragon.

long_description.id: Dilong adalah nama naga Tiongkok yang secara harfiah berarti naga bumi. Dalam mitologi, Dilong dipasangkan dengan Tianlong, naga langit. Naga Tiongkok dianggap dapat terbang dan karenanya dipandang sebagai makhluk langit, bukan makhluk darat seperti dilong.
long_description.en: Dilong is a Chinese dragon name literally denoting an earth dragon. In mythology, Dilong is paired with Tianlong, the heavenly dragon. Chinese dragons were supposedly able to fly and so were considered celestial creatures rather than terrestrial ones like the dilong.

long_description.id: The History of the Southern Dynasties mencatat Dilong dalam biografi Wang Sengbian. Dalam teks sejarah klasik, dua naga melompat ke langit dari sungai dan para tetua berkata bahwa naga bumi telah pergi sehingga negara mungkin binasa.
long_description.en: The History of the Southern Dynasties records Dilong in Wang Sengbian's biography. In the classical history text, two dragons leap into the sky from the river and the elders say that the earth dragon has gone and the state may perish.

long_description.id: Dilong juga menjadi nama yang anggun bagi cacing tanah. Bencao Gangmu mencantumkan Dilong dan Tulong sebagai nama lain cacing tanah, dan Li Shizhen mencatat nama itu berasal dari mitos bahwa cacing tanah, seperti naga, dapat menciptakan cuaca yang tak menentu. Dilongsan dibuat dari perut cacing tanah merah dan dipakai dalam pengobatan tradisional Tiongkok.
long_description.en: Dilong also serves as an elegant name for earthworms. The Bencao Gangmu lists Dilong and Tulong as alternative earthworm names, and Li Shizhen notes the names come from the myth that earthworms, like dragons, can create unsettled weather. Dilongsan is prepared from the abdomen of the red earthworm and used in traditional Chinese medicine.

claims.quote: Dilong (traditional Chinese: 地龍; simplified Chinese: 地龙; pinyin: dìlóng; Wade–Giles: ti-lung; lit. "earth dragon") is a Chinese dragon name that is also used to mean "earthworm" in traditional Chinese medicine and Geosaurus in zoological nomenclature.

statement.id: Dilong adalah nama naga Tiongkok yang secara harfiah berarti naga bumi.
statement.en: Dilong is a Chinese dragon name literally denoting an earth dragon.

claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, dilong (地龍; "earth dragon") is one of many types of -long (龍) dragons ... the dilong is paired with the tianlong (天龍; "heavenly dragon").

statement.id: Dalam mitologi, Dilong dipasangkan dengan Tianlong, naga langit.
statement.en: In mythology, Dilong is paired with Tianlong, the heavenly dragon.

claims.quote: Dilong first occurs in the mid-7th century CE History of the Southern Dynasties biography of Liang dynasty Admiral Wang Sengbian 王僧辯 (d. 555 CE). It says witnesses saw lianglong (兩龍; "two/paired dragons") that ascended into the sky, and this dilong "earth dragon" leaving Liang territory was interpreted as a portent of their defeat in 550 CE.

statement.id: Sejarah Dinasti Selatan mencatat Dilong dalam biografi Wang Sengbian.
statement.en: The History of the Southern Dynasties records Dilong in Wang Sengbian's biography.

claims.quote: Dilong or dilongzi (地龍子; "earth dragon child") is an elegant name for the "earthworm; worm", which is usually called qiuyin (蚯蚓). "Long 龍 is employed in Chinese zoological nomenclature in much the same way that English dragon is used in dragonfly or dragonfish".

statement.id: Istilah Dilong juga menjadi sebutan halus untuk cacing tanah.
statement.en: Dilong also serves as an elegant name for earthworms.

claims.quote: Dilong first means "earthworm" in the Qixiu Leigao (七修類稿) written by the Ming dynasty scholar Lang Ying 郎瑛 (1487–1566 CE). The 1578 Bencao Gangmu pharmacological entry for qiuyin (蚯蚓; "earthworm") lists alternate names of dilong and tulong (土龍) (see above).

statement.id: Bencao Gangmu mencantumkan Dilong dan Tulong sebagai nama alternatif cacing tanah.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu lists Dilong and Tulong as alternative earthworm names.

claims.quote: Chinese dragons were supposedly able to fly, and thus were considered celestial creatures rather than terrestrial ones like the "earthbound" dilong.

statement.id: Naga Tiongkok dianggap dapat terbang sehingga dipandang sebagai makhluk langit, bukan makhluk darat seperti dilong yang "terikat bumi".
statement.en: Chinese dragons were supposedly able to fly and were thus considered celestial creatures rather than terrestrial ones like the "earthbound" dilong.

claims.quote: Li Shizhen notes these names derive from the myth that earthworms (like dragons) can create yinqing

statement.id: Li Shizhen mencatat bahwa nama-nama itu berasal dari mitos bahwa cacing tanah (seperti naga) dapat menciptakan yinqing (cuaca mendung dan cerah yang tak menentu).
statement.en: Li Shizhen notes these names derive from the myth that earthworms, like dragons, can create yinqing (unsettled cloudy and clear weather).

claims.quote: Dilongsan (地龍散; "earth dragon powder"), or Di Long, is used in traditional Chinese medicine. It is prepared from the abdomen of the Red earthworm, Lumbricus rubellus, and has many purported medicinal uses.

statement.id: Dilongsan (地龍散; "bubuk naga bumi"), atau Di Long, dipakai dalam pengobatan tradisional Tiongkok; dibuat dari perut cacing tanah merah Lumbricus rubellus dan dikatakan memiliki banyak khasiat.
statement.en: Dilongsan (地龍散; "earth dragon powder"), or Di Long, is used in traditional Chinese medicine; it is prepared from the abdomen of the red earthworm Lumbricus rubellus and has many purported medicinal uses.

claims.quote: 三月庚寅，有兩龍自城西江中騰躍升天，五色分明，遙映江水。百姓咸仰面目之，父老或聚而悲，竊相謂曰：「地龍已去，國其亡乎。」

statement.id: Dalam catatan sejarah klasik ini, pada hari gengyin bulan ketiga dua naga melompat naik ke langit dari sungai di barat kota dengan lima warna yang jelas memantul di air; rakyat menengadah, dan para tetua berkumpul dengan sedih sambil berkata, "Naga bumi (地龍) telah pergi, apakah negara akan binasa?"
statement.en: In this classical history record, on the gengyin day of the third month two dragons leapt into the sky from the river west of the city with five distinct colors reflected on the water; people looked up, and elders gathered in grief saying, "The earth dragon (地龍) has gone; will the state perish?"

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
